## Canon established by the Volume 03 close (Chapters 101–150 read as a finished book; the Volume 04 outline is built on this)

**Items 1–380 are the record of Volume 01, of the Volume 02 plan, of Chapters 51–100, of the Volume 02 close, of Chapters 101–150, and of the Batch 0015 review repair pass, and none of them is renumbered by this section.** The close record is `outline/volumes/volume-03-close.md` and it is read first. Items 373–380 are the Batch 0015 review repair pass and are not repeated here.

381. **THE CHAPTER 138 DATING IS DECIDED AND IT IS THE PAGE: THE GUILD'S PLAN IS OF THE TWELFTH ROLLING OF THE YEAR BEFORE. This supersedes item 375's finding and does not renumber it.** `chapters/volume-03/chapter-0138.md` lines 11, 13 and 43 and `chapters/volume-03/chapter-0149.md` line 31 now read **the twelfth rolling of the year before**, in five places across two chapters. **The defect was that a plan written in the twelfth rolling cannot be on the table in the eighth, against Chapter 139 in the ninth rolling with four rollings left in the year.** The decision is the rolling the page already implied: `chapter-0131.md` is in the fifth rolling and has Coll Ferrow hold up the book and say *That is the twelfth rolling. Written before I met any of you. It has been in that press since the spring and I have not altered one line of it, and the reason I have not altered one line of it is that I wrote it in the twelfth rolling and it was wrong in the twelfth rolling, and a man who corrects his own plan before anybody has read it is a man who wants to be agreed with.* **Dating it to the twelfth rolling of the year before resolves the contradiction in the direction the manuscript supports and sits before the Water, which is the seventh rolling, which is what the plan's four stops are for.** Three consequences, binding: **Aren arrives in the eighth rolling of the current year**, because Chapter 138's clause is *the seventh of this year is the rolling before the man with the bar came up the stair*; **no chapter may state an arrival rolling and none does, and no phase may infer one from a chapter that does not say it, and the block order is unchanged — fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth, eleventh, twelfth, thirteenth**; and **the plan's date moves, the day map does not.** Chapter 131 is deliberately left reading *That is the twelfth rolling*, said in the fifth rolling by a man talking about a book, and a reader who has Chapter 138 supplies the year.
382. **TWO MORE PLACES OF THE SAME DATING ERROR, FOUND AND REPAIRED IN THE CLOSE, AND A GARBLE. `chapter-0145.md` no longer dates the new work to a single rolling and `chapter-0138.md` line 57 no longer reads the fourth rolling of the fifth rolling.** **Chapter 145's first column, in the fair copy the volume's climax turns on, read *the four hundred and forty yards already opened in the fifth rolling, and the new work of the twelfth rolling* — a parallel construction putting all the post-fifth-rolling work in one rolling, which after item 381 could only have been read as work done in the twelfth rolling of the year before, before Aren arrived and before the council took the plan. It now reads *the new work of the sixth, the eighth and the tenth*, which is what Chapter 149's own working says: the causeway and the trench in the sixth, the nine-day working in the eighth, the re-cutting in the tenth.** And Chapter 138 line 57 read *the four words he wrote in the fourth rolling of the fifth rolling are in no book at all*, against Chapter 138's own line 31 which says the fourth week of the fifth rolling; **it now reads the fourth week of the fifth rolling, and the word count is unchanged by that fix.** **The fifth place in a two-chapter dating error is the signature of a defect that is in the calendar and not in the prose, and a calendar does not get fixed by a review pass.** One looseness is recorded and not changed: **Chapter 131's *It has been in that press since the spring*, against a plan dated to the twelfth rolling of the year before in a county whose year is thirteen rollings of four weeks. It is loose and it is not wrong, and a later phase may not "correct" it and may not call it a fresh error.**
383. **THE FIGURES, ON THE PAGE, AND WHAT FOUR STATE FILES AND ONE PROMPT WERE CARRYING. Batch 0011 31,648 · Batch 0012 29,130 · Batch 0013 16,315 · Batch 0014 35,340 · Batch 0015 34,128. Volume 03 is 146,561 words in fifty chapters and the manuscript is 601,642 in one hundred and fifty.** Per chapter, Batch 0014: **4316 / 3952 / 3156 / 2975 / 3959 / 2943 / 2978 / 2928 / 3724 / 4409**; Batch 0015: **3408 / 3368 / 2794 / 3183 / 2916 / 3014 / 3380 / 3634 / 5136 / 3295**. The five columns foot: **31,648 + 29,130 + 16,315 + 35,340 + 34,128 = 146,561.** The three volumes foot: **270,562 + 184,519 + 146,561 = 601,642.** Volume 01 and Volume 02 are untouched, **and the nine-word discrepancy between the page and `workspace/volume-02/volume-02-close/PROMPT.md` on Volume 02 stands as recorded and is not this close's to close: the page is 184,519 and the close prints 184,519.** **Items 372, 374 and 380, the Batch 0015 entry, `state/current.md` and the close prompt all carried 35,318 / 34,113 / 146,524 / 601,605, which was right before this close's own three prose fixes and is wrong after them.** **A later phase that prints a total must foot it on the page first, which is the whole of item 145 and the whole of the Volume 02 close's §10 item 3, and this is now the second time in one volume that a figure reached four files.**
384. **THE THREE HOOKS, IN `outline/volume-03.md` §11'S ORDER, AS THE CLOSE STATES THEM.** **Hook one: the seed-and-bridge company's four-line letter for a jar, sent the twenty-first of Hearthmonth, YR 313 in a bag, not answered inside the year and not going to be answered, because there is no longer anybody in the county of nine hundred and forty-one hearths holding the other end of anything and the road to it is closed in four lines of writing. Volume 04 may not answer it, may not deliver it, and may not find a living holder of the other end; what Volume 04 may do is let a sent document stand unanswered, which is a real instrument this manuscript has never used.** **Hook two: Form R.C. 4 with the marginal instruction that manufactures a keeper, and Sabin Dain, whose offer is dead in a form — the four-hundred-and-eleven-word refusal is in a mail sack behind a salt loft, cut open along the left edge, and nobody in the world knows it exists including Mara Vey. Volume 04 inherits it as a practice with a refusal attached and not as a recruitment that failed, and Volume 04's file is the one that gets the refusal out of the sack, and getting it out is a party receiving a document and not a scene in which he explains himself; the clause that lands is the number of persons the offer has been made out to, which the office left off its own sheet.** **Hook three: a tile on a coping, a hand's width, with a rope on it and no yoke, whose maker is dead, on the far side of a road that is not there — and, beside it and not to be joined to it, a hearing entered for the ninth of Rainmonth of the year following at the second hour for a delegation that cannot arrive and that stands whether anybody comes or not, and three marks on the outside of a seed vault that a woman of sixty-six has decided nothing about.**
385. **THE TILE'S PROHIBITION IS *NOT EXPLAINED AND THE DEVICE NOT NAMED*, AND *NOT NAMED* IS THE WRONG PROHIBICTION.** Item 372 and three other places recorded the tile as **not named**, and **Chapter 148 names it and Chapter 150's last line names it — *a tile on it with a rope on it and no yoke, and nobody looked at it*.** The tile may be named as an object and has been, twice. **The rule a later volume works with is: the tile may not be explained, no character may name its device, and no batch may schedule an explanation, a flashback, an origin, a maker or a deathbed — and nothing may be built on a prohibition of *not named*, which would forbid the last line of Volume 03.** The road to that end of the line is closed in four lines of writing and nothing may reopen it. **The close's finding is that a Volume 04 prohibition built on *not named* would have forbidden the best object in the book.**
386. **THE STAGE 3 DECISION, AND WHAT IT COSTS. Volume 04 reaches Threadkeeper by qualification, in Block 5, and completes the qualification.** `outline/series.md` gives the Second Door to Volumes 2–3 and Threadkeeper to Volumes 4–6; `bible/power-system.md` gives Threadkeeper three paths, path-lineage reading and a limited forced-connection cut, and its qualification as **one consensual cut made while a local bridgekeeper remains present, and then helping the same community repair the physical scar before the route is declared stable**; and Volume 04's sixteen-month interval is the longest in the manuscript. Therefore: **three paths held at the close of Volume 04 — Bellweather-Living, the Hearth Marches and the Ninefold Winter valley — and two to three is the whole of the movement; no lineage is read and no cut is made, attempted, offered as a plan, priced or described as available in Blocks 1–4; one cut in Block 5, consented to, with a valley bridgekeeper at his shoulder, and the same community repairs the scar before the route is declared stable.** **The cost is not a limp: every cut leaves a visible seam in the current world and gives the affected path a lasting memory of him, and the seam in the current world is in a bridge, in a stone course, about nine inches, and it is the first thing in two hundred chapters a stranger can see and not explain. The Many-Handed stage's worsening of the limp belongs to Volume 15 and Volume 04 adds no second bodily cost. The fever after the return is a week, because the stage earns it.** And the volume's second power movement is a **refusal, in writing**: a fourth route offered cheaply that would open for him alone and cost the offering community nothing, refused, and **it is the second refusal in a document in two volumes and Dain's is the first and neither party knows the other exists.** **The Volume 06 row of the failure table — a cut made on a false witness, the community's anchor tears, contact ends — is Volume 06's and is not scheduled, forecast with a date, or priced here; the risk is carried forward as known-and-refused, from the Chapter 124 refusal on a date and a community and a forged witness, unexplained.**
387. **THE CORPUS OF DOCUMENTS AT THE END OF CHAPTER 150, EVERY ONE ON A PAGE, NONE A MYSTERY: the Marches' fair copy of four hundred and eight words and a working on a second sheet, on a board under a stair in a county that is not on any map, where anybody coming up two flights may read it; the seven-column hand-over with the last line under the rule in the keeper's own hand and the yard's name in the fair copy and not in the minute; the four-line notice that closed the County of Ash, whose fourth line is the county's second term given back whole, forty-one words; the four rules of the guild; the six terms of the Marches with term four the price and term six the door; the three rules in a fair copy in a day-book with the hour, signed by the keeper; the hearing entered for the ninth of Rainmonth of the year following; the four-line letter for a jar, sent the twenty-first; the refusal of four hundred and eleven words in a mail sack behind a salt loft, cut open along the left edge; Form R.C. 4 and the marginal instruction on its reverse; the leaf of a return with Oswin Rill's hand on the back of it, dated two years before the return, held entered entire and un-copied; the column of eleven counties entered as a question and not as a finding; the winter book of a valley, which is new and is not on this list; and the bell's band of forty-one rivets and its dull red seam.** **The three books that cannot be served are the Marches' minute, the guild's book and the Archive's day-book, and the only object in the case a court can be served with and take nothing out of is a half tile in a press that weighs a shade over ten ounces and is the account of nobody.**
388. **THE CAST SPENT AND THE SLOTS UNFILLED: Volume 03 is seven names of a possible thirty, with twenty-three of thirty slots unfilled, and the cap is closed.** **2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 7, and the rows declare 4 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 23, and seven and twenty-three is thirty.** The seven are **Thessa Wend** (Batch 0011), **Oswin Rill** (0011), **Coll Ferrow** (0012), **Delya Munn** (0012), **Ordmar Gace** (0013), **Aled Rhys** (0013), **Sian Pugh** (0014). **Sian Pugh's name is spoken once in the whole volume, by the man at the drawknife, in a yard, in Chapter 136, and is not spoken again by anybody in that county, and the question of whether it is spent is closed for the fourth time and may not be re-opened and no Volume 04 chapter may use it.** **Volume 04's own plan is six names of thirty with twenty-four unfilled, and one new name per fifty-chapter volume may not exceed six, and Volume 04 is built to beat Volume 03's seven.** **Edric Hunn is not a Volume 03 name, is not a Volume 04 name, is not written in a column, and does not appear.**
389. **CORRECTIONS THIS CLOSE MAKES TO EARLIER ITEMS AND RECORDS, WITHOUT RENUMBERING ANYTHING.** **Item 375 is superseded by item 381 and is annotated, not renumbered, and its heading no longer stands as the open record of the defect.** The Batch 0014 entry's phrase *a printed plan written in the twelfth rolling* and the Batch 0015 entry's first deviation's *Chapter 138 says the plan was written in the twelfth rolling* are both corrected to **the twelfth rolling of the year before**. `state/current.md`'s last-change paragraph no longer says the dating was left open for the close. **The Batch 0012 entry has no repair-pass record and this is a real gap and is recorded and not invented: its own *Landed* line says the block is "after the review repair pass recorded below" and there is no such record in it, four traces of the pass survive inside its deviation list, and this close does not manufacture a repair pass for a batch it did not review.** And **the promise's age, Chapter 70's "eight weeks" and the Chapter 10 column remain standing recorded defects and none is repaired**, for the reasons the Volume 02 close gave, which have not changed: **a defect that is recorded is a fact about the book, and a defect that is inherited silently becomes a canon with a footnote.**
390. **THE CLOSE'S TWO FINDINGS, WHICH ARE FINDINGS AND NOT OVERSIGHTS, AND WHICH ARE BOTH BINDING ON VOLUME 04.** **First, Volume 03's ending does not resolve the relationship the book is about.** A man conceals the order of an ordinary morning from the only person in the world who can hold him to a document about himself, and in fifty chapters he gives her every number he has and not the morning, **and he does not tell her that he cannot**; nine not-askings are entered and there is no tenth, and the one time she says the word *tenth* she puts her pen down and neither of them says why. **The breach is open, unrepaired, and is not to be repaired in Volume 04 in a scene, an aside, a document or an apology, and Volume 04's chosen intimacy is bought with it and the cost of that intimacy is a thing that has to be paid and not a cure.** **Second, Volume 03's answer to its own question is a door and not a cure, and the door is made of the same material as the thing that was killing the county** — a promise that can be broken, in public, on a day named in advance, with a release in it and a consequence and no office behind it, and a release is a document, and a document names a body, and a body can be served. **The Marches cured itself of a hundred and forty years of a promise by producing a piece of paper, and the paper is now in a county that has become a place a record gathers in, and the county entered the fact at the head of its own list and did it anyway. There is no version of this volume in which the Marches wins.**
391. **TWO PLAN CONFLICTS FLAGGED BY THE CLOSE AND NOT ABSORBED, BOTH IN `outline/volume-04.md` §16.** **First, `outline/series.md`'s Volume 4 escalation line and its Volume 4 knowledge-control row say that Aren learns Edric's name appears in older Gatehouse administration, and the close's guard forbids writing that name anywhere in Volume 04.** The guard is binding and is the more careful instruction, **because a name in an older administration in a valley is one join away from a join in a provincial office, and that join is Chapter 894's and belongs to the second severance held since Chapter 58.** The Volume 04 outline puts **an office's hand on a two-hundred-year-old form with a count of carrier obligations in it, never answered and never withdrawn, and the office named and not a man's name**, and records that the series outline's Volume 4 knowledge-control row **is not satisfied by that outline and is carried forward as an open item.** **Second, `outline/series.md`'s pressure-rotation table gives Volume 4's relationship work as *Aren and Edric's last private warning*, and the volume's relationship work is instead the breach and Mara, the brothers, and the two hundred people on a roll**, and the dominant pressure and the recovery anchor are taken from the table. **Both are recorded as deviations and not as improvements, and a later phase may not read `outline/volume-04.md` as having satisfied either row.**
392. **THE QUESTION CHAPTER 151 OPENS ON, AND IT IS NOT THE VALLEY.** **The twenty-fifth of Hearthmonth, YR 313, a Saturday, a market day, the fourth hour, the day after the volume ends — and a man who was paid in ninety-six bushels of salt comes up two flights of a stair in Weir Street and reads a fair copy off a board under the bench, because anybody coming up two flights may read it, and asks for it to be copied, and nobody has to be asked. And the copy goes four hundred miles to a bench of nine that has been asked four times and has said yes four times and is not a bench, and asks it a fifth question, and the answer is no, and the reason is in the fair copy, and the person who put the fair copy where anybody coming up two flights may read it is not the man who wrote it. The road that opens is made of paper and carries nobody, and the man who cannot open it is the man who built it.**

## Canon established by Batch 0001 (Volume 04, Chapters 151–160, prose on the page)

**Items 1–392 are the record of Volume 01, of the Volume 02 plan, of Chapters 51–100, of the Volume 02 close, of Chapters 101–150, of the Batch 0015 review repair pass and of the Volume 03 close, and none of them is renumbered by this section. Items 381–392 are the Volume 03 close and are not repeated here. The close document is `outline/volumes/volume-03-close.md` and the volume plan is `outline/volume-04.md`, and both are read first.**

393. **THE BOARD UNDER THE STAIR IS IN MEREFEN AND IS A FAIR COPY OF A FAIR COPY, AND THE PERSON WHO PUT IT THERE IS THE KEEPER OF RECORDS AND NOT THE MAN WHO WROTE IT.** Chapter 151. **The Marches' fair copy of four hundred and eight words and a working came down the line on the twentieth of Hearthmonth, YR 313, addressed to a shelf, and the Archive had a fair copy of it made and sent it to the board under the bench at the bottom of the two flights of the guild hall over the wharf, nailed on four corners with the nail heads left proud.** The board is four feet by two and a half and is not lath and lime. **A water-barge hand of twenty-seven from the Hearth Marches, in Merefen eleven weeks on a crew's account and paid, read it standing in the rain and asked for it to be copied, and nobody had to be asked.** The Archive copied it in about two hours on two sheets, **with the addition left standing exactly as the county that did the addition wrote it, and the keeper of records refused to foot it and said so out loud, and gave the reason in four words: *it is not ours*.** **A later writer may not have the Archive foot the addition, may not print the addition's total in a speech, and may not print the figure at the head of the fair copy, which is struck in the keeper's margin and is 9-4-1 and is not on the page of this volume at all.** Two copies went out of the room, one to the bench of nine and one four hundred miles on the same barge.

394. **THE MARCHES' SIX TERMS ARE ON THE PAGE OF VOLUME 04, VERBATIM, IN ORDER, AND NO LINE MAY BE RE-WORDED.** Chapter 151, printed in a guild hall in Merefen from the copy the Archive holds under the resolution of the twentieth of Hearthmonth. *First. The road is not to be made to carry a person. Second. No name is to be read out on the far side of the line by anybody from the north, and no name is to be written in the line's book at the north end. Third. The north is not to send anybody who can be asked to come and look. Fourth. The stone is not to be renewed in the north's presence. Fifth. The road is kept by a hand at each end and a witness at each end, and the witness at the Marches' end is chosen by the Marches. Sixth. The line is not to be opened on a day the Marches have not named.* **The second is the reason the man who built the road may not write a name at the north end of it, and the sixth is a door, and Reeve Aldis Fenn asked that the minute of this county say that a door is a thing a person can be killed in. The guild's four terms are not in this batch and the fourth of them is not named and not re-worded and is not the working.** **The prompt's parenthetical that term four is the price does not match the term and is recorded as a slip carried over from the County of Ash's five terms, and no line of the six may be altered to make it true.**

395. **THE FIFTH ASKING IS PUT, THE ANSWER IS NO, AND THE NUMBER OF YESES STAYS AT FOUR.** Chapter 151, the seventh hour of a Saturday sitting. **The asking is money for the Old Toll crossing, it has been asked four times and answered four times, and Reeve Aldis Fenn carried it up two flights on the twenty-fourth of Hearthmonth and did not put it and asked for that to be minuted, and she put it on the Saturday because on Friday she did not have the copy.** The bench refused in about a minute and a half, **and the reason given is the board: the first of the six terms, and a road built to that term carries nobody, and a bench of nine that has found money for a road that carries nobody has not been asked a hard question and has answered a soft one.** The minute carries that this is the fifth asking, that the number of yeses is four and the number of times this bench has been asked the same thing is five, and that both numbers are in it. **The chest has two marks in it and has had two since the ninth of Fallowmonth. A later Volume 04 chapter may not make the number of yeses five.**

396. **A BLANK COLUMN RULED IN A BENCH'S MINUTE BY A BENCH-CLERK AT THE REQUEST OF A MAN ON THE BENCH, AND A BLANK TWO INCHES AT THE RIGHT-HAND EDGE OF A LIST OF THINGS SENT, AND NEITHER IS EVER WRITTEN IN.** Chapters 151 and 152. **Bram Ottery, 47, on the bench because he was elected and paid fourpence a week out of a private box, had the minute of a council four hundred miles off read out twice, in which a line with nothing in a money column says that four men of a yard in this town are owed at the guild's rate, and he entered that this bench has not once asked a yard in this town what it is owed by anybody, and the bench-clerk ruled a column for it and it is blank, and the reeve initialled the blank column because in about nine years somebody will come and see a ruled column with nothing in it and think there is a sum.** **Alish Renn ruled a list of things sent in four columns — what was sent, the day it went, to whom in the words it was sent, and carriage paid or not paid — and the ruling stops two inches short of the width of the page, and the two inches is at the right-hand edge and nothing is ruled in it.** A junior clerk proposed a fifth column for what came back and was refused, **because somebody writes *nothing* in it in about four years and it is true when he writes it, and a ruled column with the word *nothing* in it is read in about forty years as the office having asked.** **A later writer may not fill either blank and may not rule either one in.**

397. **THE COUNTY POST IS ON THE POST AT HIS OWN COST AND THE FIGURE IS ON THE LIST AND NOT ON THE WRAPPER.** Chapter 152. **Rowan Petch, 26, clerk of the provincial court, is this month on the county post at his own cost, which he does twice a year, and the post is three days either way, and he pays his own way and this office has never asked him for a penny of it and is not going to.** The column, footed on the page before the total is said: **a carrier at ten pence a day is ten, a horse's keep at four is four, ten and four is fourteen a day, fourteen nine times is a hundred and twenty-six, four sheets at twopence is eight, and a hundred and thirty-four pence, which is two marks and three shillings and twopence.** **The number a later phase may quote is 134 pence and the working is ten plus four, nine days, four sheets at twopence.**

398. **THE MARCHES' CONTRACT IS CITED WHOLE IN VOLUME 04 AND NOT RE-DERIVED, AND THE ONE FIFTH OF SIX HUNDRED AND FORTY-EIGHT IS NAMED AS THE SAME NUMBER AS THE SEED AND NOT THE SAME MONEY.** Chapter 152. **Three thousand two hundred and forty pence, paid in two hundred and eighty-eight bushels of salt at nine pence the bushel and two hundred and sixteen bushels of seed at three pence the bushel, and the two together are the contract and not two payments; the one fifth, six hundred and forty-eight pence, was payable on the return and was given up in a gateway by the first hand of that county's guild and is not in any book, and a yard four hundred miles off has been out of pocket that figure since, and the same figure is the price of two hundred and sixteen bushels of seed in the same line of the same account, and the text says in one sentence that the two are the same number and are not the same money.** **No Volume 04 phase may re-derive any figure of that contract and may not scale it, and no Marches figure is set in a money column beside a Merefen figure, and 4,632 and 1,752 and 1,272 and 480 and 864 and 2,592 and 3,240 may not be re-footed in this volume.** The county's own figures are three and none of them is a hearth, and **9-4-1 does not appear in Volume 04 in any form**, and no 456, no 254, no 2,450, no 2,906, and **the four thousand and the seven hundred and twenty are never added, anywhere, in any file, in any sum.**

399. **A FOUR-LINE NOTICE CAME DOWN A ROAD FOUR HUNDRED MILES OFF ON THE TWENTY-SEVENTH OF HEARTHMONTH, YR 313, AND IT IS NOT THE ANSWER TO ANYTHING, BECAUSE THERE WAS NEVER A QUESTION, AND THE SEED LETTER WAS NEVER DELIVERED.** Chapter 152. **It is dated four days before it arrived, so it was written while it was on the road and the road took four days for four lines, and no length of road is asserted anywhere in this volume, because a nine-day road would collide with the three days' post Sarn gives in Chapter 154. REPAIRED at the Batch 0001 review: the first printing of this item said the road took nine days, which four days of dating does not yield. Its first line is that the line at this end is shut, was shut in writing, the shutting is lawful and is not to be re-opened by anybody from the north. Its second is that the book at this end is shut and kept shut and not to be asked for. Its third is that the hand at this end is released from it and is not to be sought and is not to be sent for. Its fourth is that the line at this end is the whole of what this county has to say to him.** The reason nothing was asked is the resolution of the twentieth of Hearthmonth: no person is to be sent to ask anybody in that county anything. **The four-line letter asking for a jar went into a bag on the twenty-first of Hearthmonth addressed to any county that has kept a seed of a thing it does not grow, to a post office, and a post office writes to the last address held for a county, and the last address is a roll of households with no address on it and no person at the end of it, and the letter is in a bag in a county with no writ and has not been delivered and is not going to be inside the year.** **The letter for a jar is not answered in this volume and may not be answered, may not be delivered, and no living holder of the other end may be found.**

400. **A REFUSAL OF FOUR HUNDRED AND ELEVEN WORDS CAME BACK CUT ALONG THE LEFT EDGE WITH A KNIFE AND WAS OPENED IN A ROOM OVER A WEIGH-HOUSE BY A PERSON WHO IS NOT AREN, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM APOLOGISED TO ANYBODY.** Chapter 153. **The band was cut by Rowan Petch, the post, because he is the post and he has a bag. The sheet lay on a table under a limestone weight for four days because a keeper who opens a letter addressed to somebody else is a woman who reads other people's post. Alish Renn opened it and said the thing that has to be said before a document is opened, and the reason she opened it is that it is in her hand and not because it is hers.** The address is *To Sabin Dain, aid to the register at the Office of Provincial Registration. And to no office.* **The document is in the Archive's press entire and was not copied, because a second hand on a man's own refusal is a second man's opinion of it. The cut band is in the same press with a claim number against nothing on the wrapper. Aren was four hundred yards away on a bridge for the whole of the chapter and did not know it had come back, and Mara Vey learned of it from the document and not from him, and there is no apology in it in any register, and neither of them said anything about it.**

401. **THE CLAUSE THAT LANDED IS THE NUMBER OF PERSONS THE OFFER WAS MADE OUT TO, WHICH IS NOT STATED ON THE PAGE, AND THE ARCHIVE HAS ASKED FOR IT IN A RETURN WITH NO NAME IN IT.** Chapter 153. **An office that will not print a number of persons cannot show that any person has not been instructed, and that is the other half of the same arrangement this office has held in its press for four years and a half in a whole leaf of returns in a column headed *Keeper*, in a hand that is not the man's, which the office relied on and entered nothing about.** The return asking for the number went out in a bag with no name in it and no word of how the number came by and no reference to the leaf and no reference to the refusal, **and the number has not been supplied and is not answered in this volume.** **The marginal instruction is cited in a return and refused about in a gateway and is in no mouth in a room and is not explained, and Sabin Dain is not the person who explains it and does not appear.** A carter with a barrow of lime asked a woman in a lane in Merefen what was written on the back of a printed form of that series and was refused in four words and the lane is not a room and a gateway is not a hearing.

402. **A PROPOSED COUNT OF CONTINUING OBLIGATIONS, WITH A SPACE FOR A FIGURE AND NO SPACE FOR A NAME, WAS BEATEN IN NINE MINUTES BY THE FORM'S OWN CONSTRUCTION, AND THE OFFICE'S REPLY IS A BIGGER COUNT IN A WOMAN'S HAND, DATED, AND IT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT.** Chapters 154 and 155. **The returnable paper is of the Office of Provincial Registration, is headed *Count of continuing obligations in respect of a district*, is returnable by the bench or the body corporate of the district, and was returnable on or before the seventh of Thawmonth, YR 314, a Saturday — thirty-three days out of the fourth of Goatmonth, YR 313, which is a Monday, and the first of Thawmonth is a Sunday on `outline/volume-04.md` §17's chain — and has six columns and no space for a name anywhere. REPAIRED at the Batch 0001 review: the first printing of this item gave YR 313 and a Monday, and YR 313's Thawmonth is behind the paper and the seventh of Thawmonth is a Saturday. It is not the county's own form, which is ruled in seven.** **On its reverse, in the office's own hand, in a smaller type, since the first of a month in YR 311: *For the purpose of this return, a continuing obligation in respect of a district is held by a person who has gone out of that district and whose name is entered against that district in any record of the district.* Nine words, and nobody in this kingdom can explain why it is there, and it is not explained in this volume.** Lysa Fenn's construction is the ninth of Greenmonth's and the twenty-first of Wolfmonth's and the form's own: **a count of persons is a return of a figure, a figure is not a person, no person is in default, a thing against which nobody is in default is not refused and not enforced and is therefore spent the moment it is answered, and it requires no further returnable date, and there is nobody in this kingdom who can appeal it because there is nothing in it to appeal.** **The discovery this time is that a returnable paper with no party in it expires, and the paper came to a filing office and not to a district's bench, and she says out loud that she has just handed a general machine to anybody with a door.** The return went out with the space for a figure and nothing in it and no name anywhere on the paper. **The office's reply is one sheet with a figure on it, 2,640, dated, in a woman's hand, with no seal, no number, no returnable date, no signature and no addressee, and it is not an instrument and can be neither enforced nor refused, and the figure is larger than the district, so it is a number of entries and not of people, and the only way to find out which is to count the district, and counting a district is a thing a Crown's hand is for.** **No name has been written in a Crown's hand in this county since the twenty-seventh of Fallowmonth and there is still not one, and this is the second time in two volumes that a Crown instrument has been answered with a figure and no name in it, and the first time the figure has been the answer and not the question.**

403. **THE HEARING FOR THE NINTH OF RAINMONTH, YR 314, AT THE SECOND HOUR, A TUESDAY, NOT A MARKET DAY, STANDS, AND IT IS REFERRED TO TWICE IN THIS BLOCK AND STAGED NOWHERE, AND NOBODY IS SENT FOR.** Chapters 154 and 156. It is entered against no person in the resolution of the twentieth of Hearthmonth, **the delegation is not to be sent for, and if the delegation does not come the hearing is not adjourned and is not refused and it stands.** It falls inside Volume 04's span and while he is in the path. **A Volume 04 phase may refer to it and may not hold it, adjourn it, refuse it or stage it.**

404. **THE LETTER FROM IVEN SARR ARRIVED ON THE FOURTH OF GOATMONTH, YR 313, A MONDAY — REPAIRED at the Batch 0001 review, which found the chapter and this item both printing a Tuesday against §17's chain — AND ASKS FOR A MAN WHO CAN READ A HAND AND NOT A MAN WHO CAN CROSS, AND A KEEPER OF RECORDS READ IT AND NOT THE ROAD WARDEN, AND WAS ASKED TO GO AND DID NOT, AND SAID WHY IN FOUR WORDS.** Chapter 154. **The four words are *A keeper does not travel*, and keeper is employment and is not jurisdiction, and the woman in question is answerable to a room with a door on a lane and to nobody else, and the office has a door and a number and can be sued and can be shut and a keeper can only be dismissed and she has not told anybody that in three counties.** The letter came in the same bag as the Crown instrument of item 402 and **the coincidence was entered at the foot of the wrapper and no person in the room did anything with it.** The letter is in the Archive's press entire and was not answered this week, and the reason is four words and they are *it is not a filing*. **The letter was read out in a county council meeting on the Saturday of that week and minuted as received with nothing done with it, and the person it concerns was already four hundred miles off and nobody was sent.** The hand of the man who keeps the minute in the Hearth Marches, that a fair copy is kept in that county in a county that is not on any map, is not a hand a Volume 04 chapter may compare with a hand in this one.

405. **THE NINE QUESTIONS, AND THREE OF THEM HAVE NO FIGURE IN THEM, AND THE NINTH SAYS THAT NOBODY THERE HAS BEEN ASKED AND THAT HE IS GOING ANYWAY.** Chapter 156. **Made up on the fourth step of a stair over a weigh-house in nine minutes with the hour against each of the nine, seven in four seconds apiece and two in the rest of the time, and neither of the two got a figure.** One, what the place is called. Two, the moment it turned on. Three, what is still standing of it. Four, who is at the other end — **and he reaches for a Crown's word for the person a community appoints to authorise one named contact and strikes it out, because he does not know that anybody in that valley has appointed anybody to anything, and a man who writes that word into a page about a valley he has not been in is a man who has put a Crown's word on a thing because there was a space for it.** Five, what the going and the coming are called here, and six, what a day is, **and for six he writes *no frame*, which is the first figure of its kind he has ever entered.** Seven, somebody on this side who can say it was made and not what it was for, **and the answer has no name in the book, because the second of that county's six terms is that no name is to be written in the line's book at the north end and he has been in this county long enough to know that a line's book is a line's book.** Eight, what it is for, and nine, whether anybody at the other end has been asked, **and under nine he wrote that nobody there has been asked, that he is going anyway, that he wrote it down so that he would have to read it, that he read it, and that a man who writes a thing down so that he will be frightened by it in the morning has understood about half of what that does.** **No later writer may fill any of the three blanks and no later writer may say that anybody in the valley agreed to the road.**

406. **THE WITNESS AT THIS END IS BRAM OTTERY, AND HE ASKED FOR IT TO BE WRITTEN DOWN THAT HE SAID YES BEFORE HE DID IT AND NOT AFTER, AND IT IS THE FIRST ENTRY IN THAT MINUTE EVER MADE AT THE REQUEST OF THE PERSON IT WAS ABOUT.** Chapters 156 and 157. **He is forty-seven, on the bench because he was elected, paid fourpence a week out of a private box, no trade, and he is the only person in this county who can be produced about this and cannot be got at.** He said he would stand at the abutment on the Friday at the fourth hour and say that a man he knows was at that crossing at that hour and that he did not know what he did there, **and that he will never be able to tell anybody in nine years what the man came to do, and that he wanted it written down that he was willing to do it before he did it and not after, and that he was early because if he was a fool he would rather be a fool on a bridge at the fourth hour than in a room, because a room would remember it.** **The far end of that road had no witness at this stage of the block, and the block does not supply one, and the not-supplying is the moral cost of the crossing out and it is stated in the notebook and not improved on.**

407. **THE RETURN STITCH IS PREPARED IN THE WORST POSSIBLE PLACE, IN DAYLIGHT, IN FRONT OF ABOUT TWENTY MEN, ON THE OUTSIDE FACE OF A PUBLIC PARAPET, AT THE HEIGHT OF A THUMB, ON THE SIDE THE WEATHER GETS AT, AND IT IS A LINE AND A BAR AND A FIGURE AND NOT A NAME.** Chapter 155. **Cut with a cold chisel and not a stamp, at about the ninth hour of the sixth of Goatmonth, YR 313, with the hour against it and no maker's mark and no device.** A man of about sixty could look at it for a quarter of an hour and not be able to say what it was for. **A girl of about eleven came up onto the gravel from the near bank with rushes and put her right hand flat on the mark to see whether it was warm.** One of the twenty men asked whether he wanted a hand and was told no. **The not-securing is visible in the preparation and is not explained anywhere in this block, and the chapter's last line says only what a thing left out in daylight is.** A peg cut out of a fence rail in a county that is not on any map is the other end of the same act and a yard's book holds a fact and not the paper about both. **A later writer may not secure this stitch before Block 4, may not have it taken down before Block 4, and may not explain why he put it there.**

408. **THE CROSSING OUT WAS THE EIGHTH OF GOATMONTH, YR 313, A FRIDAY, NOT A MARKET DAY, AT THE FOURTH HOUR, FROM THE SILL OF THE OLD TOLL, AND THE FAR END OF IT HAS A LINTEL WITH NOTHING ON IT.** Chapter 157. **The four things said out loud on the bridge in about eleven seconds are a line, two hands, a date, and a witness at this end who is not the person keeping it, and with them, out loud, that he does not know what he is going for and is going and both are true at once.** The bell went at the fourth hour and a half behind him and he heard about a third of it, **and a Monday is the day that far end keeps and this was a Friday, and the two facts are in a day-book separately and are not in one sentence, because a book is a place where things get joined whether they were joined or not.** **The coping on each side of the Old Toll sill has nothing at all on it — no mark of a maker, no device, no rope, no yoke, no headstock and no striker — and this is not that coping and the man of sixty-four who swept a tile on one for forty-one years and wanted it lifted is not going to be sent for, and the road to that end of the line stays shut in four lines of writing.** **The tile on the coping is not explained, its device is named by nobody, and its being named here and in the third volume's last chapter as an object is not an explanation. No Volume 04 batch may schedule an explanation, a flashback, an origin, a maker or a deathbed.**

409. **THE NINEFOLD WINTER KEEPS NO MONTHS AND COUNTS WINTERS, A GENERATION IS A WINTER, AND THERE HAVE BEEN NINE, AND THE OLDEST PERSON IN THE VALLEY SAYS THE WINTER HAS NEVER ONCE BEEN ASKED WHETHER IT IS WANTED.** Chapters 157 to 160. **No main-world month, no real-world month and no main-world weekday is spoken or written in Chapters 158, 159 and 160 in any register, including a notebook, and the spoken register inside the valley is *winter*, *generation*, *the ninth week of the cold*, *the fourth day of the cold*, *a sleeping* and *a market day*, and no year in the valley is divided into anything.** The ninth generation is arguing and has not been asked what it argues about. **The man of about eighty-one has outlived two keepers of the winter book and was in the room over the cross sixty times and was never once asked, and he said that he is eighty-one and knows exactly what he would have said and that nobody ever thought to want to hear it.** **The one conversion attempted in this volume was attempted in his own notebook in the fourth week and refused there, and it is the second refusal of a conversion in this case and the first time he has had a number and no frame: he wrote nine years to a winter and then that a guess is not a frame, and wrote nine weeks and two sleeps, and left both on the page in two registers and did not do the arithmetic.** **A later Volume 04 writer may not convert a winter into a day of this calendar, may not print a main-world date in a valley scene in any register, and may not improve on the refusal.**

410. **THE VALLEY IS NOT STARVING AND NOBODY IN IT IS IN DANGER IN ANY WAY A RELIEF COULD FIX, AND THERE IS NOT ONE YARD OF MADE ROAD IN IT.** Chapters 158 to 160. **The Burn runs the whole nine miles of the valley at about four feet a second under old ice with a great deal of water in it and is a working river with a weir and a mill at the town.** There are eleven steadings, a scatter of hamlets and one market town that is a wide place with a cross, a smithy and a room over the cross. **The byres are full. Four seed houses hold, and about half of each is barley for two of the three weeks of a winter when there is nothing else, and two families count them twice in a winter and have never compared their counts in a book.** **Eleven children were born in the last twelve months in eleven steadings and the town, and a woman of about thirty with a slate comes up the bank about once in ten days and reads the numbers out to whoever is in the room, and nobody has ever argued with her about a number, and she carries the slate about eleven years and there is one other slate in the valley and it does not do the same work.** **There is not one orphan, nobody is hungry, nobody is cold, and there is no cart at the market at all — a barrow, three sledges on hard ground and one handcart — and a man of fifty who makes nails and cannot sell them because there is nothing in the valley to put nails in has been at that stall four market days running and nobody has told him to stop.** **The ninth generation leaves on foot over the upper pass on the fourth day of the cold, about eleven of them, in a line, and it takes a week to the top of the pass, and about four come back in the first warm week and the rest are somewhere else, and nobody in the valley can say where, and the four who come back will not say and one of them has asked a man not to ask him again.** **A valley that expects people to leave builds a road, and this valley has not built a road, and the reason is on the roll, and a woman with a yoke said she would like a stranger to be able to say what the rest of her gate is for because she has never been able to.**

411. **THE WINTER BOOK IS A ROLL NINE GENERATIONS DEEP IN A STONE ROOM OVER A BYRE, IT IS THE ONLY ROLL IN THE VALLEY, AND IT HAS NO SECOND COPY IN THREE SEASONS' TRAVEL, AND ITS COLUMNS ARE THE DAY, THE MARK, THE HAND, AND A FIFTH WITH A NAME IN IT ON THE OLDER SPREADS ONLY.** Chapter 159, and it is Iven Sarr's book. **Nobody who has ever kept it is in it, not one, and the man who first did that wrote one line at the head of the first spread saying so, and the first spread is not the beginning of anything.** The fourth spread is the sixth generation; **the ninth spread is the ninth generation and is about two hundred lines that begin at the top of a page and go down in one run, and every one of them has a day against it and a mark against it, and a day against a line of that kind is the day the person was born, and Sarr has kept it for six of the nine years and did not write any of it.** There have been two reasons in nine spreads and never a third, and he has looked for a third every winter for nineteen years. **A valley that expects people to leave builds a road, and this valley has not built a road, and the reason it has not built a road is on the roll.** **The hand question is Batch 0002's and nothing in this block examines the hand, raises it, or says anything is odd about it, and Sarr's refusal to read a name is about about two hundred people and not about the book.** The roll must be read in detail and by name in at least three chapters across this volume and the names on it are the volume's people, and **no Volume 04 chapter after this batch may name a person on the roll inside the budget of one new name per batch.**

412. **IVEN SARR'S WANT, ALL THREE PARTS, IN HIS OWN WORDS, AND THE SENTENCE HE FOUND IN HIS OWN HANDWRITING.** Chapter 159. **That the original oath be found and read in the room it was made in, in the room over the cross, in the cold, by a man of about his age, to a room of about the size it was, and the whole of it and not the parts that have held; and that the ninth generation be told what it signed; and that he be in the room for that, which he says he is not going to be able to arrange, because a man of fifty-eight who has kept a book for nineteen years is a man this valley will not stop asking to read out of.** He has wanted it read by somebody who was not him for six years, and has had two readings, and the first was a man who came through with a cart in the third year and got the fifth generation wrong in a way that has been in a copy ever since, and the second was a woman who read it over two nights and told him on the second morning that she had been wrong about the first. **Nobody in this valley has ever asked him what it is for and he has not told his want to a stranger in nineteen years, and he told it to a stranger who had been in the valley a month and had not asked him one question, and he said that if he had been asked in the first hour he would have told him nothing.** And then: **that a valley which has kept a thing for nine generations and has never once been asked whether it is keeping it or agreeing to it is not a valley with a tradition, it is a valley with a habit, and a habit is a thing a place does to itself when nobody is looking — said by him as a sentence he found in his own handwriting on the back of a leaf in the fifth year of keeping the book and has not looked at in nine years, and he has never once said it to anybody and has never once heard it.** **That sentence was written four months ago by the keeper of records of the Bellweather Claims Archive in a fair copy on a page that cannot be served, in a room two hundred yards from a yard on Weir Street, and nobody in this volume knows it and no character may tell him, and the two facts are not to be joined in any file, in any room, or in any sentence.**

413. **SOMEONE RECOGNISED HIM AS A CARRIER BEFORE HE HAD DECIDED TO BE ASKED, AND HE DID NOT ASK WHAT IT MEANT, AND IT IS THE VOLUME'S FIRST NOT-ASKING AND IT IS A DIFFERENT ONE FROM THE ONE IN MEREFEN, AND NO CHARACTER IN THIS BLOCK NOTICES THE PARALLEL.** Chapters 159 and 160. **The word is said about a young man of the ninth generation in a doorway, in an argument about a gate, and Aren Kest is nine feet away with a cup he has not drunk from and has never heard the word and does not ask, and every person in that room had heard it a thousand times.** Then at the fourth hour of a later morning a woman of about sixty-six, who has been at her trade for fifty-one years and has four looms and is called the old woman with the looms by her own arrangement, **says "You are the carrier off the road" in a gap in a sentence about a gate, and had not decided to say it, and then tells him to go slower and to tell the woman over the byre to sit down.** **He says "I am not a carrier" in about a second and a half, before he knows what the word means, and hears himself say it.** She declines to use the word again and declines to use his name for the rest of the day, and says she is not going to ask him what he are. **He stands at the gate for about a minute and does not ask, and about a quarter of an hour later he notices that he did it, and the page says that noticing afterwards is not the same as not having done it.** By the sixth hour four people in that valley are using the word about him and none of them has asked him anything. **There is no form in this valley on which to enter a word somebody said at a gate, and the roll has columns for the day, the mark and the hand, and that is the design and not an oversight, and in about nine years a woman in that market will remember that a stranger came up the bank in a winter and that somebody called him a word, and she will not be able to say which word, and no instrument in this kingdom can go and look.** **A later writer may not have him learn what the word means in this volume before the second asking, may not have any character remark that this not-asking resembles any other, and may not turn it into a resolution of the breach in Merefen. A carrier is not a custodian and no Volume 04 character may call one the other.**

414. **THE GATEHOUSE VOICE, ONCE, IN CHAPTER 160, AND IT IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN.** *You are expected.* It arrives while his hand is on a stone lintel with nothing on it, in a valley that is not on any map, and **he has had four of these in four years and has written down exactly one, which has no hour against it and no name and which he cannot account for, and this one he does not write down, and that is three not-doings on one morning, none of them a decision.** **The device of the tile on the coping is not named and the mechanism of a crossing is not explained, and no character in this batch can say what the line is or why it works, and nobody learns why he can cross.**

415. **THE BREACH IS OPEN AND THIS BLOCK DID NOT ENTER A TENTH NOT-ASKING, AND IT WORKED ON THE BREACH IN PUBLIC AND REPAIRED NOTHING.** Chapters 155 and 156. **On the eleventh hour of the sixth of Goatmonth he came up the two flights and gave her the numbers before she asked, in the order they happened: the eighth of this month at the fourth hour on a line made up in nine minutes; a county four hundred miles off that is in nobody's book; a man of fifty-eight and two readings and one of them a night; a valley with a river in it and a roll nine generations deep and about two hundred people on it from birth, all of it out of a letter read aloud in that room and not out of his own observation; the printed three weeks unchanged and belonging to nobody; the leg refused a figure; and the ninth not asking, entered on the sixteenth of Longlight, standing, and not made a tenth.** And then the first thing in four years and a half that is new: **he said that there was no morning in it, and that there was no morning in it because he does not know what a day is over there and has not asked and is not going to guess one, and that a man who guesses a day in a place that does not use days is a man who has invented a thing and then had to live inside it.** She entered that as a fact, **and read back an entry that says this office has entered that statement as a fact and has not asked him for the thing it stands in for, and the reason is on the page and the reason is *he is not able to write it and there is nothing to write*, and she said that a keeper who asks that is asking a person to be able to do a thing, and that a person who cannot do a thing ought not to be asked to do it.** **The third of the three rules ends *a habit is a thing a county does to itself when nobody is looking*, and neither of them has ever said that it is about him, and it is on the page of Chapter 156 as a thing in a notebook and it is not said out loud in that chapter and he does not write it down.** **No apology in any form in a scene, an aside or a document in these ten chapters, and no mistake has been made available to anybody, and the Volume 04 intimacy is not bought early.**

416. **STAGE 3 IS NOT REACHED, NOT ATTEMPTED, NOT OFFERED AS A PLAN, NOT PRICED AND NOT DESCRIBED AS AVAILABLE BY ANYBODY IN THIS BLOCK, AND NO LINEAGE IS READ.** **The `cut` string occurs thirteen times in Chapters 151–160 and every one of them is ordinary, and the working is not among them, and the working is not named.** The `---` section rule was at thirty-eight in the first pass of this block and is at ten. No bodily cost is added: **the limp stands as Volume 03 left it, in the right leg, with a stick for four hundred yards of road, and he carries the stick four hundred miles and the stick is useless in a valley with no road, and that is not a cost and it is a fact.** No melody cost is added and the word does not appear. **The Many-Handed stage's worsening of the limp belongs to Volume 15.**

417. **THE THREE MARKS ON THE OUTSIDE OF THE SEED VAULT ARE NOT MENTIONED IN THIS BLOCK AND THE KEEPER'S DECISION ABOUT THEM IS NOT TAKEN, AND THE ROAD TO THE MARCHES' END OF THE LINE WAS NOT REOPENED AND THE FOUR LINES CAME DOWN AGAIN.** **The spring is a date in the Marches' own calendar and is not named here.** The eight ruled line in the served schedule is not looked at. The brine weights are neither mentioned nor filed. The five blanks of Volume 02 are not joined and no two of them are in one room, in one chapter or in one sentence. *Culling Order* does not appear. The word *custodian* does not appear and the Crown's title for a person a community appoints to authorise one contact is described on the page of Chapter 156 without being named, and he strikes it out. *Gatehouse* does not appear. Sian Pugh's name is not spoken once in the ten chapters.

418. **THE FIGURES, THE DEVICES AND THE LENGTH FOR THE BATCH, CHECKED ON THE PAGE.** **33,045 words**, per chapter **3766 / 3512 / 3281 / 3311 / 3388 / 3078 / 3003 / 3213 / 3265 / 3228**, **which is the count after the Batch 0001 review repair pass and not the count the batch first wrote.** **The block is over Volume 03 Batch 0011's 31,648 and under Batch 0014's 35,340, and no chapter is under 3,003, and this is the length `outline/volumes/volume-03-close.md` §10 item 3 asked for and not Batch 0013's length.** The manuscript is **601,642 + 33,045 = 634,687 words in one hundred and sixty chapters**, and Volume 04 is 33,045 in ten. **Money foots once on the page, in pence, before the total is said: 10 + 4 = 14 a day, 14 nine times = 126, four sheets at twopence = 8, and 134 pence, two marks and three shillings and twopence.** **The Marches' contract is cited and not re-derived. The fair copy of 408 words and its working are read and copied and not re-footed, and the total at the foot of the county's addition is not said in a speech anywhere in this volume.** No 456, no 254, no 2,450, no 2,906, no 9-4-1, and no hearth figure in any Marches scene. **Ten `---` rules, one per chapter, down from 38 in the first pass; forty-six bolded line-openings; zero semicolons; zero em-dashes; `the whole of` 10, down from 37, of which two are a document's fourth line printed twice because it is read twice; `about N seconds` 9; `cut` 14, all ordinary; one Gatehouse-voice line and no System panel.** Filler counts as whole words, carried forward as a baseline and not as a target: **`nodded` 0, `held` 11, `wrote` 37, `stood` 13, `plain` 2, `counted` 8, `breathed` 0, `steady` 0. All of these are the post-repair counts.** **REPAIRED at the Batch 0001 review and re-counted on the page: the block's first printing gave 32,831 words, `cut` 13 and `counted` 9, and the repair moved ten words into Chapter 152, a hundred and twelve into 155, twenty-three into 156, ten into 157, thirty-five into 158 and twenty-four into 160, and left 151, 153, 154 and 159 exactly as they were, for a block total of two hundred and fourteen words. The `about` count is unchanged at 287, one removed from 156 with the bell's second distance and one added to 160 with the valley's arrangements about the old man. `the whole of` is 10 after the repair and was 9 before it, and the reviewer's count of 9 was right and the state file's claim of 10 was wrong until the repair made it true. `about` is 287 in the block and rises 25 / 21 / 25 / 21 / 28 / 27 / 29 / 30 / 39 / 42, and the review recorded the density as a note and not as a defect, because the ages and the distances in a valley where nobody can give a figure exactly are the method.**

## Relationship state at the end of Chapter 160

- **Aren and Mara Vey: the breach, open, worked on in public, not repaired, and not bought early.** He came up the two flights on the eleventh hour of the sixth of Goatmonth and gave her the numbers before she asked, in the order they happened, and gave her the leg as a leg and refused it a figure for the fifth time. **And for the first time in four years and a half there was no morning in it, and he said so, and the reason he gave was not a refusal and not an apology: he does not know what a day is over there and will not guess one, and a man who guesses a day in a place that does not use days has invented a thing and then had to live inside it.** She entered that as a fact, and entered that this office had not asked him for the thing it stands in for, and said out loud that a keeper who asks that is asking a person to be able to do a thing, and that a person who cannot do a thing ought not to be asked to do it, and asked for the entry to be read back to nobody but her. **The ninth not asking stands, entered on the sixteenth of Longlight, and this batch does not enter a tenth, and neither of them said why.** He did not tell her he cannot; there was nothing this time for him not to tell her, and the shape of that is the only thing either of them has, and neither of them has drawn it. **The third rule's final clause is about him and he has now written the paragraph around it in his own notebook in Chapter 156 and has still not said so to her, and she has not asked, and it is a habit and not a choice.** **She now knows a refusal of four hundred and eleven words came back cut open and she learned it from a document, and he was four hundred yards away and did not know, and that is a fifth thing neither of them has said, and it is the first of the five that has arrived in a room with two people absent from it.** No apology, in any form, in a scene, an aside or a document, in these ten chapters, and no mistake has been made available to anybody. **The intimacy is not bought early and the volume's chosen intimacy is Block 4's and Block 5's.**
- **Aren and the bench of nine: a fifth answer, and a road of paper that carries nobody.** He was in the room at the seventh hour on the twenty-fifth of Hearthmonth and did not use his vote and nobody asked him to. The bench was asked the same thing five times, said yes four times, and said no to the fifth in about a minute and a half on the grounds that it is a subscription and not a bench, and a road built to the first of another county's six terms carries nobody. **The person who did not put the fifth asking is Reeve Aldis Fenn, and she is the reason the copy was worth sending, and she is a reeve who has been asked and has voted and uses a casting vote and who asked that a door be minuted as a thing you can be killed in.** He is on the roll with a vote and not an office and it is not enough to build anything on and he has never said so out loud in that hall.
- **Aren and Bram Ottery: a witness who asked to be a worse witness in writing.** A man of forty-seven, elected, fourpence a week out of a private box, who has never known what the other four men on his bench do and could not say what the yard four hundred yards down Weir Street is for. **He agreed to witness a man being on a bridge and said he would never be able to say what the man came to do, and he wanted it written down that he said yes before he did it and not after, and he was on the abutment twenty minutes early because if he was a fool he would rather be a fool on a bridge at the fourth hour than in a room.** That is the first entry in that minute ever made at the request of the person it was about, and the reeve initialled it. **He is the only person in this county who can be produced about the crossing and cannot be got at, and the far end of that road had no witness at all, and the block does not supply one.**
- **Aren and Iven Sarr: the first man in four hundred miles who told a stranger his whole want, and told it because he had not been asked a question.** A man of fifty-eight, nineteen years keeping a book, two readings and one of them lasted a night, who has wanted the book read for six years and stopped expecting it about a fortnight ago. **He told a stranger he had met a month earlier the whole of his want and said that if he had been asked in the first hour he would have told him nothing and gone on not asking him, and that is what has happened four times.** He will not read a name to a stranger and will not read one tomorrow, and the reason is about two hundred people. **He used a sentence out of his own handwriting that nobody in the book knows the source of, and no character may tell him.** At the end of Chapter 160 he has said there is a fifth thing and it is the last thing he has got and he is keeping it for a man who asked, and he has asked a man who had been in the valley a month to ask him a question that is not about the book.
- **Aren and the valley: recognised in a doorway by a word he does not know, twice.** A young man of the ninth generation stopped in a doorway because a word was used about him in an argument about a gate, and a man nine feet away had never heard the word and did not ask. **At the fourth hour of a later morning a woman of about sixty-six said "You are the carrier off the road" in a gap in a sentence about a gate and had not decided to say it, and he said "I am not a carrier" in about a second and a half before he knew what the word meant, and she declined to use the word again and declined to use his name.** By the sixth hour four people were using it. **There is nowhere in that valley to enter a word somebody said at a gate, and the not-asking is this volume's first one, and it is a different one from the one in Merefen, and it is going to cost more, and nobody in the block has noticed that it resembles anything.**
- **Aren and the woman at the Low Holm and the man of about eighty-one: a gate and a bench and a soup.** The woman with a yoke told him unasked that the room over the stair is the winter book and that nobody in nine generations has had that room in a day, and told him the valley's way of not asking a stranger anything: on the bank a thing is said to the river and at the fire a thing is said to a person. The old man told him the winter has never once been asked whether it is wanted, and that he would have said no, and then asked him to have some more soup. **A girl of about nine at a gate told him the whole of the valley's position in nine words and a sentence, and would not give her name, and gave him a place instead.**
- **Aren and the man of thirty-four and sixteen men: a floor laid wrong, and no request.** Sixteen men who can build a road and have not had a job in this valley since before he was twenty. **He was shown three faults in a floor in about four seconds from a doorway and said all three, and the man said that that finishes the first day and that he was not going to ask him to do anything and would like it understood that he had not asked.** The valley's word for a roadkeeper is *the hand*, said once, and not argued, and a reader who has met it in two other counties is left to do what he likes.
- **Aren and the woman of about thirty with the slate: a room where refusal is not the point.** She came up the bank about once in ten days and read the numbers out to whoever was in the room, and nobody has ever argued with her about one, and she told him, without being asked, that he would find out what the word is and that she was telling him a week early so that he could have had it before he asked anybody. **She is the only person in the valley who has warned him about anything and she warned him about a word and not about a danger.**
- **Aren and Tovan Kest: one exchange in a gateway, six words, and nothing else.** **"You said you were going to be here on Monday and it is Wednesday," said Tovan Kest, and went on planing, and that is the whole of what was said in that gateway.** A job on the bench-board with a line under the date that the boy of fifteen ruled and filled with nothing, and the yard's rule that nothing belonging to a man goes in that yard's book and only a thing set, and a man going out of a county is not a thing set. **The word brother is not used and nothing in this block touches the estrangement, and the yard is off the page for nine of the ten chapters and that absence is the cost.**
- **Aren and Lysa Fenn, Aldis Fenn, Alish Renn and Sarn Oyelaran: a room with four people in it and a body corporate in it that can be sued.** Lysa beat a count in nine minutes with a construction nine words long and said out loud that she had just handed a general machine to anybody with a door. The reeve put the fifth asking and asked that a door be minuted as a thing you can be killed in. **The second copyist has four things in four years and a half that she has written down, ruled a list with two inches of paper left bare, entered a coincidence and done one single thing with it, and opened a letter that was not addressed to her and said the reason out loud in the room.** The junior clerk wanted a column for what came back and was refused, and is a man who wants a post with his name in the day-book and still does not have it.
- **Aren and the Office of Provincial Registration and Sabin Dain: a refusal that came back cut, and a figure with no name in it, and neither of them in a room.** Her offer is dead in a four-hundred-and-eleven-word document and the document has come back open and the only copy is in a press in this county. **The clause that landed is the number of persons the offer has been made out to, which is not stated on the sheet, and the Archive has asked for it in a return with no name in it, and the number has not been supplied.** The office's only answer to a legal argument was a figure of 2,640 with no seal and no name. **She is not in this volume in a room and is not the person who explains the marginal instruction, and her want is unchanged and nothing in this block touched it.**
- **The Marches' sixty, the four gateway answers, the four true words, the man of fifty-two's entry, the three marks on the vault, Sian Pugh: not in this block, not asked about, and not available.** No Volume 04 character may be a Marches character coming home, and no Volume 04 scene may ask a Marches character anything. **Aled Rhys is the one Marches face on the page in this block and he is a water-barge hand working in Merefen on a crew's account, and he read a fair copy of his own county's account under a bench and asked for a copy and got one, and the reason he wanted it is that he has been asked eleven times what his county gave away and cannot answer, and a man who cannot answer gets told he is lying.**
