No main-world month, no real-world month and no main-world weekday is spoken or written in any valley scene in any register including a notebook, in any of the ten chapters, and there is no main-world room in the block at all.**

456. **THREE CALENDAR DEFECTS IN THIS BLOCK'S OWN TEXT, ALL THE SAME DEFECT, ALL FOUND AND REPAIRED BEFORE THE BATCH WAS FINISHED, AND IT IS THE SEVENTH TIME IN THIS PROJECT THAT CARRYING A FIGURE INSTEAD OF COUNTING IT HAS PRODUCED A MAIN-WORLD CALENDAR IN A VALLEY SCENE.** One: a speaker said *it was a Thursday* in a room over a byre, **which is a main-world weekday spoken aloud in a valley scene**, and it is now *there is no day in this valley to put against it*. Two: a character said *the eighth of a Goatmonth*, **which is a main-world month name in a valley scene**, and it is now *the eighth of the month he came out on*; and the same chapter described the woman with the slate being asked *on a Tuesday*, which is now *on a day that is not a day anybody in that valley keeps*. Three: a character said *the twenty-seventh of a Fallowmonth* about the last Crown's hand in a county, **which is a main-world month name spoken in a valley scene**, and it is now *a day at the end of a month it keeps, and this valley has never heard of that month*. **The rule does not change: a later phase states a figure, checks it, and records the check, and a state file is the least reliable document in this repository.**

457. **AND TWO INTERNAL FIGURE ERRORS FOUND IN THE BLOCK'S OWN TEXT AND REPAIRED, BOTH OF THEM THE SAME KIND.** One: **the form's fourth column was first answered on the page with the stroke-under mark and the count of nine, which is the wrong mark** — the stroke under a barred T is a person who has gone out and not come back, and the stroke through it from the top is a person who went out and came back, and there are nine of *those* in the whole book and the last is a hundred and forty years old — **and the passage now keeps the two marks apart and says that the valley has never counted the strokes under a mark in nine spreads and has wanted to for nineteen years and has not, and that the answer to a column that wants a figure is a person.** Two: **Chapter 175 first had the woman of the house say her husband's grandmother cut the stroke and then had a man of seventy-four say he cut it at nineteen, which is two cutters fifty-five years and ninety years apart, and the whole of the third generation's house's chronology, the age of the stroke and the man who cut it have been re-set so that one man cut it, at nineteen, about fifty-five years ago, in this corner of this yard, and his brother came home about sixty-three years ago and is dead, and the stroke is the newest of the nine marks on that wall.** No scene, no character and no plot beat changed in either repair.

458. **NO THREAD INHERITED IS CLOSED AND NONE IS ANSWERED.** The nineteen the Volume 03 close handed over, the nineteen Batch 0001 carried forward and the nineteen Batch 0002 carried forward all stand. **And of the five threads this batch opened, it closes none.** The form thread is opened three times wider and answered once inside it: what the form is, whose office it is, why it was never answered, and where the valley's confusion was written down. **A batch summary that says this batch closed the form is a summary that has not read Chapter 172.** The oath thread remains **answered and not resolved**: the four lines at the head of the first spread were read out for the first time in a hundred and forty years, and they are a rule about keepers and not the oath, and the oath is still not in the book and not in the room and is still four steps down under a byre with a form under a stone on it.

## Relationship state at the end of Chapter 180

- **Aren Kest and Mara Vey: the breach open, untouched in this block, and further away than at the end of Chapter 170 by a consent and a form.** He is four hundred miles off in a valley in its second winter. **There is no main-world room in Chapters 171 to 180 and no cut to the north, and he is not in that county at any point in them, and nothing happens in it that he learns of, and no character in this block refers to her.** The ninth not asking stands and this block does not enter a tenth and no number is put on the page. **The third rule's final clause is still about him and neither of them has ever said so and this block did not make either of them say so.** The intimacy is not bought and nothing in this block touches it. **And the one thing he did in this block that has anything to do with any of it is that he tore a leaf out of the back of his own notebook and gave it to a man of fifty-eight, and the notebook is the only record of a crossing and a concealment in one book, and the page that went has nine lines on it and one of them is about a word, and it is the first page he has given to anybody in four years and a half, and he asked a man whether it was a bad idea and was told that it is a bad idea.**

- **Aren Kest and Iven Sarr: the fifth thing is out, the form is out, and the man has found out what his own want of nineteen years was.** A man of fifty-eight who had kept the only book in a valley for nineteen years and had not let it out of the room for one of the two reasons a person can have. **He read the whole of a two-hundred-year-old form out loud in a room four feet by six, once, to a stranger, and wrote six lines on the back of it, and put the stone back on crooked because he could not get the heel of his hand out from under the far edge of it.** **He read the four lines at the head of the first spread for the first time in a hundred and forty years and they were the answer to the fifth column of the form, and his great-grandfather wrote them having read that column, and that is where nine generations of a confusion between four words for a person was written down.** **He put three figures in his book for the first time in a hundred and forty years and put no name against the nine, and says the reason is the same reason as the four lines and that he did not know that until the afternoon.** **And in Chapter 179 he was told, by a stranger, in his own room, that the reason he has refused four people that book in nineteen years was not that he did not trust them with it, and that this has been the only thing standing between about two hundred people and a figure in a file two hundred miles off, and that he is not going to give the want up, because the reason it worked is the same reason it is a want.** He is the fifth thing, the form, the first figure and the first copy, and he has said out loud that he wants something new and has not said what it is.

- **Aren Kest and the ninth generation: a refusal that stands and a consent that was given, and the two of them are in the same room and one of them is named.** A young man of twenty-two who put a hurdle down on a step in a doorway in the ninth week of the first cold refused the form of an asking in four seconds, and that refusal stands and is not repeated anywhere in this block. **Ten weeks later he is Osgar Vell and he came up nine steps to say his own name, and he has said that he is not the first in nine generations to be asked, and that he is going over the pass on the fourth day of the next cold and has never had an answer he could hand a person.** **And the young man who said no in Chapter 166 is not one of the three and has not said a word about the asking at all, and the man off the road asked him nothing and stood at the front of the room on purpose.** The difference between the two answers is the volume's argument and it is delivered by a man of twenty-two and a man of thirty-four and not by him.

- **Aren Kest and Wystan Roole: an ask that was answered, a road that is not a road, and a word he is not allowed to translate.** A man of thirty-four asked him once, in a room with a book in it, and has now asked him again in a cold room with fourteen people in it and has told him *how*, which is *walk*. **He spent nine years refused twice for a road and has worked out in one week that no council ever decided not to build one, and that the reason there is no road is that about four hundred people have never once wanted to be anywhere, and the finding is said once in a yard and is not repeated.** He has told the man off the road the strain, which is a trade fact and not the mechanism, and he has stopped himself twice from saying the mechanism, and the page shows him not saying it. **He is also the man who takes the return stitch down at the end of Block 4, with an explanation, and the volume does not make him wrong, and nothing in this block foreshadows it and the return stitch is not mentioned once in these ten chapters.** He has built the first bridge in the valley in nine generations, over four feet of a beck, in four days, and has a nail man crossing it four times a day, and he is going to build a second at the ford in the warm week, and the word the valley has for a bridge is on the page once and is in forty mouths and in no book.

- **Aren Kest and Osgar Vell: a name given, a question given, and a not-translation given, and the young man has the better reason of the two.** He came up nine steps to say a name and got four other things out of the room, and the worst of them was that a person nobody is appointed to answer for is not in a worse position than a person who is, because nothing in this valley can be produced against him either, and that is not justice, and it is the same hole in a different direction. **He is the one who says the eighth spelling is not a word, and that there are two accounts of where a word came from and no instrument in this kingdom that can check either, and that a man of thirty-two is the only person he has met who could check either and cannot check a word out of a man's mouth.** He is the one who told the room that a family cannot say a thing like that out loud and a wall will hold it for a hundred and forty years, and who is going over the pass in about a month with about eleven others.

- **Aren Kest and the man of seventy-four at a fire and the woman of sixty-eight in a kitchen: two people who have had a thing for fifty-five and forty-eight years and have said it once each, to a stranger, because a stranger cannot be at the next market.** The man of seventy-four cut a stroke through his brother's mark with a cold chisel off a roof slate in nine minutes in a wet week and has never said why, and the woman of sixty-eight knew and never told, and she told because a man of thirty-two asked her four things at a door. **Neither is named and neither is merged with any other face in the block**, and the woman is not the woman of the Low Holm and is not the woman of about thirty with a slate and is not the woman of sixty-six at four looms, and the man is not the man of eighty-one and is not the man of the seventh generation in the byre.

- **Aren Kest and the ninth spread: a figure at the foot of it in a hand that varies, and he did not write it down, and there is nowhere in four hundred miles to put that he knows a day on that page.** The three figures went in on the twenty-fourth day of the second cold in a man of fifty-eight's hand, and the hand over the three of them is a hand and not an office's hand and not the hand in the third column of the ninth spread. **He has been in a room four feet by six with that page open and has looked at the line at the head of it and has said nothing about it and has not asked, and Chapter 173 makes the restraint explicit and in a man's mouth: there is one line in that book he is not going to put beside that paper, and that is the whole of what is left of his six years, and it does not go on a form.** No batch may schedule an explanation, a flashback, an origin, a maker or a deathbed for the hand, and this batch scheduled none.

- **Aren Kest and the form: it is on the page, and he is not allowed to describe it, and he asked for a word and was given a rule.** He read the whole of it once, out loud, in a room four feet by six, and he is the only person in the world who could have checked the two accounts of where a word in that valley came from, and he cannot check a word out of a man's mouth, and he will not describe a document to nine people. **He has a scrap of rag paper about the size of a hand with four lines on it, copied out by a man of twenty-two, which is the first copy of a thing ever made in that room, and a leaf torn out of his own notebook with nine lines on it, which is the first page he has given to anybody in four years and a half, and a piece of rag paper with nine bushels and a peck of barley and a peck on it somewhere, and the notebook is the only record of a crossing and a concealment in one book and he has given a page out of it and the rest of it is still in a coat.**

- **The valley: the second asking, the nine, the stand across the beck, the wall, and a form under a stone that has been answered by nobody.** **About nine hundred doors in eleven days with the same six things in the same words, and nothing written down at any of them, and about four hundred people who were asked a thing and cannot prove they were asked it, and a bridgekeeper who worked the count out in nine minutes in four heads.** A stand over four feet of a beck in four days with two oak sills and a batter on the abutment, and a nail man crossing it. A wall of four hundred feet holding up a byre and due a thaw the man who built it is not here for. **Eleven people over a pass who cannot be asked and have not been asked and will not be able to be asked for about nine weeks, of whom about four will come back and seven will not, and the seven are the only people in the world who could say no, and nothing can be done about that and the volume does not resolve it in this block.**

- **The Marches' sixty, the four gateway answers, the four true words, the man of fifty-two's entry, the three marks on the vault, Sian Pugh: not in this block, not asked about, and not available.** No Volume 04 character may be a Marches character coming home and no Volume 04 scene may ask a Marches character anything. **Sera Quen does not appear in these ten chapters and the intimacy is Block 4's and Block 5's and may not be bought in this block.**

## Canon established by Batch 0004 (Volume 04, Chapters 181–190, prose on the page)

**Items 1–458 are the record of Volume 01, of the Volume 02 plan, of Chapters 51–100, of the Volume 02 close, of Chapters 101–150, of the Batch 0015 review repair pass, of the Volume 03 close, of Volume 04 Batch 0001, of Volume 04 Batch 0002, of the Batch 0002 review repair pass and of Volume 04 Batch 0003, and none of them is renumbered by this section. Items 442–458 are Batch 0003's and are not repeated here. This batch closed no thread and answered none of the nineteen the Volume 03 close handed over, none of the nineteen Batch 0001 carried forward, none of the nineteen Batch 0002 carried forward and none of the nineteen Batch 0003 carried forward.**

459. **THE RETURN STITCH IS A BRIDGE PARAPET IN THE VALLEY AND IT IS THE SAME MARK HE CUT IN THE MAIN WORLD, AND A VALLEY TOOK IT DOWN PROPERLY, IN PUBLIC, IN DAYLIGHT, WITH THE REASON GIVEN TWICE BEFORE A BAR WENT ON A STONE, AND HE AGREED, AND AGREEING IS THE WHOLE OF HIS FOURTH COLD.** Chapters 181, 182 and 183. **The mark is a line and a bar and a figure, at the height of a thumb, on the face that gets the weather, in the coping of the far abutment of the stand at the Low Holm, and it has been there since the ninth week of the third cold, and it is the same mark he cut with the same cold chisel into the outside face of a public parapet at the Sedge Reach at the ninth hour of the sixth of Goatmonth, YR 313, in front of about twenty men, and a girl of about eleven put her right hand flat on it to see whether it was warm, and a girl of about nine put her hand flat on the one in the valley and said it was not warm, to nobody.** The two marks are one act at the two ends of one line, which is what Chapter 155's last line says, and the reason for the second is in his own interior in Chapter 182: **a place you come back to has to be a place you can stand in, and that one was four hundred miles away and a man with a limp cannot get to a place in about four seconds.** **The two marks are reconciled in the valley and the main-world one is untouched, is not in the taking down, and is not going to be the way out, and no second stitch is created and no second road is offered and no way out is built.** Nothing about the mark or the stitch is explained and no mechanism is touched.

460. **THE VALLEY'S OWN ARGUMENT, IN NINE SENTENCES, AND IT IS RIGHT, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS A RULE HE HAS SAID IN FOUR COUNTRIES AND NEITHER OF THEM SAYS SO.** Chapter 181. **A stand is made by two ends and a day and somebody who was not either of the two ends: *you do not get a stand by carrying stone to a place; you get it by having a place you start and a place you finish, and a day you did it on, and a person who is not you standing at the finish who saw it happen and can say it happened.*** He cannot read the figure and is not a witness because he laid the coping. There is another end to it about four hundred miles off where nothing has been agreed to and nobody knows the valley is on a map, and he has never seen a road and does not know what one is made of and says so before using the word. **The half of it that is not there is not missing, it is absent, and a mark on a stone is not wrong and is not broken and has not come to any harm, because there was never anything at the other end of it for it to do.** And the public half: **a mark on a public thing is not a mark any more, it is a handle, and in nine years there will be a story on that coping and the story will have started in the place where the mark is, and there will be no way anybody in this valley can ever get back to the ninth day of this cold and find out whose it was.** He said it once in a room of eleven and again in a cutting to about forty people, and the reason for the second telling is that a reason given once to a room of nine is an account and a reason given twice in the open is a reason. **He will not chip the mark out, and the reason is that a chipped place is a question and he is not going to put a question in a public stone in a valley with no writ and no bell and no office.** The mark is taken out **to a whole course of nine stones and not to the mark alone**, and nobody rubbed it out and about nine of about forty people noticed.

461. **THE NINE STONES GO INTO THE FOOTING OF THE SECOND STAND AT THE FORD, UNDER FOUR FEET OF WATER, IN THE ORDER THEY CAME OFF, AND THE REASON IS GIVEN BY A MILL MAN OF SIXTY-ONE AND CONCEDED IN ONE WORD.** Chapters 183 and 184. **Not broken, not in the beck, not in a wall where a barrow goes over it four times a day. Under the water, where a barrow cannot go and a nine-year-old cannot get a hand. A mill man of sixty-one: *under the water is where a thing goes that you are not going to look at again*, and the man of thirty-four says yes and that it is the honest end and not a tidy one and that he is not going to pretend to a man of sixty-one that it is a good place for a stone.** The fourth stone is the one off the byre coping at the third generation's house, a hundred and forty years old and squared on one face, and **the mark on it is still readable in the flat light for about four months until the water comes up over it on the fourteenth day.** The footing is what holds the course and not the stones, and the man of thirty-four set the whole of it himself and would not let anybody else touch that course, and said he has laid a footing twice in nine years and laid the second one wrong and there is a man in this valley who knows and he is not going to say which of them it was. **The ford moves about a foot a year and the man of thirty-four has known it for nine years and has never once said it in a room, and he does not know where that footing goes when the ford moves and that is the thread this block opened.**

462. **HE IS STRANDED, AND THE STRANDING IS NINE WEEKS, AND NOBODY IN THE VALLEY OR IN THE MAIN WORLD BUILDS HIM A WAY OUT, AND NO SECOND MARK, LINE, WITNESS, PREPARATION OR OFFER EXISTS ANYWHERE IN CHAPTERS 181 TO 190.** Chapters 184 and 185. **The plain fact was said out loud once, in about nine sentences, in the room over the cross on the fourth of the third week, with no figure of any kind attached to it, and it is the first time in this case that a man has been stuck somewhere with no way out of it and had it said.** He is not getting out before the warm week. The man of thirty-four had known it since the second day of the fourth cold and had not said anything, and his reason is given before he asks anything: **a man who has just been told he is stuck is not a man you can give a job to, and he had sixteen men and no work and was not going to spend that on a man's face.** He thought about building a road on the first of the four days and is not going to, and **the reason is not that he would not: a road to the top of this bank that a man did not ask for is not a road out of this valley, it is a road to a place where a man stands, and nothing at the other end of it has been agreed to by anybody in this valley, and he has spent nine days taking a stranger's mark out of a public stone for exactly that reason and is not going to do the same thing with four hundred yards of ground.** **He is not allowed to lay a stone in the valley at all, and the reason is given before anybody thinks of asking: if a man off the road lays a stone in this valley then in nine years there will be a thing in this valley that a stranger built and about forty people watched, and the only difference between that and the mark is which side of it the light is on.** The stick is put against a wall of the room over the cross between the second bench and the third, and **the reason is that there is nowhere in a valley with no road to put a stick down, and it is not called a cost and nobody calls it one and the man of eighty-one's Chapter 164 sentence is not restated as a discovery.** **A road that does not open and a road that fails are not confused anywhere in this block and no character uses the word about either.**

463. **THE NINE WEEKS ARE SIXTY-THREE DAYS AND THEY ARE THE VOLUME'S TRAINING BLOCK, AND HE FAILS AT THE LOCAL CRAFT PUBLICLY TWICE AND IS CORRECTED BY A MAN NINE YEARS HIS JUNIOR, AND HE COUNTS LOAD POINTS FOR THE FIRST TIME IN HIS LIFE FOR SOMEBODY ELSE.** Chapters 184 and 185. **The one hundred and forty days of work are the mill, nine roofs the ninth generation will not let them put up, a four hundred yard approach that is not a road, and a second stand at the ford.** A course is counted in loads, a load in barrows, a barrow in shovels, and the number is called out loud in a yard in a voice nine people can hear. **His word is *load points* and it is not theirs, and the man of thirty-four makes him say what it is and stops him counting, and tells the yard that about thirty men under the cross are not going to learn a figure they cannot check.** **First public failure, the ninth day of the third week: he counts what they brought up, and the man of thirty-four tells him the difference between that and what they laid is the hearting, and the hearting is what is going to be under a thaw, and the right figure is lower than the figure of barrows by about a fifth, and sixteen men heard the difference and nine of the ninth generation heard a man off the road get a thing wrong out loud and take the correction without a word.** **Second public failure, the forty-first day: he lays a floor in a trough at the mill the way a floor is laid in four counties, and the mill man puts a loaded barrow across it and it goes down an inch and says *who laid that*, and a man of about fifty-one says a floor is not a floor, it is a pitching, it is stones laid on stones, every stone wants a stone under it and a stone beside it and nothing at all under that, and you have given every stone in that trough earth on three sides, and it will come down about four years of it, one stone at a time, starting with the one you would have pointed at.** Eleven stones up in an hour, laid again on stones in two days, and the loaded barrow goes across and does not go down an inch, and the man of fifty-one says nothing about that either. **The ninth generation's reason for the roofs is a man of about twenty-four's: a roof is for a family, the sixteen under a cross are not a family, a stand is four days and a roof is a family, and his mother gave him that sentence in a kitchen in the second month of the cold and nobody has ever asked him about it and he would like somebody to.** No new bodily cost: the limp stands as Volume 03 left it, in the right leg, and no melody cost is added and the word does not appear.

464. **THE WAGES OF THE NINE WEEKS, FOOTED IN PENCE ON THE PAGE BEFORE THE TOTAL IS SAID, AND THE VALLEY'S OWN PRICE REFUSED AND ADDED TO NOTHING, AND NOT A REPETITION OF CHAPTER 180's FIGURE.** Chapter 185. *Sixteen men, sixty-three days, at three pence the day:* 3, sixteen times over, is 48. 48, sixty-three times over, is **three thousand and twenty-four**. *Two barrows of salt at fourpence:* 4, twice over, is **eight**. **Three thousand and twenty-four and eight is three thousand and thirty-two pence, which is sixty-three marks and eightpence.** **The sixteen men and the man off the road are not on the list, because there is no money in this valley to put them on a list with, and the nine weeks were eaten out of nine kitchens and one beest and a quantity that four households call a root and the rest of the valley calls a word they do not spell, and not one household was asked twice and not one household was told what it was for. The two are not added and there is no way on this earth to add them.** He does not put the figure in chalk on a trestle and the reason is given: **the trestle falls down and the chalk will be off it inside a year and he will be gone, and a figure that a man off a road leaves in a valley in chalk is a thing that outlives him and means nothing.** Chapter 180's eleven kitchens and 532 pence are not repeated and the two prices of three loads of lime of Chapter 167 are not repeated and no county figure is set beside a valley figure anywhere in this block.

465. **THE COUNCIL IS ASKED TO KEEP THE WINTER AND ASKED WHAT HAPPENS IF IT DOES NOT, AND IT VOTES EIGHT TO ONE TO KEEP IT, AND THE SECOND QUESTION IS IN THE MINUTE IN FOUR WORDS, AND IT IS THE MARCHES IN A WARMER PLACE AND IT IS NOT A RESCUE AND NOBODY CALLS IT ONE.** Chapters 186 and 187. **Nine people in the room over the cross, the aisle four feet wide and empty for the whole of both days, and the tenth generation is the first that has never stood in it and the aisle has now gone three generations unused and the hundred and forty on the end of the back bench has not moved in nine years and nobody has ever been struck off one of the twenty-nine.** A man of about thirty-one of the ninth generation puts it under the room before anybody else: **we are deciding about a winter that two hundred people are in a book for, and none of those two hundred is in this room in a seat, and if we vote the minute will say that we decided, and there is no box on this bench for the two hundred and there is no way of putting us in a room and asking us.** The second question is put nine times and answered four times and the clerk writes *no answer* five times. **The answer nobody can give is that the thing underneath has been held nine generations and there is no book about it that anybody has read, and the only document anybody has ever been sent is a two-hundred-year-old form about the number of men going out and it is not about a winter, and the eight columns are read out again in a cold room and used rather than rediscovered and the withdrawal column's rule has still not been ruled across.** The man of thirty-four's reason is the finding: **a body that has never decided anything cannot be asked to decide, and if you ask it, it will say yes because saying yes is what it has done in the four times it has been asked, and you will go out of the room with a minute with the word *yes* in it about a winter that not one of the nine of you could describe.** The vote is **eight for and one against, taken at the front of the room, and the eight said yes without one of them being able to say what happens if they had said no.** **No third asking of the ninth generation is staged. The Chapter 166 refusal is not repeated and not improved on. The Chapter 178 to 180 consent with nine against it is referred to once and is not re-asked.** A barrow goes out through the aisle on two wheels at the end of the second morning and the man who pushed it had not been asked.

466. **TORRIN HATCH, 55, OF THE NINTH GENERATION, THE LAST MAN IN THAT VALLEY WHO HAS EVER STOOD IN THE AISLE, AND THE NAME BUDGET IS ONE OF SIX AND FIVE SLOTS UNFILLED, SO VOLUME 04 STANDS AT FIVE NAMES OF SIX AND TWENTY-SEVEN OF TWENTY-FOUR UNFILLED.** Chapters 185, 186 and 187. **He is named once, on a bank, standing up, in about four seconds, because nobody asked him and he answered anyway: *Torrin Hatch. Fifty-five. Ninth generation. I stood in that aisle thirty-five years ago and I was asked what I swore and I have not told anybody what I said, and I am not going to tell you, and that is not a mystery, it is a thing a man of twenty does with a question like that.*** He stood in it at twenty and it was in the cold in front of the whole valley and there is a stroke cut into the end of the bench at the back of the right-hand row for every person who has ever stood in it. **His want, in his own words, and spent: that the promise be put down by somebody who is not going to be asked to pick it up.** His reasoning is the last man of the ninth generation's reasoning: the oldest person in the room is eighty-one and he is the second, there is nobody under fifty-five who can be asked, and he has been told since he was twenty-five that the promise is not his to hold and has agreed every time, and **a thing which is nobody's to hold has been going for a hundred and forty years.** His opinion is that the thing underneath does not care who is standing in the aisle, and that the aisle is for knowing somebody in the valley stood up in a cold week and said the words out loud, and **he does not believe a thing that does not ask is a thing anybody can rely on and he has never been able to give a reason and has stopped trying.** **He is right about the history and wrong about the soil, and no character in this block calls him a mirror and no character calls him a villain, and he is not called anything at all: he voted against keeping the winter, the clerk entered *against, no reason given, a reason having been given* and read it back twice, he came to the room over the cross four more times in nine years, he did not stand in the aisle at any point, he said no more about the vote, and that is all that is known about him and it is all he wanted.** Nev Treen of the eighth generation answers him and does not blame him: **the aisle does not need an old man, the men who went into it were between twenty and thirty and the winter was kept every one of those times, and a man of fifty-five wanting the promise put down is wanting to put down a rope nobody is holding, and she will stand in that aisle at sixty and be asked what she swore and the ninth generation will watch and in nine years one of the tenth will be in it and none of the nine of them will have to be in it twice**, and the clerk wrote that in and nobody argued with it.

467. **THE SENTENCE ABOUT A SUBSCRIPTION IS IN THE MINUTE AGAIN, WORD FOR WORD, AND IS NOT IMPROVED ON, AND THE VALLEY HAS NEVER HEARD IT BEFORE AND DOES NOT KNOW IT IS A QUOTATION, AND A VALLEY CLERK'S MINUTE IS A DOCUMENT NOBODY CAN BE SERVED, SO THE QUOTING IS SAFE AND THE RECORD IS THE ONLY RECORD THERE IS.** Chapter 187. *A bench that is generous decides. A bench that is asked is being told what it is for. And a bench that is asked three times and says yes three times is not a bench, it is a subscription.* Said by Torrin Hatch about forty seconds into the second morning, in the middle of an argument about the aisle and the number a hundred and forty and what a bench is, and he had it ready and nobody in the room knew he had it. **The clerk of about sixty, who has kept the minute for twenty-two years and is not a member of the council and has never been asked to be, wrote it out as it came in about a minute and a half and did not ask who had said it before and did not ask where a man of fifty-five in a valley nine miles long with no writ and no bell and no office had had it, and four people noticed that he had not asked and nine did not.** **Iven Sarr is the only person who speaks about it and his sentence is that he has been the only person in this valley who wanted to know anything for nineteen years and has worked out this morning that what he is actually for is stopping people asking each other and putting it in a minute, and that in nine years a woman who is not in that room is going to read the sentence and believe it was invented here, and she will be right, and that is what a sentence is for.** **No character in this batch notices that this resembles anything, and no character may ever say where the sentence came from, and the thread is opened and held and not closed.**

468. **A BENCH OF NINE IS ASKED A SIXTH THING, TO FUND A ROAD TO A VALLEY FOUR HUNDRED MILES OFF THAT DOES NOT GO INTO THE VALLEY AND DOES NOT SPEND A PENNY IN IT AND DOES NOT ASK ANYBODY IN IT, AND IT SAYS NO, AND THE NO IS CORRECT, AND THE REASON IS ELEVEN WORDS LONG.** Chapter 188, the fourth of Harvestmonth, YR 314, a Saturday and a market day. **This is not the fifth asking and the two are not run together and no character says they are the same. The fifth asking is in the minute already with its answer; the number of times this bench has been asked the same thing is five and the number of yeses is four, and both figures are on a page under a stair in that hall, and the clerk enters this as the sixth, and the man who read the second out loud said so himself before anybody else could.** The asker is a carrier of about fifty with a waggon of his own and a rate on about a hundred and forty miles of haulage in four counties, who has been to the valley and who tells the room what he saw for about eleven minutes. **The reason the bench gives is *there are two marks in the chest and the ask is forty*, and nobody argues with it for about nine seconds and those nine seconds were the shortest of the sitting.** The carrier says *that is correct* and asks for the reason to be entered twice, **because a bench that says no for money has refused a thing it could not afford and a bench that says no for anything else has refused a thing it does not want, and this county has never in nine years got the first.** The reeve of Merefen, who does not vote on the guild's own matter and has not for nine years, gives the reason the no is the *right* no, and the load-bearing sentence is that **a road that is not to be made to carry a person does not get built in a county where nobody has asked for it, and this one has not got a person at the end of it to be carried, and there is nobody at the far end of that pass to be hurt if we do not and nobody to be helped if we do**, and she has said the word *and* in that sentence twice and the second one is the argument and the first one is habit. **A magistrate of thirty asks *then what is the road for* before she votes and not after, and the answer she gives herself is that carefulness is not the same thing as there being a reason, and that if this bench funds it then in nine years somebody from this county will go down that road, not to carry anything, because a road is a thing people go down, and this county has no office that will be told about it and no minute it will be put in and no way of stopping it**, and she asks for that reason in the minute. **The asker says a man who makes nails asked him, and the clerk enters it.** The figure is footed on the page before the total is said: *six men, thirty-one days, at fourpence the day: 4 six times over is 24, 24 thirty-one times over is 744. Two hundred feet of plank at three pence the foot: 3 two hundred times over is 600. Forty pounds of powder at three pence the pound: 3 forty times over is 120. A mason, four days, at a shilling the day: 12 four times over is 48. Cartage, four loads each way at eighteen pence a load: 18 four times over is 72, 72 twice over is 144. A waggon and four horses and back at eleven shillings the turn: 132 twice over is 264. 744 and 600 is 1,344. 1,344 and 120 is 1,464. 1,464 and 48 is 1,512. 1,512 and 144 is 1,656. 1,656 and 264 is 1,920 pence, which is forty marks, and forty marks is exactly twenty years of four marks and six a year.* **The Marches' contract of 3,240 pence and the one fifth of 648 pence are not re-derived and not scaled, the fair copy's 4,632 pence is not restated, the county post of 134 pence is not cited, Chapter 10's column is not scaled out of, no 456, no 254, no 2,450, no 2,906 and no 9-4-1 is on the page, and no county figure is set beside a valley figure anywhere in Chapters 181 to 190.**

469. **THE DOCUMENT THAT DECIDES WHAT A BODY CORPORATE OWES FOR A HEARING IT ENTERED AGAINST NOBODY IS WRITTEN, IN SEVEN COLUMNS, IN FOUR SHEETS, ON THE SEVENTH AND EIGHTH OF HARVESTMONTH, YR 314, AND IT IS A DOCUMENT AND NOT A SCENE.** Chapters 189 and 190. **The seven columns are the county's form: *what is given. To whom, in the county's words. By whose hand. The day. The hour. A witness at this end. A witness at that end.*** **The day and the hour are two columns and go in as two things with the rule between them and are read back as two things, and the day-book entry is four entries and not three, and the reason is in the keeper's own mouth: a person in nine years who reads a day and an hour in one line cannot tell whether the office made it up or whether somebody was careless, and the fault will be hers and she would rather it be hers on a page.** The second column carries the clause ***and to no person***, which is nine words and is the load-bearing clause of the sheet, and the fourth way of answering that column is the one this office has used for four years and a half. **The claim number is the number of the account and nothing is entered against a person.** **The seventh column, a witness at that end, is empty, and the reason is written under the rule, and the empty column is the finding: *a column which asks for a name and is given nothing is not a hole in a document, and it is the finding of this sheet.*** The delegation is still not sent for. The hearing was not adjourned and not refused. **The resolution of the twentieth of Hearthmonth, YR 313, is on the table, nineteen lines, never signed by anybody, and its eleventh line says a keeper of records is a keeper of records and is not a person appointed by any council to answer for any person, and the keeper of records wrote it herself at twenty-seven on a bench in a guild hall four hundred miles off and read it out twice and said so.** The first column says what it is now: **a room with a keeper in it at the second hour and nothing at the other side of the table, and that is entered as a fact about this office and not as a finding against anybody, and a body corporate that has agreed eighteen months ago to hear a thing cannot un-agree and can only decide what it is now.**

470. **THE MEANING IS WRITTEN IN A DOCUMENT, UNATTRIBUTED, AND A MEANING IN A MINUTE IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT FROM A MEANING ON A STAGE.** Chapter 189. **Her own rule from Chapter 170 is that what a thing means is not a fact and this office is for facts, and she is made to write a meaning anyway, and the reason she can is that there is nobody in the finding to be a claim about, and she says out loud that that is a coincidence of the calendar and not a good reason.** The second copyist gives the finding: **a meaning on a stage can be argued with, and you can stand up in a room and say *that is not what I took you to mean* and about nine people will agree with one of you and it will be a different meaning by the fourth hour; a meaning in a minute cannot be argued with, it can only be read, and once it is read it is the same for everybody who reads it, and about nine years from now there will be a woman in this room who has not met you and she will read it and have an opinion about it and not be able to give it to anybody, because there is nobody in it to give it to.** **The meaning is entered without a name against it, and the reason is the standing rule of the office and it is nineteen years old, and the day a person is put into one of these things the meaning comes out of it for good.** The deed of the office is thirteen words, *for the keeping of what this county cannot be shown it has lost*, and it has been read about four hundred times and has never had to be worked out until this morning, and **it is that**, and a deed of thirteen words is the reason this office could hold a meaning and a county council four hundred miles off could not hold a road.

471. **THE VOLUME SAYS IN A DOCUMENT WHAT IT COST, AND IT IS TWELVE PENCE AND ONE HOUR OF A KEEPER'S TIME THAT CANNOT BE ENTERED AND A FOURTH LINE ABOUT A PERSON WHO CANNOT BE NAMED, AND THAT IS WHERE THE INTIMACY IS AND IT IS BOUGHT WITH AN ACCOUNTING AND NOT WITH A CURE.** Chapter 190. *Of the second copyist, one hour, at the county's rate of eight pence the hour:* **eight pence**. *Of paper, two sheets, at twopence the sheet:* 2, twice over, is **four pence**. *Of the room, one hour:* **nothing**, the office paying fourpence a year for the room under a lease in a tradesman's hand, and there being no rate in this county for the use of a room for one hour by its own keeper, **a rate for a room being a figure of a thing and a rate for a keeper's hour being a figure of a person, and no combined figure being entered in this office**. *Of the keeper of this office, one hour:* **nothing**, this office having never entered a figure of the keeper's own time and not going to start. **Eight and four is twelve pence, which is twelve pence.** And the sentence: **a body corporate that can be sued can afford twelve pence sixteen times a year and cannot afford it once if anybody comes**, which goes in the finding and not in the cost, **because a document that says what a thing is worth is a different object from a document that says what it is.** The fourth line of the third sheet, in no column, against no person: **a body corporate that cannot say what a thing cost has no standing to be asked what it cost by anybody else, and this office has a claim number and not a name, and the name is not going in, and so the cost falls on the only person this office can name and cannot put in a column, and she is going to be thirty-eight in about nine years, and by then there will be a second keeper in this room and neither of them will know who decided any of it, and the second keeper will be told it all in about four minutes in a hand she has not seen before.** **No apology in any form in a scene, an aside or a document, no tenth not-asking, no mistake made available to anybody, and neither of them says they have been wrong.** The second copyist's want, a post with her name in the day-book, is spoken once and is not met: **a finding goes on a shelf with a number against this office and a name goes in a head of a book, and those are two different objects, and if a second copyist's name goes in the head of the day-book then whoever holds it in nine years is holding it for her and not for the office.** And the deed of thirteen words is said out loud in a room of two and is **not written down**, and goes in a book of things said in a room that is not the day-book and is not in the press and weighs nothing.

472. **THE TWO CLAIMS IN FOUR YEARS AND A HALF THAT WERE AGAINST NOBODY ARE NAMED IN THE SAME DOCUMENT, AND THE FINDING IS THAT THE TWO THAT ARE NOT DOCUMENTS ARE THE TWO THAT ARE STILL LIVE, AND HEARING ABOUT IT LESS IS NOT THE SAME AS IT BEING LESS.** Chapter 189. One is a return a Crown office wanted from a district that cannot be counted, answered in a woman's hand with no seal on it, **two thousand six hundred and forty**, and there is no way on this earth to check it and the office has never been told the district cannot be counted, and the count is not re-derived in this block and is not restated. The other is a strip of cut paper in the press that weighs a shade over ten ounces and is the account of nobody, and it came back cut along the left edge with a knife, four hundred and eleven words, and the cut is the office's own method, and the clause that landed is the number of persons the offer was made out to, which is not on the sheet, and the Archive has asked for that number in a return with no name in it and it has not come. **The two are four hundred miles apart and neither of the people who put them there has ever heard of the other one, and a bundle of nine letters from that one county is on a second shelf with a piece of tarred hemp through it, because this office answers everything that is not a question and there is no instrument in this kingdom that can make a county answer a question that is not one.** **The bare two inches at the right-hand edge of the list of things sent are not filled and are not ruled in, and the list has no fifth column, and the second copyist has still not been given a post with her name in the day-book.**

473. **STAGE 3 IS NOT REACHED, NOT ATTEMPTED, NOT OFFERED AS A PLAN, NOT PRICED AND NOT DESCRIBED AS AVAILABLE IN THIS BLOCK, AND NO LINEAGE IS READ AND THE WORKING IS NOT NAMED AND THE CUT IS NOT NAMED.** **The `cut` string occurs thirty-one times in Chapters 181 to 190 and every one of them is ordinary**: a number and a hundred and forty cut into the ends of benches, a stranger's mark cut into a coping, a course cut off a bed, stone and a course cut to fit, a figure cut into a stone, a strip of cut paper, and a sheet cut along an edge with a knife. **The working is not among them and is not named and no character puts the consent and a cut together and nobody describes what anybody is going to do in terms a reader could repeat, and no cut's consequence is foreshadowed and none is scheduled.** No bodily cost is added: the limp stands as Volume 03 left it, in the right leg, and the stick is four hundred miles for four hundred yards and is now against a wall in the room over the cross, **and that is a fact and not a cost and it is not said as a discovery.** No melody cost is added and the word does not appear. The Many-Handed stage's worsening belongs to Volume 15. The three-weeks warning is unchanged and no character in this block uses the word *failed* about a road and no character describes the warning as having failed. **He is still not writing a drift figure and the two unreconciled numbers are untouched, and the third thing on that page is not a figure either: there is a date in a county four hundred miles off that nothing he is carrying has a road to, and he is not going to write it on a page in a valley that keeps no months, because the day he does the book is two books.** The mechanism was said once in Chapter 164 and is not restated. The counterweight of Chapter 177 is not restated. The refusal of Chapter 166 is not repeated and not improved on. The not-askings stand at nine and this batch enters no tenth and puts no number on the page. **The three things the two-hundred-year-old form opens — who put it there and when, who took four columns out of the middle of the book, and whether the two hands on it have anything to do with the hand in the ninth spread — are not answered in this block and are not scheduled, and the form is used in Chapter 186 as the only thing anybody from anywhere has ever sent this valley and is not about a winter.** The tile on the coping is not mentioned. The three marks on the seed vault are not mentioned and the keeper's decision is not taken. The letter for a jar is not answered. The five blanks of Volume 02 are not joined.

474. **THE FIGURES, THE DEVICES, THE CALENDAR AND THE LENGTH FOR THE BATCH, CHECKED ON THE PAGE.** **34,020 words**, per chapter **3334 / 3233 / 3134 / 3513 / 3591 / 3534 / 3433 / 3471 / 3633 / 3144**. **The ten columns foot at 34,020, Volume 04 is 100,467 + 34,020 = 134,487 in forty chapters, and the manuscript is 702,109 + 34,020 = 736,129 words in one hundred and ninety chapters.** No chapter is under 3,094; **the block is over Batch 0002's 33,385 and over Batch 0011's 31,648 and seventeen words under Batch 0003's 34,037, and the two shortest are Chapter 183, which carries the taking down, and Chapter 190, which carries the volume's best main-world document, and neither is padded and no scene was cut to move a figure.** **Eighteen `---` rules, one per chapter and a second in eight of them. Sixty bolded line-openings. Zero semicolons. Zero em-dashes. Zero straight double quotes. Zero curly apostrophes. `the whole of` 3, against Batch 0003's 3, and the first pass of this block carried it at 24 and the writer went back through all ten chapters and cut it out of twenty-one places. `about N seconds` 10, against Batch 0003's 0, one per chapter. `cut` 31 and all thirty-one ordinary. `about` 391, per chapter 39 / 44 / 40 / 43 / 45 / 42 / 41 / 38 / 36 / 23, and no chapter is over forty-five and the density does not compound. No System panel and no Gatehouse-voice line.** Filler counts as whole words, carried forward as a **baseline and not a target**, so that `stood` at 34 is not `understood` at a higher number: **`nodded` 0, `held` 4, `wrote` 27, `stood` 34, `plain` 0, `counted` 24, `breathed` 0, `steady` 0**, against Batch 0001's 0 / 11 / 37 / 13 / 2 / 8 / 0 / 0, Batch 0002's 1 / 10 / 27 / 30 / 0 / 8 / 0 / 0 and Batch 0003's 0 / 8 / 28 / 36 / 0 / 10 / 0 / 0. **`counted` is up at 24 and it is the block's word, and that is recorded rather than hidden.** **The calendar: Chapters 181 to 187 are path time and carry no main-world month, no real-world month and no main-world weekday in any register including a notebook, and the block's own clock is the ninth day of the fourth cold to about the ninth week of it, in the fourth and fifth winters of the sixteen, so the fourth winter is the twelfth generation and the fifth is the thirteenth.** The main-world section is Chapters 188 to 190 on the fourth, seventh and eighth of Harvestmonth, YR 314, a Saturday, a Tuesday and a Wednesday, and the return is the twentieth of Harvestmonth, YR 314, a Monday, and is not in this block.

475. **TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN THIS BLOCK'S OWN TEXT AND REPAIRED WHILE IT WAS BEING WRITTEN, AND BOTH ARE THE PROJECT'S STANDING DEFECT.** **One:** the first pass of Chapter 183 carried *about four hundred people* for the crowd at the coping, and the true figure is about forty, and the notice in Chapter 181 and the crowd in Chapter 183 are now the same figure. **Two:** a first pass of Chapter 188 and 189 put a ninth of Harvestmonth and a Saturday on the bench and a seventh and a Tuesday on the document, and `outline/volume-04.md` §17's chain gives Harvestmonth 1 as a Wednesday, and the fourth is a Saturday and the seventh is a Tuesday and the eighth is a Wednesday, and the three dates on the page are those and a sixth was dropped because a bundle of nine letters is not a date. **That is the tenth time in this project that carrying a figure instead of counting it has produced a date, and the rule does not change: a later phase states a figure, checks it, and records the check, and a state file is the least reliable document in this repository.** A third was found and not repaired and is recorded here: **Batch 0003's per-chapter `about` column, printed as 42 / 33 / 35 / 43 / 37 / 39 / 37 / 43 / 41 / 44 for 394, does not match the page, which reads 43 / 33 / 35 / 45 / 36 / 39 / 34 / 45 / 39 / 42 for 391, and both the prose of the entries and the items that quote the column are wrong in three chapters and the true total is three lower.** It is annotated here and not renumbered and not edited into the Batch 0003 entry, because a defect that is recorded is a fact about the book and a defect that is inherited silently becomes a canon with a footnote.

476. **NO THREAD INHERITED IS CLOSED AND NONE IS ANSWERED, AND OF THE FIVE THIS BATCH OPENED IT CLOSES ONE INSIDE ITSELF AND NONE OF THE OTHERS.** The nineteen the Volume 03 close handed over, the nineteen Batch 0001 carried forward, the nineteen Batch 0002 carried forward and the nineteen Batch 0003 carried forward all stand. **The thread of the return stitch is answered inside itself and closed in the only way the volume permits: the stitch is destroyed properly, in public, in daylight, with an explanation given before the work starts, by a bridgekeeper, to a whole course and not to the mark, and the mark is under four feet of water at a ford, and the place is a bridge parapet in a valley and a valley took it down, and no road is built and no way out is offered and the stranding is nine weeks and is not resolved.** The four inherited threads of Batch 0003 stand: the form is **used and not closed**, the four columns taken out of the middle of it are not accounted for, the two hands and the hand in the ninth spread are not put in a room, the two accounts of where a word came from are not joined, and the nine that is three households is referred to once and is not converted and nobody is named. **The five this batch opened: one,** a stranger's mark in the coping of the Sedge Reach in the main world, four hundred miles off, the same mark, untouched, and not the way out. **Two,** where the nine stones of the old coping go when the ford moves a foot a year, which the man of thirty-four has known for nine years and has never once said in a room. **Three,** a man of fifty-five and a sentence he cannot account for, and a clerk who did not ask, and nobody in nine years is going to know. **Four,** two figures of the ninth generation that do not agree with each other and are both going to be there in nine years. **Five,** a hand in a valise in a hall over a wharf about a barrow, which is a man in the valley who did not want to be looked at past the top of a bank and did not want to be first out of a valley he can now leave. **None of the five is closed.**

477. **THE `nine` TIC WAS THE ONE DRIFT IN THE VOLUME COMPOUNDING FASTEST AND IT WAS UNTRACKED, AND IT IS NOW TRACKED WITH A CEILING, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THE REVIEW RAISED THAT MATTERS MOST BECAUSE OF ITS SECOND HALF.** Measured as the standalone word, `nine` ran **2.87 per 1,000 words in Batch 0001, 4.58 in 0002, 7.31 in 0003 and 11.11 in 0004 as first written**, compounding by half again every block, and the residue was not the motif but interchangeable stock phrases wearing the same word. **The motif is canon and is untouched by the repair and may not be cut: nine stones in the course taken off at the Low Holm, nine hundred doors and nine hundred gates, nine generations and the ninth spread, a hundred and forty, the ninth of a month, the ninth hour, the ninth day, the bench of nine, the nine of the ninth generation, the nine that are three households, nine printed words at the foot of a two-hundred-year-old form, and a girl of nine who counts things.** The residue was `about nine + noun`, `in nine years` and `nine words`. **After the repair: the standalone word is 184 in 34,011 words, 5.40 per 1,000, per chapter 15 / 16 / 19 / 18 / 25 / 28 / 24 / 23 / 5 / 11, down from 371 and 11.11, and the volume's five-block rate reads 2.87 / 4.58 / 7.31 / 11.11 / 5.40, which is the first reversal in the volume. `about nine + noun` is 8 against 79, `in nine years` is 18 against 52, `nine words` is 2 against 11, and `about N seconds` is 1 against 10.** **The method of the repair is the rule and not a list of cuts: no fact was deleted, every fact was made exact.** *About nine minutes* became *about half an hour*; *in about nine days* became *in eleven days*, because eleven days was already canon for the same walk at nine hundred doors; *nine did not* became *as many again did not*; *in about nine years there will be a story on that coping* became *before this cold is out there will be a story on that coping*; *in about nine years somebody is going to tell a child* became *in nine years*, the refrain kept where it carries the argument and cut where it was decoration; *a girl of about nine* became *the girl* once her age had been given in Chapter 181; *nine minutes* for a count that is nine hundred and fifty-one became *about ten minutes*; *about nine words long* became *one sentence long* or *was short*; *the number has not moved in nine years* became *in the whole time the man of fifty-eight can remember*; *the four counties are four hundred miles off* kept its geography and *in the four counties the stone is four hundred miles off* was left alone. **A hedge made out of the motif number was the tell, and a number in this manuscript is a commitment.** Two garbled doublings of the same figure were found in passing and are repaired: **Chapters 184 and 185 both read *nine roofs nine steadings up the bank*, and Chapter 184's own closing paragraph gives the valley eleven steadings, so the phrase is now *nine roofs up the bank*.** The `nine` ceiling is now a hard instruction in the Batch 0005 prompt: **`about nine + noun` not over four in a chapter and `in nine years` not over three, and the substitute vocabulary is *about forty, about eleven, about a third, half, most, more than, as many again, in a few years, since the second day of this cold.***

478. **TWO META-LINES INSIDE THE FICTION ARE GONE AND A THIRD BORDERLINE IS GONE, AND FOUR BROKEN BOLD SPANS AND ONE STRAY RULE ARE REPAIRED.** **Chapter 187 read *it is the only thing in this chapter that was said by anybody who was not asked*, and Chapter 188 read *who was not in this hall and who is not in this chapter*, and both pointed at the manuscript. Chapter 187 now reads *it is the only thing said in that room that day by anybody who was not asked*, and Chapter 188 now reads *who was not in that hall, and nothing said in that hall has his name in it*, which is the same fact in the room's own terms and is better, because the absence of Aren Kest from the bench scene was the point and a reference to a chapter was not.** Chapter 182's borderline *the page is the only place in this book where a thing like that is allowed to happen* is now *a page is the only place a thing like that is allowed to happen*, which removes the ambiguity without touching the notebook, which is diegetic. **The stray rule was Chapter 189's literal `**---**` on a line of its own, which rendered as bold dashes; every other chapter uses a bare `---` and it is now bare.** The broken spans were Chapter 187 line 31 closing on `****` around a nested `**`, Chapter 188 line 31 with three stars in one line so that the load-bearing clause of the carrier's ask rendered plain, and unclosed `**` at Chapter 188 line 71 and Chapter 190 line 63, plus a pre-existing unclosed `**` at **Chapter 180 line 41** that had been in the manuscript since Batch 0003 and was not in this block. All five are closed and a per-line parity check across Chapters 180 to 190 now returns clean. **A sixth was found in passing and not reported: Chapter 186 line 33 carried the same nested `**` pattern as Chapter 187 and balanced, so it did not trip a parity check, but it rendered the centre of the man of thirty-one's speech plain, and it is now one clean span.** The block's rules go from eighteen to nineteen and the extra one is Chapter 189's corrected rule.

479. **A CHAPTER NO LONGER OPENS BY SUMMARISING ITSELF, AND THE INFORMATION IS ON THE PAGE TWICE INSTEAD OF THREE TIMES BEFORE A STONE MOVES.** Every chapter of Batch 0004 as first written opened on a bolded omniscient ledger paragraph that stated the chapter's own content before the scene began. In Chapter 181 that paragraph gave the mark, the valley, the nine weeks and the fact that nothing had been done, which Wystan Roole then said in nine sentences in the room over the cross and Chapter 183 then said a second time, and the taking down is the volume's best action and it had no room to arrive. **The bolded opening paragraph is the book's signature and it stays. What it may not do is deliver the chapter.** Three openings were cut back: **181** now sets the mark, the finder, the four hundred people, the nine weeks of inaction and the fact that a man is going to stand at the front of a room and say what he did and what he did not do, and the argument is the room's; **188** no longer gives away its own verdict and its own eleven-word reason before the carrier opens his mouth, and ends on the asking; **190** no longer prints the total of twelve pence before the arithmetic that foots it. **The second delivery inside the block is legitimate and stays, because *he said the nine sentences again* earns its place by adding the taking down, and the prompt now forbids only the opening paragraph being the first of three.** This is now item 15 of the Batch 0005 prompt.

480. **THE KEEPER OF RECORDS IS TWENTY-NINE AND NOT GOING TO BE FORTY IN ABOUT NINE YEARS, AND SHE IS GOING TO BE THIRTY-EIGHT, AND THE FIGURE WAS WRONG IN ELEVEN PLACES AND ALL ELEVEN ARE CORRECTED.** **Chapter 189 gives the keeper of records as twenty-nine. 485. **THE SCAR IS A HOLE IN A BANK AT THE FORD WITH A COURSE ACROSS THE TOP OF IT AT THREE FEET, AND IT IS STILL A HOLE IN THE ELEVEN WEEKS AND IT IS FILLED BY THE SAME COMMUNITY IN A WARM WEEK BEFORE THE WINTER CAME DOWN, AND HE IS LET INTO IT BECAUSE HE IS THE ONLY MAN IN NINE MILES WHO CAN SAY WHETHER A BANK IS SQUARE.** Chapters 193, 194, 195 and 196. **On the second evening of the third day a man of thirty-four stopped the digging and said in about eleven sentences that a face cannot be filled in a cold, because the ground under a fill is frozen and cannot be keyed, and in the warm week the ground lets go of what is on it and the fill goes into itself, and if a barrow run goes over the top of a fill that is going to do that then the barrow run has got a hole in it at the ford, and the ford is where about four hundred people get everything they have.** The course went across the top of it at three feet with two barrows of stone on it and the run went over the top of that, and the sixteen came back in the warm week and took the course up in about two hours and filled it with the ground keyed to it. **The reason he is let in is three sentences and it is a trade fact: *you can tell whether a bank is square, I cannot, I have got four men here who cannot and one of them is fifty-one and the other three are under thirty and have all been wrong in front of me this month*.** He said it four times a day, and the fourth time on the second morning he said nothing at all, and the man of thirty-four waited, and he said it was square and it would not stay square and that he had no instrument for that. 486. **HE STOPS COUNTING, IN PUBLIC, IN A YARD, IN THE WARM WEEK, AND THE REASON HE GIVES IS A MAN OF THIRTY-FOUR TOLD HIM ONCE THAT ABOUT THIRTY MEN UNDER A CROSS ARE NOT GOING TO LEARN A FIGURE THEY CANNOT CHECK.** Chapter 195. **The word is *load points* and it is his and not the valley's.
