487. **THE WINTER COMES DOWN OVER ELEVEN WEEKS AND THE GROUND COMES DOWN WITH IT, AND NOBODY IN THE VOLUME CALLS ANY OF IT A RESCUE, AND THE MAN OF FIFTY-EIGHT REFUSES TO ENTER THE ELEVEN WEEKS.** Chapter 196. **The warm week was nine days and after it there was no cold in that valley for the first time in nine generations, and a week of this valley is a thing a person standing up in a cold room says a week is, and there is no authority in that valley that could be asked, and the man of fifty-eight said in four words that a week is a week of this cold and entered no figure of weeks in the book and said why in nine sentences: the day there is an authority that could be asked is the day somebody in that valley can be made to answer for what happened in the eleven weeks, and he would like to know what he is going to say then before he puts a number against it.** The cost, on the page: **the four hundred yards of made ground that was the best ground anybody in that valley had seen went to a slope in nine days; the ninth stone of the new coping at the Low Holm came off on its own on the fourth day of the third week and is on the bank and the barrow run goes round it; six byres came down in the fifth week, one of them the byre the best wall in the valley was holding up; four of the nine roofs that had been open since the summer came in in the sixth week and a fifth is a roof on a house that is not there; the mill went on the low side in the seventh week, the wheel having been off since the fourth week of the fourth cold; the ford moved twice in the eighth week, a foot each time, and has not moved since, and about four people who have a barrow have noticed and none of them has said it in a room; and about nine bushels of seed went into the aisle of the room over the cross in the eighth week, and the aisle is four feet wide and has had no person in it for three generations, and the clerk of about sixty entered it in the minute on the man of fifty-eight's instruction and it is the first entry he has made in twenty-two years that was not said out loud in a room in front of him.** A man of about sixty-one who could not leave his mill was asked by four people in one day whether he was going, said he had not decided, and decided on the ninth day, and gave the reason in about nine words and the reason was the race.

488. **THE NINTH GENERATION IS ASKED ONE MORE TIME AND THE ASKING IS NOT REFUSED AND THE ANSWER IS FOUR WORDS LONG AND IT IS ENTERED AS A FACT AND NOT AS A DEFEAT AND NOT AS A PLEDGE: *We said yes once.*** Chapter 196. **The question was put by the man of thirty-four in about four minutes after he had had it ready for nine weeks: *we are not asking you to keep it, there is nothing left to keep, I am asking you one thing and it is the only thing I have got, I am asking you what it was.*** A man of thirty-one of the ninth generation said, *ask it as a question and not as a thing with a person in it*, and the man of thirty-four said it was a question and that he had not worked out how to make it one. The man of fifty-eight had it written **in the middle of the page and not at the end and not in the day column, because it is not a figure of people and it is not a figure of days and it is not money, and there is no column in that book for a thing that is a fact and not a count and he is not ruling one at eight in the morning on the ninth week of the eleventh.** The clerk read it back twice. A man of fifty-five said it was the only true sentence anybody had said in that room in two years and that he was not going to say another word about it and that he had not stood in the aisle and was not going to. **The consent of Chapters 178 to 180 is not re-asked anywhere in this block, the first asking of Chapter 166 is not repeated, and no character puts the consent and a cut together anywhere in Chapters 191 to 200.**

489. **THE STITCH IS GONE AND THE RETURN IS MADE THROUGH ANOTHER LIVING ANCHOR, AND IT COMES UP IN THE THIRD COURSE FROM THE LOW END OF THE FOURTH BAY OF THE SEDGE REACH, AND THE WITNESS AT THAT END IS A MAN OF FORTY-SEVEN ON THE ROLL WITH A VOTE AND NOT AN OFFICE, AND THE SEAM IS UNDER HIS HAND.** **[ANNOTATED AT ITEM 498: the witness is Bram Ottery and he is on the bench of nine because he was elected, and the phrase *on the roll with a vote and not an office* in this item is the Batch 0005 first pass's error and is not canon.]** Chapter 199. **The main-world return is the twentieth of Harvestmonth, YR 314, a Monday, not a market day, the fourth hour. He comes up out of the joint between the third and the fourth course, and he comes up the way a man comes up out of a river, and his hand is on the stone before the rest of him is out of it, and he puts his hand flat on the stone on either side of the line and the stone is the same temperature on both sides and he takes his hand off, and he looks at it once, and he does not put a rule on it.** The witness is not the person keeping the reach, which is kept by the bench of nine, and he has a vote in it and has not used it since he was elected. **The mark he cut in the coping of the first bay in June is four yards behind him and is the same mark cut with the same chisel, and nobody in that county can read the figure in it from thirty feet and a mason's mark can be read from thirty feet, and it is not a mason's mark, and a girl in that town put her hand flat on it in the summer to see whether it was warm and it was not and she has not asked anybody about it.** Neither the mark nor the seam is touched, measured, ruled across, or explained, and nothing in the volume says what either of them is.

490. **THE SEAM IS A LINE OF ABOUT NINE INCHES IN A STONE COURSE IN A BRIDGE IN MEREFEN, IT DOES NOT MOVE, IT IS THE FIRST THING IN TWO HUNDRED CHAPTERS THAT A STRANGER CAN SEE AND NOT EXPLAIN, AND IT WAS FOUND BY A CARTER OF THIRTY ON THE FOURTEENTH OF HARVESTMONTH, YR 314, A TUESDAY, AND WAS POINTED OVER ON THE TWENTY-THIRD AT THE JOINT AND NOT AT THE STONE.** Chapters 198, 199 and 200. **A line in the third course from the low end of the fourth bay, nine inches, in the stone and not across the joint and not in the joint, not got at with a nail or a cold chisel, and it did not move when two men put their thumbs on the two ends of it and pushed.** A carter of thirty told four men and not the yard. **[ANNOTATED AT ITEMS 498 AND 499: the man of forty-seven is Bram Ottery, elected to the bench of nine and not on a trade, and is the witness at this end; and the sentence about a decline and a survey and a form is the guild's man with the levels' own, said in Chapter 150, and the first pass of this block put it in the wrong mouth and also re-worded it.]** A man of forty-seven on the bench of nine because he was elected would not have it measured, and a man of about sixty who is the guild's man with the levels and has kept his own book for two years and been paid sixpence twice out of a box would not put his rule down, and his sentence is the reason: *a thing that has been measured once gets measured again in a year, and the second one is a decline, and a decline is a survey, and a survey goes in a form*, and he said he had told that to one man in his life and the man was not in that yard and was not going to be told by him twice.** The four men who were on the stone were asked separately and their four accounts do not agree; the mason of fifty and a half and the man of forty-seven agree that a course is not coming up on a boy's word and a man's memory. **The course was not taken up and the seam was not measured, not pointed, not cut out and not filled, and it is under about half an inch of lime, and it has not moved and has not grown and has not closed.** The protagonist looks at it once on the Monday he comes up and does not measure it, and is offered a rule on the Thursday by the mason and says no. **The volume does not explain it and no character links it to the valley and nobody in either county has put a figure against it.**

491. **THE FOURTH ROUTE IS REFUSED IN WRITING, IN A DOCUMENT OF FOUR SHEETS, DATED, WITH THE HOUR AS A SECOND THING AND NOT MERGED, AND IT IS THE SECOND REFUSAL IN A DOCUMENT IN TWO VOLUMES AND NEITHER PARTY KNOWS THE OTHER EXISTS.** Chapter 199, and the offer it refuses. **The offer is a sheet of good paper about the size of a broadside that came in the ordinary post with nine other things from a county four hundred miles off, and this office has nine such things on a second shelf with a piece of tarred hemp through it and has never opened one and has never written to a person in that county, and the second copyist refused to open the tenth and said that the day she opens the eleventh is the day the office is a body corporate that goes through a county's post.** The keeper of records opened it. **The terms: a hand, being a road warden with a vote and not an office, a room, a house, an allowance of four shillings the week, and a clerk; that the eastern paths be closed by the man so appointed and by nobody else and for so long as he holds the appointment, and that no other office be given to him for the term; that the county of nine hundred and forty-one hearths be entered in the register of the office making the appointment by number and not by name and that the number be not given to the man so appointed; and that no question be asked of the man so appointed about the object of the appointment, in that county or in this one, at any time, by anybody.** **No part of the terms describes what the thing is and the volume does not describe it and no System panel does.** The refusal refuses the hand, refuses the closing, states that the number of persons the appointment was made out to is not on the sheet and has been asked for in a return and is not going to be supplied, and says there is no thanks in it. **The word eastern is in that document and in a bag on the ordinary post and in a copy on a shelf in a room over a weigh-house with a number against the office and nothing against a person, and the office that made the offer does not know that a body corporate in that county exists, and the keeper of records does not know who the offering party is, and the second copyist knows nothing about the other two documents in the same press.** The march is not a character in this block, the eastern paths are not closed by him, nobody is harmed by the refusal, and the refusal is correct.

492. **THE INTIMACY HAPPENS AND IT IS BOUGHT AND IT IS NOT A CURE, AND IT IS BOUGHT WITH A LEG, A SEAM AND ABOUT TWO HUNDRED PEOPLE, AND IT IS NOT AN APOLOGY, AND THE BREACH IS NOT REPAIRED IN A SCENE, AN ASIDE, A DOCUMENT OR AN APOLOGY, AND NEITHER OF THEM SAYS THEY HAVE BEEN WRONG, AND THE NOT ASKING STANDS AT NINE.** Chapter 199. **Mara Vey makes him say all three in a room of two on the fourth of the seven days of the fever, with the finding of the eighth of Harvestmonth and its third sheet on the table, and the fourth line of the third sheet is in no column and against no person, and the three are said in about nine minutes and none of the three is an apology and none was available.** He says the leg is the same leg and does not get up a bank any better. He says the seam is nine inches long and was not there in the spring and he has looked at it once and has not measured it and does not know what it is, and that he was told in a hall four years ago in nine seconds on a Friday what a figure turns into. He says the two hundred, in about four sentences, and that about two hundred are going to be somewhere else in a year, and that he asked none of them to be anywhere. **She says then it is not a cure and it is not a settlement and it is not the end of anything, and that she is going back to the room over the weigh-house at the eighth hour and will be there tomorrow and the day after, and that he will be on the reach in the morning because that is where his hands are, and that she is not going to walk up that road with him, and the reason is given in nine sentences and it is that a road warden with a vote and not an office who walks up four hundred yards with a keeper of records in front of a town of four thousand people is a thing this county will have an opinion about inside a week and the opinion will be about her.** **The third of the three rules on the wall of that room ends in a sentence about a habit that a place does to itself when nobody is looking and it is about him and she wrote it four months before the volume opened and he knows it is about him and neither of them has ever said so and neither of them said it in the nine minutes and it did not go into the finding and it is not put near a document in a way that states it.** The not askings in that day-book stand at nine and there was not going to be a tenth and there was not one. The second not asking, a man at a gate in a valley who will not say what a word means, was not turned into a mirror of the first and no character in this block noticed that the two resemble anything.

493. **THE FEVER IS A WEEK AND THE PRICE IS ON THE PAGE IN THREE PARTS, AND THE YARD HOLDS HIS TOOLS AND A MAN OF TWENTY-FIVE RUNS HIS ERRANDS AND TELLS HIS FAMILY WHERE HE IS, AND THE WORD IS NOT USED.** Chapter 199. **The fever took him on the night of the return and six days after it and broke on the seventh morning, and it is a week because the stage is a stage that takes a week, and nobody in that county knew that except him and a woman of twenty-nine in a room over a weigh-house and neither of them said so out loud.** A man of twenty-five who owns the crews and the yard on Weir Street, four hundred yards up a road, took two boxes out of the room over a cooper's on a barrow at about the seventh hour on the first day and put them on the bench-board and wrote nothing down, because the yard's rule is that nothing belonging to a man goes in that yard's book and only a thing set, and he carried them back down on the eighth day and said *your barrow is out of true and I have not looked at it because it is not mine to look at* and went up the road. **He told a woman of about seventy in Weir Street, the aunt, on the second day where his brother was, and did not say anything else, and she asked him on the fourth day what the place was called and he said it was called a valley and he did not know the name of it and had not asked.** The word is not used between the two of them anywhere in this block, the spent sentence from Volume 01 is not re-said, improved on or alluded to as retractable, no Volume 04 scene re-teaches him an ordinary morning, and the yard is off the page for the whole of the block except for these two pages, which is the block's cost and not a convenience.

494. **A CARRIER OF ABOUT FIFTY WITH A WAGGON OF HIS OWN CAME DOWN TWO FLIGHTS OF A STAIR ON THE FOURTH OF THE SEVEN DAYS AND TOLD THE BENCH, UNASKED, THAT THE MAN HE HAD DESCRIBED TO IT ON THE FOURTH OF HARVESTMONTH WAS IN THE TOWN, AND ON THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF FALLOWMONTH HE SAID IN THAT HALL THAT HE DID NOT GO UP THE PASS.** Chapters 199 and 200. **The six askings and four yeses of the bench of nine stand, and the fifth asking was brought up two flights on the last day of the year before by the reeve and not put, and that is in the minute in about eleven words in a clerk's hand read back twice. The sixth asking, a road to a valley nine days over a pass with forty marks footed in pence on a page, was refused in about a minute and a half in eleven words and the reason was entered twice and the reeve's reason for the no being the right no is in the minute.** The carrier's account of why he did not go up the pass is in about four sentences and it went in the minute: **a man of fifty with a waggon of his own goes up it to carry things and to be paid for carrying them, and the day he goes up it to ask is the day he has a reason to be listened to that has nothing to do with the asking.** The document road of paper that opened in the first year of the case is on a board under a stair four hundred miles from that valley and carries nobody, and the two ends of the whole arrangement are four hundred miles apart and neither of them is holding the other.

495. **THE VALLEY'S MEMORY OF HIM IS NOT A FOND ONE AND IT IS SAID OUT LOUD IN THE OPEN TO A CHILD ON THE NINTH DAY OF THE ROAD BY A MAN OF ABOUT TWENTY-EIGHT OF THE NINTH GENERATION, AND NOBODY CALLED HIM ANYTHING.** Chapter 197. *That is the man that took the winter out. And there are nine roofs open in this valley and there were nine roofs open before he came and there are nine roofs open now, and four of them came in in the eleven weeks, and the mill went, and the ground he made with sixteen of us went to a slope in nine days, and I am not saying a word against him and my roof is on and it is on because of the sixteen and I know that. And my daughter is nine and she will be told that a man came and the winter went, and she is not going to be told what it cost, because there is nowhere in nine miles to tell her, and in a generation there will be a woman in this valley who will say that the man came and the winter went and nothing else, and she will not be wrong, because the other half is not hers and it is not anybody's.* **A man of fifty-eight has said out loud in a room that a sentence in that valley about a man off a road is the second one in two years and that he does not know what to do with two of anything.** Torrin Hatch is not called a villain and is not called a mirror and is not called anything. About two hundred people in a valley of about four hundred have begun to leave, the first three households out are the three that said no, and the man of thirty-four put the man of nails off a barrow run for fifty-nine days for the opposite reason and did not tell him and said afterwards that the day he says it to him it is a thing he has put in him and not a thing he has done.

496. **NO MECHANISM IS EXPLAINED, NO TILE IS EXPLAINED, NO FORM'S QUESTION IS ANSWERED, NO WARNING IS CALLED FAILED, NO NAME IS WRITTEN IN A CROWN'S HAND, NO SECOND BODILY COST IS ADDED, AND THE `nine` CEILINGS ARE HELD.** Chapters 191 to 200, and the standing prohibitions, all verified in this block. **The three questions the two-hundred-year-old form opens — who put it there and when, who took four columns out of the middle of the book, and whether the two hands on it have anything to do with the hand in the third column of the ninth spread — are not answered and are not scheduled, and the form is not mentioned once in this block, and the four lines at the head of the first spread are used once and are not re-derived and are not improved on, and the eight columns, the Office of Quarters at Grayford, the two hands, the press-mark, the twenty-nine benches and the hundred and forty, the mechanism under the winter and the strain in it all stand exactly as Batch 0004 left them.** The printed warning is three weeks, in an office's hand, for two years, unchanged, and **no character in this block uses the word *failed* about a road and no character describes the warning as having failed.** The limp does not worsen and the Many-Handed stage's worsening belongs to Volume 15. The first-crossing loss of one verse's remembered pitch remains the only melody cost and the word does not appear. The stick is in the room over the cross, against the wall between the second bench and the third, and it is used to hold the door open at the fifth morning of the fourth day and is not carried on a job. The form under the byre, the third column's *four in this year*, the fifth column's *none appointed*, the seventh column's rule that has not been ruled across, the eighth column's rule no more faded than the third, and the nine printed words at the foot all stand. **The word *custodian* does not appear in Chapters 191 to 200 and no character calls a carrier one and no character calls one a carrier.** The marginal instruction is not in anybody's mouth. Sian Pugh's name is not spoken. Edric Hunn is not written anywhere and is not in a column and is not in a room. The Office of Provincial Registration and the Office of Quarters at Grayford are never joined in one sentence by anybody. *Culling Order* does not appear. *Gatehouse* does not appear. No 456, no 254, no 2,450, no 2,906 and no 9-4-1 in any form, and the two nines hundred and forty-ones are never printed in one line. The four thousand and the seven hundred and twenty are never added. The five blanks of Volume 02 are not joined. The eighth ruled line is not looked at. The brine weights are neither mentioned nor filed. **The bare two inches at the right-hand edge of a list of things sent are not filled and not ruled in and the blank ruled column in a bench's minute is not filled and not ruled in.** The three marks on the outside of a seed vault are not read and the keeper's decision is not taken. The letter for a jar is not answered and not delivered and no living holder of the other end is found. The road to the Marches' end of the line stays closed in writing and is not reopened. **The tile on the coping is mentioned once in this block, as an object, with its device not named and nothing scheduled and nothing explained. The bell with forty-one rivets went at the fourth hour and a half on the twenty-fifth of Fallowmonth, rung by a boy and a carpenter, and the arrangement is not anybody's and nothing in the sound of it belongs to anybody, and a Monday is the day the far end keeps and the two facts are in two books in two counties and are not joined in one sentence.** `outline/series.md`'s Volume 4 escalation line and knowledge-control row, which require the antagonist's name in older administration, **remain unsatisfied and are carried forward as an open item and no later phase may read Batch 0005 as having satisfied them.**

497. **STAGE 3 IS REACHED BY QUALIFICATION IN CHAPTERS 191 TO 195 AND BY NOTHING ELSE, AND THE COST IS A VISIBLE SEAM, A WEEK OF FEVER AND A REFUSAL, AND NOTHING ELSE.** Chapters 191 to 200. **`bible/power-system.md` gives Threadkeeper's qualification as one consensual cut made while a local bridgekeeper remains present, then help the same community repair the physical scar before the route is declared stable, and both halves are on the page and the second half is in Chapter 195 and not in Chapter 194.** Three paths are held at the close of the volume: Bellweather-Living, the Hearth Marches and the Ninefold Winter. **There is one System panel in the whole block and it is two plain lines at the end of Chapter 194 and it is not a list and it has no number in it: *The line is open. What is under it is not mended by the man who dug it.* He does not write it down, as he has not written down the other four.** The volume's one cut to the north was spent in Batch 0004 and this block's main-world section is the volume's second and last, in one bounded section of three chapters on the fourteenth, the twentieth and the twenty-fifth of Harvestmonth and Fallowmonth, YR 314. **The cut is consented to, is not made on a witness's word, and no consequence of it is scheduled, forecast with a date or priced anywhere in the block, and the Volume 06 row of the failure table is Volume 06's and is not foreshadowed as an event and the risk is still carried forward as the thing he said no to in Chapter 124 on a date and a community, unexplained.** The `cut` string occurs twenty-five times in Chapters 191 to 200 and every one of them is a number cut into the end of a bench, a mark cut into a coping, a line cut into a stone, stone cut to fit, a step nobody had cut, a course cut off a bed, a strip of cut paper and a sheet cut along an edge with a knife, and the working is not among the twenty-five and is not named.

## Relationship state at the end of Chapter 200

- **Aren Kest and Mara Vey: the breach open, and further along a road, and not walking it together.** The not askings stand at nine and no tenth was entered and none was available. No apology in any form, in a scene, an aside or a document, and no mistake made available to anybody, and neither of them has said they have been wrong. **On the fourth of the seven days of the fever she made him say three things out loud in a room of two — a leg, a seam, and about two hundred people who are going to be somewhere else in a year — and the saying took about nine minutes and was not an apology and the three of them are the price.** She said then it is not a cure and not a settlement and not the end of anything, and that she would be in the room over the weigh-house at the eighth hour and on the two mornings after, and that he would be on the reach because that is where his hands are, and **that she is not going to walk up that road with him, and the reason is nine sentences long and the whole of it is that the opinion of a town of four thousand people would be about her and she has four years and a half of a body corporate that answers to nobody and is not going to lose it to an opinion about a man with a limp.** **The third of the three rules on the wall of that room ends in a sentence about a habit a place does to itself when nobody is looking and it is about him and she wrote it and he knows it is about him and neither of them has ever said so and it did not go into the finding.** He gave her the numbers before she asked. He did not tell her that he cannot. **The two of them are further along a road than they were at the end of the ninth of Rainmonth and they are not walking it together and the volume does not pretend otherwise.** A document road of paper from a county four hundred miles off is on a board under a stair and carries nobody, and the reach is four hundred yards from that room and he is on it every working morning and the tide is at the wharf at the fourth hour.

- **Aren Kest and the Ninefold Winter valley: a lasting memory and it is not a fond one, and the leaving is the resolution and it is not a cure.** A man of about twenty-eight of the ninth generation said it out loud in the open to a child on the ninth day of the road and nobody called him anything. About two hundred of about four hundred people have begun to leave, and the first three households out are the three that said no, and the man of thirty-four had put the man of nails off a barrow run for fifty-nine days for the opposite reason and did not tell him. The four days are three with a bar through the four in chalk on a public bench. The second column of the ninth spread has eight names in eight hands and a ninth line that is not ruled across. A figure of money and a figure of people and a figure of days and a figure of eleven weeks, and no figure of what it cost. A barrow road of nine hundred yards with a turning place that has no name and a refusal, three times, in three yards, to have it attributed to anybody.

- **Aren Kest and Wystan Roole: the four days, and a man who would not explain what for, and a road.** He stood at his shoulder for four days with his hand on a rope and did not explain what for and was asked nothing and answered nothing, and four people asked him afterwards what the rope was for and got four sentences and not one of the four sentences was the reason. He refused attribution three times. He said the road was going to happen before he asked anybody for it and then said they were not building it that week. **He did not let him lay a stone in the valley and did not let him lay one in the repair, and the only thing he was given in the valley that was not carrying was the question of whether a bank is square, and it was given because there is no instrument in nine miles that can answer it.** He refused the first asking's form and said the asking was right. He put the ununanimity in a minute. He has not been thanked and asked for no thanks.

- **Aren Kest and Iven Sarr: a second column, a first distinction, and a ninth line.** A man of fifty-eight ruled a second column on the ninth spread, about the width of two fingers, in his own ink, and eight people wrote their own names into it and the ninth line is empty and he is not going to rule it across. He put three figures and a figure of money and three named accounts and the four words about a yes that happened on a day into a book that cannot be served, and refused to enter a figure of weeks because a week of that valley is a thing a person standing up in a cold room says a week is and the day there is an authority that could be asked is the day somebody can be made to answer for the eleven weeks. He said that a sentence about a man off a road in a valley is the second one in two years and that he does not know what to do with two of anything.

- **Aren Kest and Osgar Vell: not asked again and not answered again.** The ninth generation was asked one more time, in the ninth week of the eleven, and he was not among the four who were asked in a seat and he was in the room. What they said was four words long. The second asking is not re-asked anywhere in this block and the first asking of Chapter 166 is not repeated and no character puts the consent and a cut together.

- **Aren Kest and Torrin Hatch: one sentence on a turning place, and nothing asked of him.** A man of fifty-five said that the promise was nobody's to hold and that there is now nothing to hold and that he has not been asked to pick anything up and would like that in a minute, and there is no column for it. He did not stand in the aisle. The aisle over the cross has now gone three generations unused, the hundred and forty cut into the end of the back bench has not moved in the whole time the man of fifty-eight can remember, and nobody has ever been struck off one of the twenty-nine, and about nine bushels of barley are in the aisle and nobody stood in it.

- **Aren Kest and Tovan Kest: the tools, held, and the word not used.** A man of twenty-five carried two boxes up a barrow to a bench-board in a yard on Weir Street and wrote nothing down and left them seven days and carried them back down and said a barrow was out of true and he had not looked at it because it is not his to look at. He told a woman of about seventy where his brother was on the second day of a fever and did not say anything else and said it was called a valley and that he did not know the name of it and had not asked. **The word is not used in a room the two of them are in anywhere in this block, and it was not used in those two pages either, and the spent sentence is not re-said, and the yard is off the page for the rest of the block and that absence is a cost.**

- **Aren Kest and the form, the ninth spread and the two hands: untouched and unadvanced.** The form under the byre is not mentioned once in Chapters 191 to 200. The three questions it opens are not answered and are not scheduled. The four lines at the head of the first spread are used once, in Chapter 191, to put eight names in eight hands into a second column, and are not re-derived and not improved on. The two figures of the ninth generation that do not agree with each other are used in Chapter 196 and are not reconciled and neither is struck out.

- **Aren Kest and the brothers and the 417-mile question: the yard is on the page for two pages and the question is a question.** A man of about fifty with a waggon of his own is the only person in this case who has been to that valley and has been up the pass twice in eleven weeks and on the twenty-fifth of Fallowmonth said out loud in a hall that he did not go up it, and why, and had it minuted. **The 417-mile-scale question of what a road is for without a keeper is a question and not a man in this block and no batch may manufacture one, and what answers it is a man of fifty refusing to go up a pass and saying so in a room.**

- **The main world at the close of Chapter 200: the reach, the bench, the bell, the seam, the bag, and a road four hundred yards long.** The Sedge Reach is open with about forty men on it and the road open and the salt coming over the lane; the fourth bay is finished and is being pointed and pointing is never finished on the day it is begun, and the joint at the parapet is a foot and a half short and nobody in that yard has measured it. The bench of nine has been asked five times and has said yes four times and the fifth asking was not put and that is in the minute. The seam is under half an inch of lime in the third course of the fourth bay and has not moved. The bell went at the fourth hour and a half, rung by a boy and a carpenter, and nothing in the sound of it belongs to anybody. A refusal is in a bag on the ordinary post and a copy is on a shelf with a number against the office and nothing against a person, and a strip of cut paper in the same press weighs a shade over ten ounces and is the account of nobody and the number of persons that offer was made out to is still not on the sheet. A bundle of nine things from a county four hundred miles off has a piece of tarred hemp through it and the tenth was opened on a Tuesday in the third week of Harvestmonth in a room of two. And the road up from the water is four hundred yards long and it is there.

## Volume 04 — Batch 0005 Review Repair Pass

## Volume 04 — Batch 0005 — Review of the Review Repair Pass

507. **THE REPAIR'S OWN CENTRAL FINDING HAD SURVIVED IN THE VOLUME'S LAST PARAGRAPH, AND A REPAIR THAT MISSES THE LAST PLACE IT LOOKED IS NOT A REPAIR, IT IS A DRAFT.** Chapter 200, `chapter-0200.md` line 23. **Item 498 repaired Chapters 198 and 199 out of calling the man of forty-seven a road warden on the roll with a vote and not an office, and Chapter 200's yard inventory, the last full description of that yard in the volume, still read *And a road warden of this county's bridge guild on the deck of the first bay with a hod, who has a vote and not an office, who does not hold this reach or the Old Toll or the crossing, and who has worked eleven days in a year in which he has not voted once*.** It was contradicted four ways on the page: Chapter 200 line 3 and line 15, Chapter 198 line 27, and Chapter 198's own *He is not a road warden. There is a road warden of this guild with a vote and not an office and it is a different man and he is not in this yard.* **Repaired in place, and the last paragraph of the volume now ends on a man of forty-seven on the bench of nine because he was elected and not because he is on a trade, who does not hold this reach or the Old Toll or the crossing, and who has not voted since the day he was elected and did not use it then.** Two further faults went with it. **The clause *who has worked eleven days in a year in which he has not voted once* is garbled — there is no such thing as eleven days in a year and no year in this chapter — and it collided with Chapter 198's two uses of *eleven days* for the reaching of the fourth bay, which is a count of this month; it is cut.** **And the sentence gave the yard a second man with a hod beside a man of about nineteen carrying a hod badly, and left the following paragraph's *he carried a hod for four hours and a half and he did it well* with two candidates; the surviving sentence is now the man of forty-seven, which is the one the next paragraph is about.** The man is Bram Ottery, a Volume 03 character, on the bench of nine in Chapters 152, 156 and 157, and no name is spent and the volume's cast budget is unaffected. **A rule for the next repair pass in this project: grep the answer, do not grep the finding.**

508. **THE WRONG DESCRIPTION HAD ALSO BEEN WRITTEN INTO THE NEXT PHASE'S INSTRUCTIONS, WHICH IS THE `reviews/volume-04/batch-0002.md` FAILURE MODE VERBATIM — A WRONG PROHIBITION IS OBEYED.** `workspace/volume-04/close/PROMPT.md`, the promise-by-promise audit. **The prompt instructed the Volume 04 close to record as a delivered promise that *the man who would not have it measured is a road warden with a vote and not an office*, and `state/current.md` in the same commit says the close must not read the man of forty-seven as a road warden. A later phase must not read those as the same man either.**

## Canon established by the Volume 04 close

**Items 1 to 497 are not renumbered. Item 502 and item 505 are annotated in place. The three review passes above this heading are left as they were. This heading and everything under it were written by the phase that closed Volume 04 and outlined Volume 05, and it is the first place in this file where a whole volume's close and the next volume's plan live together, so a later phase that reads the top of this file has still read the rest of it.**

517. **THE VOLUME 04 CLOSE RECORD IS `outline/volumes/volume-04-close.md`, ELEVEN THOUSAND WORDS OVER TWELVE SECTIONS, AND IT IS THE FOURTH DOCUMENT OF ITS KIND IN THIS PROJECT.** It is **31,237 words** and its sections are, in order: **what the volume was about; the state files and what the close found on the page; the volume's argument as it landed; the five-block audit; a state-of-the-world ledger at the close of Chapter 200; a promise-by-promise audit; the corrections Volume 05 must not undo; the three hooks in the order `outline/volume-04.md` §11 gives them; the one plan conflict still open; what Volume 04 did badly and which of it Volume 05 inherits on purpose; what this close changed and what it did not touch; and the question Chapter 201 opens on.** **The model is `outline/volumes/volume-03-close.md` and the close's own header says so.** **A defect is recorded on its face: the close's opening sentence calls Volume 04 the third document of its kind and it is the fourth, since `volume-01-close.md`, `volume-02-close.md` and `volume-03-close.md` all exist. The sentence is a claim about the project's own record and a phase that edits the file should repair it and say that it has.**

518. **THE CLOSE FOUND SIX THINGS ON THE PAGE THAT THE STATE FILES DID NOT SAY, AND THE LARGEST IS THE DEVICE LEDGER.** They are set out at the close's §2 and they are, in short: **the `nine` count for Batch 0004 was recorded as 184 at 5.40 per thousand and the page reads 195; the volume's true rate is 2.87 / 4.58 / 7.31 / 5.73 / 7.26 and the sixth block is 7.26 and not 5.40; the batch deviation lists total 107 and not the 98 the close was told; Batch 0004's `about` column was recorded at 391 and the page reads 337; and the batch review findings that were written to a gitignored log and to this file and not to `reviews/` are now in `reviews/volume-04/batch-0005.md`.** **Every one of these is a figure a later phase may not inherit. The lesson is the project's oldest one and the close restates it: a state file is the least reliable document in this repository, and a figure that has been carried for one block is two blocks from being canon.**

519. **THE `nine` DEVICE, COUNTED AGAIN ON THE PAGE FOR THE CLOSE, AND THE COLUMN IS NOW THE ONE A LATER PHASE USES.** The standalone whole word is **941 across the volume in 168,814 words**, per block **95 / 153 / 250 / 195 / 248**, which is **2.87 / 4.58 / 7.31 / 5.73 / 7.26 per thousand.** The fifth block's per-chapter column is **27 / 27 / 18 / 27 / 25 / 36 / 28 / 15 / 22 / 23.** The residue devices are counted and not estimated: **`about` 404 in the fifth block and 1,801 in the volume, per block 287 / 382 / 391 / 337 / 404; `the whole of` 10 / 36 / 3 / 3 / 1, so one in the volume; `about N seconds` 1; `about nine + noun` 9; `in nine years` 7; `cut` 35 in the fifth block and all thirty-five ordinary.** Whole-word counting only, and a filler count is a baseline and not a target: `nodded` 0, `held` 7, `wrote` 25, `stood` 42, `plain` 0, `counted` 16, `breathed` 0, `steady` 0. **`---` rules 93, bolded line-openings 303, semicolons 0, em-dashes 0, straight double quotes 0.** **A per-line bold parity sweep across all two hundred chapter files returns zero and a duplicate-paragraph sweep across the fifth block returns clean, and both were run and both are recorded as having been run, which is the difference item 516 is about.** **Seven curly apostrophes were found in Chapters 152, 154, 159 and 160 and are recorded as a defect against the straight-apostrophe convention; a phase that edits the close and is not certain of the convention must check a chapter file before repairing them and must say what it found.**

520. **THE VOLUME 05 OUTLINE IS `outline/volume-05.md`, EIGHTEEN THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-TWO WORDS IN SEVENTEEN SECTIONS, AND ITS SPAN IS ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY DAYS.** It is the same species as `outline/volume-01.md` through `outline/volume-04.md` and it takes its section names from Volumes 02 to 04. **Main world: the twenty-fifth of Fallowmonth, YR 314, a Monday, to the twenty-fifth of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Thursday, one hundred and fifty days elapsed and one hundred and fifty-one inclusive, which is the five months of the Volume 5 row of the ledger in `outline/series.md`.** **Path time: ninety days in Calderwick, counted by the city's own day count, which the same ledger states as three months and which is a main-world conversion of a count the city does not keep.** **The first of Longlight, YR 315 falls at day 217 and is outside the volume, so this volume has no boundary oath-stone in it, and Longlight is the month the county renews them.**

521. **THE VOLUME 05 CALENDAR CHAIN IS BUILT FORWARD FROM VOLUME 04'S OWN LAST DAY AND FROM NOTHING ELSE, AND A PRE-EXISTING ONE-DAY CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO AUDITED CHAINS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED.** **Item 111 gives Fallowmonth 1, YR 312 as a Monday and item 147 audits forward from it and gives Mudmonth 1, YR 313 as a Tuesday, while `outline/volume-04.md` §17 gives Fallowmonth 1, YR 314 as a Friday, which is not the day that chain produces. Forty-three of the hundred and fifty-one days are market days.** **A phase that later audits the whole chain moves both of these together or neither, and must restate the last date when it does.**

522. **THE MARKET RULE IS TWICE A WEEK, SATURDAY AND THURSDAY, AND TWO FILES IN THIS REPOSITORY STATE IT WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS.** The count settles it: **Volume 04's two hundred and forty days contain sixty-nine market days, and this volume's hundred and fifty-one contain forty-three, and both are two in seven.** `bible/world.md` says the county keeps market days on the fourth and ninth day of each month, which is true of one month in Volume 02 and is not the rule, and continuity item 153 says the county's market days are Saturday and Thursday, which is the rule and is stated as if it were a description of that month. **A writer who uses the fourth-and-ninth rule will misdate every market in Volume 05, and the two lines must be reconciled in a later phase rather than in a chapter.**

523. **THE VOLUME 05 POWER STATE IS STAGE 3, THREADKEEPER, HELD AND NOT ADVANCED, AND THE SERIES PUTS THREADKEEPER IN VOLUMES 4, 5 AND 6.** Going in and unchanged from the close of Chapter 200: **three paths held, the County of Ash closed in writing and not lost, a fourth route refused in writing, a permanent limp in the right leg and a stick that is a ferrier's stick, a road-marked left palm warm at about the fourth hour, one object under a pound and two half tiles, a visible seam of about nine inches in a stone course in a bridge in Merefen that does not move, and the return stitch gone and not rebuilt.** **Volume 05 makes no cut, opens no fourth path, does not worsen the limp, adds no melody cost, and spends its one act of Stage 3 on a lineage reading, which `bible/power-system.md` gives the stage and which has never been used on the page in two hundred chapters.** The Many-Handed stage's worsening of the limp belongs to Volume 15. **The seam is not a door and not a key and not a mark, and no character in Volume 05 may use it as one.**

524. **THE VOLUME 05 DRIFT IS PLANNED, NOT CANON, AND IT IS THE FIRST NARROWING IN THIS CASE.** Main-world absence ninety days, printed warning three weeks, error sixty-nine days, about three quarters of the absence, against Volume 04's one hundred and seventy-one at one hundred and ninety-two, about nine tenths. **The ratio is error over absence in every case, never error over the warning and never the path interval over the warning.** The narrowing is a consequence of the absence being shorter and not of anything the city does, and the outline keeps a character's claim about the city's frame and the ledger's arithmetic in two separate registers and forbids a chapter from stating them together. **These are planning figures. A batch foots the real ones on the page, records the count, prints no figure it has not counted, tells no character any of it, and no character says the word *failed* about a road. The printed warning does not change and no later volume changes it.**

Third, the series' Volume 5 relationship row is a last private warning between Aren and a man whose name may not be written in this volume, and the outline does not take it, and takes the series' own stated milestone instead, which is learning to accept a refusal, including his own.** **And a fourth item, which is a false flag rather than a conflict: `outline/series.md`'s Volume 5 next-volume question and `outline/volume-04.md` §11's closing question are the same question in two registers, the cell giving the proposition and §11 giving the hand-off, and the Volume 04 close was told they differed.**

526. **THE ANTAGONIST'S NAME IS NOW IN NEITHER `outline/volumes/volume-04-close.md` NOR `outline/volume-05.md`, AND THAT IS A CHANGE A LATER PHASE MUST NOT UNDO.** The close was written with the name in it and the phase removed every occurrence before finishing, on the Volume 03 close's standing guard. **The name remains in `outline/series.md` and in `outline/volume-04.md` §16, where §16 records the conflict that the series' Volume 4 knowledge-control row is unsatisfied because of it.** **The separate-sheet rule holds: a claim and a name may be read together by a court that wants to and by nobody else. Thread 89 of `state/open-threads.md` and the Volume 02 close's §7.1 hold the second severance for Chapter 894, and a phase that eventually writes the name must check that thread and must not join any two halves in one sentence before Chapter 894.**

527. **THE VOLUME 05 NAME BUDGET IS PLANNED AT FIVE OF SIX PER BATCH, AND IT IS A PLAN.** Batch 0001 spends three, Batch 0002 one, Batch 0003 one, and Batches 0004 and 0005 none, which is five of thirty slots and twenty-four unfilled against a cap of thirty, one under, and against Volume 04's six of six and twenty-three unfilled. **A new name means first named in prose, and a child does not count, and the seventh child of Calderwick is not named.** **A batch that finds a face necessary spends a slot and records the arithmetic in its own state entry, and a batch that spends none records six unfilled.**

Her exact survival remains intentionally unknown, is Volume 09 and Volume 18 business, and the Volume 06 midpoint about what she saved and what she concealed is not pre-empted here.**
