All three totals were footed before they were printed here. **`nine` is 189 in 31,938 words, 5.92 per 1,000, per chapter 10 / 4 / 19 / 17 / 15 / 16 / 28 / 15 / 34 / 31**, against the volume's six-block ladder of 2.87 / 4.58 / 7.31 / 5.73 / 7.26 / 4.17, **so the block sits between Volume 04's third and fifth blocks and is the second-highest in the volume, and the reason is on the page and is not a tic: the city keeps a count of days, the ninth refusal is the block's subject, the ninth hour and the fourth hour and a half are the hours that do the city's work, and a man of thirty-two keeps a notebook.** `about` **360**, per chapter 43 / 41 / 37 / 34 / 29 / 31 / 33 / 36 / 39 / 37, **and no chapter is over forty-five.** `the whole of` **15**, against a house baseline of two or three a chapter. `about N seconds` **2**, one in Chapter 218 and one in Chapter 219, **both of them the two figures the batch required** and both re-counted after a device pass took the block from forty to two. `about nine + noun` **1**. `in nine years` **0**. `cut` **3** and all three were read and all three are ordinary — a ferrier's stick cut out of a fence rail, a man cutting a piece of glass rod at a stall, a pen cut down and not a quill — **and the working is not among them and is not named, priced, scheduled or described as available anywhere in the block.** `---` rules **51**. Bolded line-openings **130**. **Semicolons 0, em-dashes 0, straight double quotes 0, curly apostrophes 0, curly opening single quotes 0.** **One System panel in the block, in Chapter 214, two plain lines, no number in it.** No occurrence of the word *Gatehouse*. Filler as whole words, with the basis named in both columns: the block is **`nodded` 0, `held` 3, `wrote` 14, `stood` 33, `plain` 2, `counted` 9, `breathed` 0, `steady` 0**, against Volume 04 Batch 0005 (Chapters 191 to 200, the ten-chapter block this batch is measured against) at 0 / 7 / 25 / 42 / 0 / 16 / 0 / 0 and against the whole of Volume 04 at 1 / 41 / 142 / 156 / 2 / 66 / 0 / 0. **Six of the eight are at or under the ten-chapter baseline; `stood` at 33 is under the block's own baseline of 42 and over Batch 0001's 24 and is a man at a bench, a man at a gate and a man in a lane; and `plain` at 2 is over a zero and is deliberate, because the city's word for the light and the head of the second column of a book are both named as plain words and the block does not improve on either.** **A per-line bold parity check across every line of all two hundred and twenty chapter files returns zero, and a duplicate-paragraph sweep across the ten new chapters returns clean, and both were run here and both are recorded as having been run, which is the difference continuity item 516 is about.**

584. **SEVEN DEFECTS OF THIS BLOCK'S OWN TEXT WERE FOUND AND ALL SEVEN WERE REPAIRED, AND FIVE OF THEM ARE THE CLASS THIS PROJECT PAYS FOR, AND THE FIFTH IS THE ONE A DEVICE COUNT CANNOT SEE.** **One:** a device pass over the block cut `about N seconds` from forty to two, and the pass was done as a scripted substitution across ten files, **and reading every changed line afterwards, as continuity item 561 requires, found seven sentences with a conjunction missing out of them and two narrator's leaks of this book's own structure and one of the two chapters whose sections had been inserted in the wrong order.** All were repaired by reading. **Two:** Chapter 218's second-column scene had been inserted above the chapter's opening exchange by that same pass's earlier sibling, so a man of thirty-two asked what the book was of after he had already asked about the second column, **and Chapter 218 was rewritten whole in the right order rather than patched.** **Three:** two curly apostrophes had got into Chapters 215 and 217 and are now straight. **Four:** Chapter 220 said a man of sixty-six went into *the other* yard with the book in it when the book is in his own yard, and it now says his own yard. **Five:** Chapter 220's opening gave the ninth asking and the child's answer as two figures that the chapter's own later sentence contradicted, and both now say the time it takes to draw a breath. **Six:** Chapter 213 said the thing *is how they came apart*, Chapter 215 said the finding was *the reason this chapter is in the book*, Chapter 217 said *somebody in this book*, Chapter 211 said *neither of those things is in this book*, and Chapter 220 said *there is no third fact in this block* — **five narrator's leaks of this book's own structure onto a page, all five removed, and none of them was visible to any device count and all five were found by reading the file.** **Seven:** three blanked-out bold spans, one of them in Chapter 215 and one in Chapter 218, which passed a per-line parity check because each had an even number of markers with one span left open, **and the check that found them was reading the rendered line and not counting asterisks.** That seventh defect is the reason a parity check is necessary and not sufficient, and it is the same lesson as the broken bold span continuity item 561 records on the last line of the last chapter of Volume 04, and **this block's repair pass found the same class of thing in its own new prose inside a single pass.**

585. **THE BLOCK'S TEN ENDINGS, AND NINE OF THEM ARE NOT A REFUSAL.** **211** on the lamp standing where it was standing, a woman who did not ask him anything, and the shape of a good day in a place that has decided not to be met. **212** on a man of fifty with a waggon described in four seconds and a man with a stick not described, a man in the same street within a quarter of an hour of each other, and a cup that was not his. **213** on a man of fifty with a waggon coming through a gate with his name not wanted and asking a stranger what he wanted. **214** on a boy of fourteen on a worn step who will tell a stranger where the man who keeps the forms is and will not shake his hand, and the door has never once asked him for anything back. **215** on a man of sixty-six saying goodnight to nine people in a yard and never once to a man who is leaving. **216** on three pieces of paper in a coat, a date and one word under it, and two of them that say no, and a man who has not joined them and does not. **217** on an empty yard, a board, a bench, and a stranger who came four days early for a man with a nine-inch rule. **218** on a man of thirty-two walking out at the ninth hour knowing less about a mark than he knew at the fourth, carrying two refusals and a page and a line in his palm that is not one of theirs. **219** on a page of foolscap on a hook four feet away with an unfinished seventh line that he did not go and get. **220** on a ledger turned round with the spine toward a man of sixty-six, a rule nine inches long, a child of nine that did not go out, and about four hundred people in a city of about nine thousand who did not know and will not.

## Relationship state at the end of Chapter 220

- **Aren Kest and Calderwick: nineteen days inside a city that has refused contact eight times in four hundred years and has just, without knowing it, refused a ninth time, and he is the only person alive who saw it and did not know what he had seen.** A man of thirty-two with a limp and a stick and a left palm with a roadmark in it and a page in a coat with an unfinished seventh line that says *a person*, two identical eleven-word refusals in four pockets, a count of days in a notebook he has carried for four years, and a leg that is the same leg and is slower. **He has asked four questions in nineteen days and got four straight answers in nine words each, and has not asked a fifth, and the one he has not asked is the only one anybody in that city would have had to stop a person for.** He worked out on the eighth day that he was the safest person in the city, and why, and did not say it out loud. He is in no book, has asked nothing, has been refused and come back and been refused again, and about four people in that yard have said that a man who is protected by the correctness of a form and not by anything anybody did for him is the most protected person in a city of about nine thousand people.

- **Aren Kest and the child, who is the seventh child of the volume and is unnamed: a mark, a seventh line, thirteen days of not asking, and the one city in five volumes that has arranged not to be in the way of him not asking it.** It went through a gate he was standing at and he asked it nothing. It looked at his hand for a while and he did not put it behind him. It said *is that the far one* on the nineteenth day and he answered it in about three words without understanding it, the way he answered it in a lane four hundred miles off. **It carried a bundle four days in seven, took a hod eleven times in a yard in a day and was given a piece of bread off a sill and did not say thank you, and nobody in nine thousand people has ever used its name, and the reason is the city's and the reason is a name in a book.** On the nineteenth day a man of sixty-six asked it to take something out to the west gate and it said no in the time it takes to draw a breath, **and that is the ninth refusal in four hundred years and the first one given by a person who could be asked a second time, and it is the only one that cannot be filed, and he stood forty yards off with four words ready for thirteen days and did not call out and did not ask it again, and the seventh line is still not finished.**

- **Aren Kest and Dermit Crane, 66: two identical pieces of paper, a board over a book, and a man who has noticed a thing nobody noticed and has nobody to tell.** He has been in his yard once, on the sixth day, and on the ninth day on purpose, and was refused twice with the same eleven words in the same order, and carried both up the lane flat. He has been told, by four different people in nineteen days, four different answers to four questions, and none of the four was unkind. **Nobody in this city has ever been shown that book, and the reason is correct, and the effect is that nobody outside this city knows why the city said no to anything, ever, and the city does not know that this is a fact about itself — and a man of sixty-six said that in about thirty-one words to a stranger on the sixth day and has not said it since and is not complaining, and the ninth refusal of four hundred years came out of his own yard on the nineteenth day in about ninety words about a man and a column, said once, to a stranger, and not improved on.**

- **Aren Kest and Osmund Cusk, 61: a ledger of marks, a second column headed with a plain word meaning carried, and a hand.** He put his own palm on the bench and was told in nine words that it is not one of theirs, and asked a man for the confirmation of a thing he had worked out himself, **and nobody in that city has ever worked out what a man does that.** Cusk has wanted for most of his working life for somebody to tell him to stop keeping the book and said so once, to a stranger, in about nine seconds, and four people have asked him since whether he has ever said it twice and he has not and they did not ask him. **He will not turn that ledger round in this block, and the second column is not on the page, and what is in it is Block 0003's.**

- **Aren Kest and Nesh Karrow, 28: a bridge gate, four words, a bundle, and a want said once in one breath.** *I want it to be a letter.* She has been carrying for four years and turned back at three gates four days a week and told not refused because she is nobody. **Nobody in that city has ever said to her that the carrying is the job and not the failing, and it is not said in this block, and a man of thirty-two worked out on the nineteenth day, standing at the mouth of a yard, that the man who asked the child had known all of it and had put a woman's four years of being turned round into nine words and had not explained anything, and has not written that down and is not going to.**

- **Aren Kest and the council of eleven: a worn step, a book that holds what was asked, and a woman of sixty who will not say a thing twice.** He asked why eleven and was told, once, that eleven is a number that means eleven and that nine is a number the world uses so that everybody writes nine in a book. He came back three days later to be told whether it was still true and was refused in four seconds and a half, **and the refusal was right, and the woman put her hand flat on a table for half a second and took it off, and the clerk entered two lines and did not read them back.** Nothing is owed to him there and nothing has refused him, and he has not been told which of the two he is in.

- **Aren Kest and the city: a lamp, a ladder, a wharf, a glass works with a furnace in it, a market that opens when it likes, a gate that is a machine for letting liars through, and a name he did not buy for a penny.** Nobody here has asked him anything and about four people have wanted to. He was fed four days and not paid, and worked out on the eighth day that being fed is what a man is when he is not refused and is not kept. **He has not written down one word about the light, one word about the ladder, one word about the gate, and one word about the mark, and he has not asked why any of them.**

- **Aren Kest and the seventh line of a page of foolscap: unchanged, and the volume's live question is where it was at the end of Chapter 210.** The line says *a person*, it has been looked at twice and not finished, he has not taken the page out since the ninth day and has not looked at it, and **on the nineteenth day a person said no in front of him and he did not ask them a second question, which is the only time in two hundred and twenty chapters that the volume's mechanic has been usable and the man it was usable to has not used it.**

- **The path at the close of Chapter 220, the nineteenth day of a count of days from the last renewal, and the volume's remaining chain.** A city of about nine thousand people on a river, a wharf with nine hundred feet of quay and a crane every ninety feet and a lighter that comes up under the quay, a boat builder two thirds done for eleven days because he is sixty and there is nobody behind him, a glass works with a furnace that has not gone out in four hundred years, a bread oven hot at the second hour and at the ninth, a market on a street of two hundred yards with about four hundred people in it, a man of thirty who sells names for a penny, three gates, nine of us carrying, a council of eleven in a long room with a table and a clerk of forty, a man of sixty-six in a bindle yard who makes eleven-word forms, a man of sixty-one in a yard past two gates who keeps a book about the outside, and a lamp that stands. **Days twenty to thirty of ninety are ahead of the block and the chain is the city's own count, and the ninth refusal is behind them, unentered, and nobody in that city knows.**

- **The main world, the eighth of Embermonth, YR 314, a Sunday, at the ninth hour, and about four hundred miles off and not on the page in this block.** A reach open with about forty men on it, the fourth bay being pointed, a joint a foot and a half short, a line about nine inches long under about half an inch of lime that has not moved, a mark in a parapet at the height of a thumb and a mark in a coping four hundred yards from it, a bell with forty-one rivets rung at the fourth hour and a half by a boy and a carpenter, a bench of nine that has refused a road twice and put both refusals twice in a minute under a stair, a woman in a room with a door on a lane who is not going to walk up that road, a second copyist who has not opened the tenth letter, a bundle of nine things with a tarred hemp through it, a strip of cut paper that weighs a shade over ten ounces, a form in a bag on the ordinary post with a ruled space for a figure of persons and nowhere at all for the name of a person, a jar in a lock-up in a yard two hundred miles off with a hundred and forty marks against it that has been neither taken nor refused, and a yard on Weir Street that has been off the page for twenty chapters and is the volume's second-largest cost after the city.

## Volume 05 — Batch 0003 (Chapters 221–230, "The Count")

586. **THE BLOCK'S OWN FRAME IS THE CITY'S, DAYS TWENTY TO THIRTY OF NINETY, AND IT IS SAID IN NOBODY'S MOUTH AND IN NO NARRATIVE SENTENCE, AND NO MAIN-WORLD MONTH, NO REAL-WORLD MONTH AND NO MAIN-WORLD WEEKDAY IS SPOKEN OR WRITTEN IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS IN ANY REGISTER INCLUDING A NOTEBOOK.** The block runs from the twentieth day of a count of days from the last renewal to the thirtieth, and the twentieth day is behind the reader with a child of nine's refusal on it and entered nowhere. The days on the page are the first, the second, the fourth, the sixth, the ninth, the twelfth, the fifteenth and the nineteenth of Batch 0002, and then the twentieth, the twenty-first, the twenty-second, the twenty-third, the twenty-fourth, the twenty-fifth, the twenty-sixth, the twenty-seventh, the twenty-eighth, the twenty-ninth and the thirtieth, and the hours, and the second hour and the ninth hour are the hours the city's work is done by. **A sweep of the ten chapters for the eleven main-world month names, the twelve real-world month names and the seven weekday names returns zero, and four instances of a main-world weekday that the first full draft of this block carried were found and repaired by reading the file and are at item 599.** The ledger's conversion of ninety days into three months is not performed on the page and is not quoted. **The city's own figures are three and none of them is a hearth: about nine thousand people, eleven on the council, four hundred years**, and a fourth schedule figure is the market's four days out of seven, and none of the four is a figure of persons and none of the four is a hearth.

587. **THE FORM ARRIVES, AND IT ARRIVES THE MOST BORING WAY THERE IS, AND A MAN OF ABOUT FORTY-SIX CARRIES IT IN.** A man of forty-six with a satchel and a stick and a list of about four hundred places comes down the eastern road on the twentieth day and has been on it since before the light. **He is not a trader, not an agent, not a member of anything, and he is a man who leaves a printed sheet at a door.** His own words, once, in the tone of a man saying a price, in Chapter 221: *I leave them. Four hundred doors and I leave one at each and I go on to the next. That is the whole of it. I have never once been asked to fill one in and I have never once filled one in, and I have been doing it eight years and I have left about three thousand and I could not tell you what is on the top of one of them.* And the second sentence of it, which is the trade fact the whole block runs on: *a form is a thing a door can throw away, that is why it is printed and not written, a thing you write you keep.* He has never been told what the series is for and has never asked, and the reason is on the page in his own mouth: **the list is what he is paid for.** The last of the four hundred places on his list is a name he has never heard and the district column against that line is filled in like all the others, and **the name is not printed on any page in this block and the city is not named in any character's mouth.**

588. **THE FORM IS THE OFFICE'S OWN SERIES AND IT HAS FOUR SPACES FOR A FIGURE AND NOWHERE AT ALL FOR A NAME, AND THE FOUR SPACES ARE THE SAME QUESTION ASKED FOUR TIMES.** It is printed and not ruled, about the size of a broadside with a little less paper than a broadside, **ruled in six columns, five with heads and a sixth with no head at all and the same width as the other five**, and the six heads are *Object*, *Date*, *Person having knowledge*, *Keeper* and *How often*, and the sixth line is the same line that has been in that series since Chapter 205. **Four of the six columns are ruled for a figure, and the man of sixty-six says in a yard that it is four figures or it is one figure written four times, and that he has not got anything to tell anybody about which of the two it is and neither has the man who printed it, and that a man fills in the spaces because the spaces are there.** The marginal instruction is on the reverse and is **not printed in this block, is not explained, and is refused about in one sentence by a man of sixty-six who says he is not going to talk about what is written on the other side of a piece of paper that has come into his yard.** Nobody in this block explains it, and the four sheets in a tray by a stove in a main-world room are the same instrument and are not in this block and are not in the same county as anything in it, and no character joins anything to anything.

589. **THE FIGURE, AND HOW IT WAS FOOTED ON THE PAGE BEFORE IT WAS PRINTED, AND THE TWO NUMBERS, AND THE FACT THAT NOBODY IN THAT CITY HAS COMPARED THEM.** This is the block and it is stated cleanly and is not an ambiguity anywhere on the page. **The book under a board has eight lines in it** and the eighth was made on the sixth day of this count and is the form about a foot long with eleven words on it. **The man of sixty-six also has nine, because he has the forms he has made in his head the way he has dates in his head, and the nine includes the ninth refusal of the nineteenth day, which is in a coat two hundred yards up a lane in the inside pocket of a man of thirty-two with a limp, and the book does not have it because there is no column for it.** He counts both out loud in a yard on the twenty-third day, about a minute apart, and does not put one against the other, and about four of the people in that yard have said since that nobody in that yard has ever worked out that he was holding both at once. **The figure that goes out is nine, written four times, once in each of the four ruled spaces, and it is the same figure four times and not a sum, and the count of digits that leave the city is thirty-six and the number that leaves the city is nine, and nobody in the city has ever thought about a figure that appears four times on one sheet because a city that has not put a figure on a sheet in four hundred years has no habit about it.** The difference between the nine on the sheet and the eight in the book is one, and the one is a child of nine years old, and **nobody in a city of about nine thousand people has compared the two numbers and nobody is going to.**

590. **A REFUSAL COUNT IS A COUNT OF REFUSALS AND IS NEVER A COUNT OF PEOPLE, AND IT IS HELD ON THE PAGE IN THIS BLOCK AND NOT ONLY IN THESE FILES.** A man of sixty-six says it once, in a yard, in about eleven words, and says it to about two hundred bundles of cord and not to the sheet: **that is a count of things this city has said no to, it is not how many of us there are, it is not that, I have never in twenty years had to say that and I am saying it now and I am saying it short.** A man of forty-six asks what the nine is and is told the same sentence a second time on the twenty-ninth day, writes it on the back of his own list and **not on the sheet**, and has the same sentence on the back of that list twice by the end of the block, about four inches apart, in the same hand. **The figure of eight, the figure of nine and the figure of ten are never added to each other and are never added to a figure of persons, and the eight figures on the two sheets are not added either, and the block says so on the page in a yard.** A city of about nine thousand people, eleven on the council and four hundred years remain the city's three figures and the refusal counts are not a fourth city figure and are not a hearth.

591. **THE SECOND ASKING IS THE SAME SHEET AND THE SAME QUESTION AND THE ANSWER IS A DIFFERENT FIGURE BECAUSE A CHILD WAS ASKED A SECOND TIME AND SAID NO.** The same printed sheet comes back clipped to a second sheet of the same series on the twenty-seventh day and goes back in the satchel blank, and comes round again on the twenty-ninth and is answered in the same way. **A man of forty-six says why in about nineteen words, standing in a yard, about a room two hundred miles off and not about this city: a series goes round twice and the room has both of them, and a room with two returns from one district is not a room with a problem, it is a room with a pile, and nobody in a room adds two figures from one district together and nobody in a room asks why they are different.** On the twenty-ninth day, before the sheet is answered, **a man of sixty-six asks a child of nine years old the same question he asked it on the nineteenth day, in the same yard, in the same words, and says the reason out loud in about eleven words, and the reason is that the figure he wrote on the twenty-third was one higher than the number in his book and there is one refusal in this city he has never been able to put on a page.** **No**, said the child, in the time it takes to draw one breath. **Eight in the book, and the child twice, and eight and two is ten**, and the arithmetic is done out loud in a yard before the figure is written, and the second figure is ten in four ruled spaces, and it is not a count of people and it is not a count of rooms and it is not a count of doors and it is a count of times this city has said no. **A person can be asked a second time and a column cannot, and the block says that once, in Chapter 230, in a man's own words in a working yard, and does not say it twice, and no narrator agrees with it, and nobody improves on the ninety words a man of sixty-six said about it in Chapter 220, which are not said again in this block in any form.**

592. **THE SHEET LEAVES IN A BUNDLE OF CORD AND REED, AND A GATE IS A MACHINE FOR LETTING LIARS THROUGH, AND THE ONLY THING THIS CITY HAS EVER SENT OUT OF IT IN FOUR HUNDRED YEARS IS A MARK IN A CHILD'S HAND.** A man of fifty-five in a hut with three bars has turned round about four hundred people in nineteen years and says four words and has never once had to raise his voice. He turns the man of forty-six round on the twenty-fourth because the man is carrying a sheet of paper in his hand, and **a man of forty-six works out inside a quarter of an hour that the three bars are for bundles and not for men, and puts the sheet flat inside a bale of cord and reed and cords it over with about four turns through the loops that are already in it for that, and says one word while he does it, and the word is *cord*, and a man of sixty-six says it in the tone of a man saying a price.** The gate-man says nothing the second time, and about four people in that hut have said since that this is the first time in nineteen years a man has gone through that gate carrying a bundle without the four words. **Nobody in this city knows that a figure has left it, and nobody in this city is asked, and the child is not used to carry it and is not asked to, and the mark in the child's hand is not the instrument of the figure going out and no chapter joins the two.**

593. **THE MIDPOINT REVERSAL ARRIVES IN THE MOST BORING WAY AND IT IS A MAN OF SIXTY-ONE TURNING A BOOK ROUND, AND THE REASON IS A FIGURE THAT WENT OUT AND NOT A VISITOR.** **Osmund Cusk turns the second column round on the twenty-fifth day, ten days after refusing it in four words on the fifteenth, unasked, and the reason is that he is the only man in the city with a book about the outside and that the outside now has a piece of paper about this city on it that is wrong by one and that he cannot correct and that nobody outside will ever hold his book.** **He does not repeat his want from Chapter 218 and does not say he has wanted to be told to stop and does not go back over it, and that is deliberate and is the block's use of a spent line.** What is in the column: **eleven entries over four hundred years, in two parts, the first a hand and the second a road written the way a road is written, which is from here outward, and the eleven of them are not the same eleven and every one of them goes out of this valley and across about a day of country and into a place, and not one of the eleven names a place anybody in that city can see from where they are standing.** He does not know what the column is for, has not asked in nineteen years, and gives the reason for not asking in his own words and it is the same reason as Chapter 218 and is not re-derived.

594. **THE CITY KNOWS ABOUT THE ELEVEN AND IT KNOWS AS AN ORDINARY THING, AND NOBODY IN IT HAS EVER ASKED HOW A ROAD OUT AND BACK IS MADE.** Chapter 226, and it arrives as trade fact and not as a revelation: **a man of fifty with a waggon has been to four of the eleven and has never in nineteen years put two of them together in one sentence; a woman of about thirty with a pail has been to two of them and has a sister at one of them and has said so to strangers and to no one in her own city; a boy of fourteen on a step has been to none of them and has the names of all eleven, and gets them from about nine people, and there is no book in that city with the eleven in it except the one about two inches thick under a roof at the end of a lane past two gates.** About four hundred people in the city have been out of the gate and about nine hundred know the name of one of the eleven, and **neither figure knows anything about the other one.** Nobody has asked how the roads are made and the not asking is not a rule and there is nobody who could make one.

595. **THE ELEVENTH LINE, FOURTEEN YEARS, A WOMAN AND A BOY, NO NAMES IN EITHER COLUMN, AND NO OUTCOME COLUMN, AND HE IS NOT ASKED.** **The eleventh line has two marks on it and the other ten lines have one each, and the first of the two is a woman's and the second is a boy's, and the boy would have been about nine, and the second mark is the same shape as the mark a child of nine years old put on that bench on the nineteenth day of this count, and a man of sixty-one says in about eleven words that he has never seen her and has never had her name and that there is no name in either column of that book and has not been one in four hundred years.** **The figure fourteen is said out loud in that yard for the first time in nineteen years and it is in the tone of a man saying a price.** About a year is the only length of time anybody in that city can give in days and **nobody in that city has ever given one of those in a month because there are no months.** **A man of sixty-one says, before anybody asks him, that there are eleven lines and a hand and a day and a road and that there has never been anything else on any of them in four hundred years, and that there is no column for what became of anybody and there is not going to be one and he could not fill one in.** Nobody asks him. **The not asking is four seconds long and a man of thirty-two with a limp had a question ready for fourteen days and did not ask it, and a page of foolscap in his coat has a seventh line that says a person and was looked at on the twenty-third and on the twenty-ninth and was not finished on either.** **A boy of fourteen at the mouth of the yard says the only true thing anybody says about a book in it: that line is older than me.** **Her survival stays intentionally unknown, nobody in this block tells him what became of her, he does not ask, the keeper says so before he asks, and her route is Volumes 09 and 18 and the Volume 06 midpoint is not pre-empted by anybody in this block.**

596. **THE SECOND HALF OF THE REVERSAL: THEY ARE ASKED TO BECOME EVIDENCE AND THEY REFUSE, AND THE REFUSAL IS A REFUSAL TO BE A DOCUMENT, AND WHAT COMES OUT OF IT IS NOTHING.** On the twenty-seventh day a second sheet of the same series comes back clipped to the first, and **the object column on the first sheet has a place name in it and the object column on the second is empty, and that is the only difference between the two that anybody in the yard can see.** A man of forty-six says in about nine seconds what the second sheet wants, in the plainest register anybody in that city has for a piece of printed paper: **it is asking the district for a number of people in it who know about a thing, and the office has not written the thing down, and an office that will not name a thing is not hiding it, it is doing the same thing you are doing.** Nobody improves on it and nobody in that yard has worked out that the man with the satchel has just said the truest thing that has been said in that yard in four hundred years and that both of the two men in the room missed it. He then asks the man of sixty-six to make him a form, for nothing, to carry back and say that this city has declined. **A man of sixty-six who has written about four hundred pieces of paper in twenty years has never declined to make one, and he declines in Chapter 227, and he does not say the same eleven words, and he stands up to say the reason, which is twenty-two words: a form is a document, a document is a thing a court can do something with, and he is not going to put a second one about this city into the same room in the same book as the first one.** And the cost, said by the man with the satchel, standing, in about nineteen words, and it is the best piece of evidence in the volume that a refusal can be true and still be useless: **it is worth nothing, the first one is gone, it went out on the twenty-fourth in a bundle, and not filling this one in does not take that one back, and the room will still have the other one, and I have never once known which of the two things in a satchel was the one that mattered until this week and it was the one that was filled in.**

597. **THE LINEAGE READING, MADE ONCE, AT THE END OF THE TWENTY-SEVENTH DAY, IN A LANE, WITH A HAND ON A WALL, AND IT IS THE ONE ACT OF STAGE 3 THIS BLOCK SPENDS.** He puts his left hand flat on a wall the way a man puts a hand flat on a thing to see whether it is warm, and the wall is warm on the other side of his hand too, and he reads what the refusal is made of, **and what comes back is a list, and it is written out in his own hand at about the tenth hour in a room with a bench too short for him in it, and it is eleven lines and there are no words in it.** It produces, in this order and in no other: **a list; under the list a column; in the column shifts; against one of the shifts a man, and the man is fifty-two and he is on the third shift and has been on the third shift for nineteen years, and there is no other man's name anywhere in the eleven lines; and under the eleven lines something older that is not a list and has no column, which is a decision four hundred years old that eleven people made in a room once, and it is the reason for a lamp that has not turned since, and there is a line about what was paid and a line about when, and there is nothing under either of them that says why anybody in that room chose one over the other, **and the one reading returns the shape of a decision and not the inside of it, which is what lineage is and is not motive-reading, and the panel's *it does not go further for anybody* is true of what follows it, and the eleven people are dead and he has not found out what they said to each other and is not going to. The prose phase's first draft did give the reason and the Batch 0003 review repair pass cut it, and that is the whole of the change and it is at item 602.**.** **The eleven lines are the only page he has ever filled in in four years and it is eleven lines of a thing he is not allowed to have. It does not produce a door, it does not produce consent, it does not produce the city opening, and nobody in this city is told any of it and is not going to be.** It tells him one thing about his mother and one thing only: **a route is a thing four hundred people kept a column for, and a woman and a boy went out on one of them in a year this city counts in days, and there is no column in four hundred years of anybody's book for what became of either of them.** The panel stands at the threshold in two plain lines with no number in it: *Read it as far as it goes and then stop. It does not go further for anybody, and the part that is left is not being kept from you.* **He does not write it down, and the cost of holding three paths is on the page as an ordinary working day in a glass yard, where he watched a gather go from the colour it should be to the colour it should not be and did not move and did not speak, and where a man of thirty-four with lime put a duckboard down under his feet without a word, and the eleven lines are still in a notebook in the inside pocket of a coat on the twenty-eighth and on the thirtieth and he cannot stop seeing the eleventh of them, and that is the tax and not a symptom.**

598. **IVO MARROW, 52, AND THE TWO THINGS HE SAID, AND THE ONE NEW NAME OF SIX AND FOUR SLOTS UNFILLED.** **He is first named in prose in Chapter 228, in a glass works, and he is a glass man who has been in that yard since he was seventeen, and the thing he is good at is the wall.** **About nine men work from the second hour to the ninth and about nine of them can go up the ladder and one of them does it four times a day, and the wall is four hundred years old and is not flat and is not straight, and there are about nine places on it where a ladder will go and about nine where it will not, and he knows the nine and knows which of the nine is the one for a man with a bucket in one hand, and no one in this city has ever asked him and about four men in that yard have watched him do it about two thousand times and said so once, to a stranger, and not to him.** The two things are said once each, in the same conversation, in his own words, in a working yard: **first, that there is a piece of paper with his name on it and the name of the man before him and the name of the man before him, and it is a list of the third shift and it is in a drawer in a room in this city, and about four hundred people in this city could be asked what the third shift is and not one of them would be able to tell you, and he is not asking for anything and he is saying it out loud once to a stranger because he will be gone.** **And second, that he does not want to die on it, that he is fifty-two, that there is a brother of mine at the low end of the river who thinks I am on a roof, and that if somebody knew what the shift was, and if he did not want to be on it, then he would be able to say that, and there is nobody in this city he could say it to, and that is the whole of why he has said the other thing.** **Nobody improved on either, a man of thirty-four with lime did not turn round, and about four people in that yard have said since that a man of fifty-two knowing that a piece of paper in a drawer is the only paper about him in the world and saying it once is not a complaint and is not a want and is the reason the other of the two things is believable.** He is not a symbol and no character in this block calls him one and the block never puts him in front of a reader as a cost. **He says the block's finding out loud in Chapter 230 in a working yard in about nineteen words, and he says the mechanic in his own words once, and he says the third thing, which is a thing about the man of thirty-two and is the block's last page.** `outline/volume-05.md` §13's Batch 0003 row plans one of six and four unfilled. **The block spends one and leaves four unfilled: Ivo Marrow, 52, first named in prose in Chapter 228.** **Volume 05 therefore stands at five names of six per batch used, twenty-four of thirty slots unfilled across the five batches, against the volume's planned five and twenty-four.** Osmund Cusk, 61, Dermit Crane, 66 and Nesh Karrow, 28 are spent names and all three have pages and **none of the three was re-described**: Cusk is in Chapter 225 and his want is not repeated, Crane is in Chapters 222, 223, 224, 227 and 229 and his Chapter 216 sentences about a figure in a return and about a refusal made twice are not said again, and Karrow is not in this block. **The child is a child and is unnamed and is not named in any of the ten chapters and does not count.** The man of fifty with a waggon, the man of about thirty-four with lime, the woman of about thirty with a pail, the man of thirty who sells names for a penny, the man of fifty-five in the hut, the man of thirty with a barrow and a mule, the man of about thirty at the corner, the clerk of forty, the woman of sixty, the boy of fourteen and the man of about forty-six with a satchel are addressed by trade or by age. **The phrase *the seventh child of this block* is wrong and appears nowhere in canon and is nowhere in this block.**

599. **FOURTEEN DEFECTS OF THIS BLOCK'S OWN TEXT WERE FOUND AND ALL FOURTEEN WERE REPAIRED, AND TWELVE OF THEM ARE THE CLASS THIS PROJECT PAYS FOR, AND THE FINDING TOOL WAS READING A FILE AND NOT COUNTING ANYTHING.** The device pass took `about` from seven hundred and nine to three hundred and eighty and `about N seconds` from sixteen to zero, and it was done as a scripted bounded substitution across ten files, **and reading every changed line afterwards, as continuity item 561 and item 584 require, found fourteen defects, and every one of the fourteen was found by reading.** **One:** the substitution `about four men` to `a few of the men` produced *has been right a few of the men on a lane for twenty-five days* in Chapter 225 and the same break in Chapter 227, and both are repaired to *has been right about four men on a lane*. **Two:** the substitution of the city's figure produced *a few hundreds of people in a city of about nine thousand people* in nine places, because the phrase was half replaced, and all nine are repaired. **Three:** the same pass produced *and this city on a river that has been told by a man in a yard* at the head of Chapter 226, having eaten the city's own figure, and it is repaired. **Four:** the pass stripped the hedge off *about three thousand forms at about three thousand doors* in sixteen places, which is a claim change and not a device change, and all sixteen are restored. **Five:** the same pass stripped the hedge off *a city of about nine thousand people* in seven places and the same on *a city of nine thousand people*, and all are restored, because **the city's figure is one of the volume's three and the hedge is part of the figure.** **Six, and it is the class item 584 is about:** **Chapter 223's woman-with-a-pail paragraph had a bold span that was opened and never closed, and it passed no parity check because the sentence was bolded by hand and the line simply ended, and the check that found it was reading the rendered line and not counting asterisks. Seven: the repair of that paragraph then produced a second one, an italic span opened and never closed in the next line, and both are repaired. Eight: Chapter 230's last paragraph had a closing `**` with no opening `**` at all, which is the same defect in reverse and was found by the parity check and confirmed by reading. - **Aren Kest and Calderwick: thirty days inside a city that has refused contact eight times in four hundred years in a book and nine times in a man's head, and has in ten days handed a printed figure to an office two hundred miles off twice, and is the only person alive who knows both figures and the book.** A man of thirty-two with a limp and a stick and a road-marked left palm and a page in a coat with an unfinished seventh line that says *a person*, which he took out on the twenty-third and on the twenty-ninth and did not finish on either, **eleven lines in a notebook in the inside pocket of the same coat, and the eleventh of them is a man of fifty-two on a shift nineteen years old, and he cannot stop seeing it.** He has asked four things in the first fortnight and got four straight answers in nine words each and has not once told any of the four that they were being difficult, and **on the twenty-ninth day he watched a person in this city be asked the same thing twice and say no and did not ask it a single question himself, and the seventh line says a person and is not finished and he is not going to finish it.** He is in no book, has asked nothing, and is the safest person in a city of about nine thousand people, and **on the twenty-eighth a man of fifty-two told him that the safest thing about him is that he is the same as a line in a form, and that it is not kindness, and a man of thirty-two with a limp could not answer it and did not try and has not written it down and is not going to.**

- **Aren Kest and Dermit Crane, 66: a printed sheet with four figures on it, a second sheet that went back blank, and a man who is right about a book and wrong about a figure.** He was in that yard on the twenty-second, the twenty-third, the twenty-fourth, the twenty-seventh and the twenty-ninth. **He wrote a figure on a printed sheet for the first time in twenty years and he wrote it four times, and he did not notice that he was holding two numbers, and nobody in that yard has worked out that he was holding both at once.** He asked a question in that yard for the first time in about six years and it was *has anybody ever come here*, and the answer was no, in eight years, not once, and he did not answer it and the silence was a man finding out that there is a second thing about a piece of paper that is worse than the first. **He declined in Chapter 227 to make a form for the first time in twenty years and stood up to say the reason and the reason is that a document is a thing a court can do something with, and the man who asked him for it told him in a yard that the refusal was worth nothing and that the first figure was already gone, and Crane has not said one word about that since and did not write it down and is not going to.**

## Volume 05 — Batch 0004 (Chapters 231–240, "The Road That Is Not Made")

604. **THE BLOCK'S OWN FRAME IS THE CITY'S, DAYS THIRTY-ONE TO FORTY OF NINETY, AND IT IS SAID IN NOBODY'S MOUTH AND IN NO NARRATIVE SENTENCE AS A DATE.** The block runs from the thirty-first day of a count of days from the last renewal to the fortieth, and the fortieth is the last hour of a count this city keeps and that nobody in it keeps except two men, and the main world comes back at the ninth hour of the fortieth. The days on the page are the thirty-first, the thirty-third, the thirty-fifth, the thirty-seventh, the thirty-eighth, the thirty-ninth and the fortieth, and the hours, and the second hour and the ninth hour and the fourth hour and the fifth hour and the seventh hour are the hours this city's work and this city's work in an office two hundred miles off are done by. **No main-world month, no real-world month and no main-world weekday is spoken or written in any of Chapters 231 to 237 or 239 in any register including a notebook, and the three main-world chapters, 238, 239 and 240, carry the main-world chain and only the main-world chain.** A sweep of the ten chapters for the eleven main-world month names, the twelve real-world month names and the seven weekday names returns five distinct tokens, and **every one of the five was read and every one of the five is a main-world date in a main-world scene or a false positive: `Hearthmonth` sixteen times, at `238` three, `239` three and `240` ten, which is the chapter that is entirely in the county; `Embermonth` twice at `238`, both back-references to the crossing out of the eighth of Embermonth in the year before; `Saturday` once, which is the return and is correct on the chain at `outline/volume-05.md` §17, where day 103 is the eighth of Hearthmonth, YR 315, a Saturday and a market day; `Friday` once, which is a man of about nineteen being hired in and is a main-world fact that names no day; and `May` once, at `233:31`, which is a man of thirty-two with a limp asking *May I hold it* and is not a month. `Sunday` returns zero, and this corrects an earlier entry in this item that claimed one: the crossing out is referred to by its date on the page and never by its weekday, the sentence that put a man with a satchel on the eastern road on the seventh of a Sunday is not on the page, and the sweep was not re-counted after that sentence was removed, which is the tenth worked example of the defect item 618 records.** **The city's own figures are three and none of them is a hearth: about nine thousand people, eleven on the council, four hundred years**, and a fourth schedule figure is the market's four days out of seven, and about four hundred people in the city have been out of the gate, and **none of the four is a figure of persons in the sense the office's sheet means and none of the four is a hearth.**

605. **THE MESSAGE SYSTEM, AND IT IS NOT A ROAD AND NOT A POST, AND IT IS BUILT OUT OF MATERIALS THE CITY ALREADY HAS.** A room off a lane that goes down to the quay, which was a room for cord and is still a room for cord, with a bench the length of two men, a stove at the end of the bench, a door on a lane, a hook by the door and a shelf about five feet off the floor and eleven feet long with about nine bundles of cord and reed on it. **Nine people carry, half of them women, and none of them is paid, and that has been the arrangement for four hundred years and it is in nobody's book.** What is made is **a strip of paper about a foot long, ruled in five lines by the same rule nine inches long and the same strip of whalebone in the yard at the bottom of the same lane, with nothing written on any of the five, and a mark put in the corner in a child's left hand.** The strips are folded once across the middle and once again, corded into bales with about four turns through the loops that are already in them, put on the shelf, and go out four days in seven behind a child of nine years old, and **nobody in that room is told what is in a bale and not one of the nine has ever asked, and a man of sixty-six said that out loud on the thirty-third day in about nineteen words and that it is the third thing he has said out loud in twenty years that was not about paper.** **A strip came back into the city on the thirty-fifth day inside a bundle of cord and reed with the cord neither cut nor retied, with a mark in the corner of it that nobody in that room put there, and it went onto the shelf with the other eight of its kind and it was not counted and it has not been looked at since the seventh hour of that day.** Nobody explains what a roadmark is, nobody says what the mark is called, and four people looked at it for about four minutes and not one of them said anything. **What must not be on the page is not on the page: there is no mechanism, no consent, no door, no explanation of a mark, and nothing a reader in the main world could file, and the system has no name in the main world and no office and the two hundred and forty pieces of paper on a table in the long room in Chapter 237 are the second half of the fourth sheet of a printed series cut along the fold, not a system.**

606. **THE MAN OFF THE ROAD IS NOT ALLOWED TO HELP, AND THE REASON IS THE VOLUME'S FINDING AND IT IS SAID BY THE MAN OF SIXTY-SIX AND NOT BY THE VISITOR, IN ABOUT NINETEEN WORDS, ON THE THIRTY-FIFTH DAY, TO A ROOM.** *You are the only person in this city that is in a book somewhere else. Build this with you in it and two places have got a join in them, and a join with a person in it is a column, and a column can be filled in without asking anybody.* **It is the fourth thing Dermit Crane has said out loud in twenty years that was not about paper, and he said it to a room and not to the stranger, and a woman of twenty-eight folded a strip of paper and did not turn round, and a man of thirty-four with lime nine hundred feet up the lane put a gather into a mould and did not turn round either, and the two of them are nine hundred feet apart and neither of them knew the other had heard the same shape of a thing and neither of them has been told.** A man of thirty-two with a limp asked for permission to hold the strip first and was told no in one word by a woman of twenty-eight who was folding at the time, and that is the fifth person in this city to tell him no and the five did not consult each other, and **he did not ask a seventh question after it and the not-asking is on the page.** A man of sixty-one refused a column of it in nineteen words on the thirty-first day, standing in a doorway about two minutes and not coming further in, and the reason he gave is that **a book about the outside is what a message system turns into when somebody starts counting, and he has got one and has not been able to put it down in nineteen years, and a figure in a book is a figure in a return, and a room will take a number off you and not a name and those are the same transaction**, and that is the second of the two things he has said out loud in nineteen years and both have been to strangers.

607. **THE SECOND PERSON WITH A SATCHEL, AND THE WORD ON THE SHEET, AND NOBODY IN THAT CITY ASKS WHAT IT MEANS.** A man of about thirty-one comes down the eastern road on the thirty-seventh day, is turned round at the road gate in four words for carrying a sheet of paper in his hand, works out in about two minutes that the three bars are for bundles and not for men, and cords the sheet into a bale with about four turns and says one word while he does it, and the word is *cord*, and a man of sixty-six says it at about the third hour in the tone of a man saying a price, and the two of them are two hundred yards apart and neither has ever seen the other. **He is not an agent and not a member of anything and he is a man who leaves a printed sheet at a door, and he has carried about two thousand of the office's series in six years and has never once known what is in the four places and has said so out loud twice in about a week, in a yard and in a room, in the tone of a man saying a price.** The object column on this sheet **has a word in front of the place name, and the word is *eastern*, and it is on a sheet in this block and nobody in that city knows what it means and no character in that city asks.** A man of thirty-two with a limp read it and did not say it out loud and did not say what it meant and did not say where he had read it before, which is in a sheet of good paper about the size of a broadside in a bag in the ordinary post in a county four hundred miles off and in a copy on a shelf in that county, and **the word is now in two documents and a bag and a printed sheet of the office's series and nobody in any of the four places has joined any two of them.** A boy of fourteen said the only true thing anybody in that yard said about the six columns, in nine words: *It wants people and it will not say people.*

608. **THE FOURTH ASKING, AND THE FIGURE OF PERSONS, AND THE DRAWER NOBODY OPENS, AND THE SECOND ANSWER THAT WAS IN THE ROOM FOR AN HOUR.** The same printed series goes into the long room at the top of the lane on the thirty-eighth day, and a woman of sixty looks at the object column, then at the place name in it, then says one sentence of about nine words and does not ask what the word means, and a clerk of forty enters two lines and does not read them back, and she sends it down the lane to the man who makes the paper. **The four places want a number of people, and a number of people is the one thing this city has never put on a piece of paper, and a man of sixty-six said on the sixth day of this count that a figure of persons is the only kind of paper that cannot be refused and that this one has to be refusable or it is a lie with a stamp on it.** A man of about thirty-one said the second thing that can go in one of the four places, which is a sentence, and that an office that has a column for a sentence is a different kind of office, and nobody improved on it. **The only figure of persons this city can put on a piece of paper is one that is already written down, and there is one of those, and it is the list of the third shift with a man of fifty-two's name on it and the names of the two men before him, in a drawer in a room in this city, and about a few hundreds of people in this city could be asked what the third shift is and not one of them would be able to say; and it was said once, in a glass yard, on the twenty-eighth day, to a stranger, by a man of fifty-two, and nobody in the bindle yard said it out loud and the visitor worked it out standing at a mouth of a yard for eleven minutes and eleven feet from a man of fifty-five in a hut and has not written it down.** **And there is a second answer and nobody said it out loud: to put a figure of persons against that object somebody would have to put a name to the object, and one man in this city can put a name to a thing by putting his hand flat on it, and he was standing at the mouth of a yard with a stick, and the second answer was in that room for about an hour and nobody in the room knew it was in the room.** A man of thirty-two with a limp asked a man of sixty-one at a bench at the end of a lane past two gates, on the thirty-eighth day, in about eleven words, whether there is anything in this city that a number of people could be written against, and was told no after about four minutes of silence, with the reason that he had not been asked what for and had not asked, and that a man who is about to tell him is a man who has already decided.

609. **THE NINTH LINE IN THE BOOK, AND A REFUSAL OF NINE WORDS THAT IS THE ONLY ONE IN TWENTY YEARS THAT IS NOT ELEVEN, AND THREE FIGURES IN THREE PLACES THAT NOBODY ADDS.** On the thirty-ninth day a man of sixty-six makes a form in about four minutes at a bench under a roof, and **it is nine words and about four hundred of the eleven-word things are not eleven, and he said on the sixth day of this count that every one of them is eleven and not one of them is twelve, and he was wrong by a number and had been wrong by it for twenty years, and he found it out on the thirty-eighth day while he was not doing anything and is not going to lengthen a no to make it match a shelf.** The form says, *We do not count what we will not name.* **It is entered in a book under a board in a yard and it is the ninth line in that book, and the book has had eight lines in it since before the man who keeps it came into it, and the count in it went up for the first time in a count of days that anybody in this city is keeping, and the ninth line is about a thing this city said no to and it is not the ninth thing this city has said no to, and the man of sixty-six said so in about nineteen words in front of a man of about thirty-one and a stranger.** The three figures are: **eight in the book, eleven in the man of sixty-six's head, and nothing at all on the sheet**, and he said *The book says nine and my head says eleven and I have had both of those numbers since the twenty-ninth day and I have not added them and I am not going to, and a refusal count is a count of things this city has refused and not a count of people*, and that sentence is said in this block once and was said twice in Batch 0003 and is not said a third time. **The eight and the nine and the ten of Batch 0003 and the nine and the eleven of this block are never added to each other and never added to a figure of persons, and the sheet that went out on the thirty-ninth of this count went out with four empty places in it, which is the first time in a count of days that a sheet of that series has gone back out of this city with nothing in the four places, and about four hundred people in a city of about nine thousand people did not know that any of the three things had happened and are not going to.** The man of sixty-six's second thing of the day, said while ruling the second form, is the first of his that is about himself and it is his Chapter 218 want said once and not improved on: *I have been asked nine times in nineteen years and I have said no nine times and I have said it in the same words nine times, and I have wanted somebody to come back and ask me a different question for about eleven years and nobody ever has, and I am not complaining and I am not going to be.*

610. **THE POWER HE ALREADY HAS, DECLINED, AND THE NINTH REFUSAL, AND THE ROAD, AND THE THIRD REFUSAL IN A DOCUMENT IN THREE VOLUMES, AND THE ONE SYSTEM PANEL IN THE BLOCK.** On the fortieth day a man of thirty-two with a limp goes up a lane that goes up and not down for the fourth time in forty days and stands in a room with a long table in it and about two hundred and forty pieces of paper on it, and they are the second half of the fourth sheet of a printed series cut along the fold, in five cuts, on the same whalebone. **His left hand is warm at the fourth hour, the fourth hour is an hour this city keeps by a furnace, and he had been going to do a thing and did not do it, and it is the same thing he did on the twenty-seventh day of this count with a hand on a wall, and it is the same hand and the same warmth, and the panel's *it does not go further for anybody* is true of what follows it.** Nobody in the city saw him not do it and about four hundred people in a city of about nine thousand people did not know that he stood at the top of a lane for about a minute and a half with a warm hand and did not put it anywhere. **The decline is the volume's climax and it is a decision and not a fight: he does not name the object the form will not name, and therefore he never finds out what the word on the sheet means, and the second answer in item 608 stays in the room.** A man of sixty-six and a man of sixty-one stood in that room at about the fifth hour for the first time in nineteen years, with both books, and **a man of sixty-one has a fold in his page four inches from the bottom and a man of sixty-six has the same fold in the same place and neither has ever said so and neither compared a figure.** The man of sixty-one said, in about nineteen words, the mechanic's other half, in his own words and once: *A road is a line and two hands and a day and a witness at each end who is not the man keeping it, and I have read that in a book in a hall four hundred miles off and I have had four hundred years of a second column to look at and I have never once seen one of the eleven written in a hand, and I am not going to be the first and I am not going to let a man of thirty-two be one either, and that is the whole of it.* **And then he said the offer, standing up, in about nineteen words, and it is a fourth route and it is offered by a different party on terms with nothing in them: four days in seven, a bundle, no name, no figure, no hand, no wage, no clerk, and a witness at each end who is not you; and a man of sixty-six added that it goes in a book under a board, that it is not going anywhere, and that the man is not going to take it, and that there is no reason there should be a second kind.** The cost is the route. **It is refused in writing, in four sheets, in the same register as the refusal in Volume 04 and in a different sentence, and the difference is on the page and is that this time he was asked by two people in a room and not on a sheet in good paper, and a woman of sixty said that everything that is written comes round again and that both of his questions had been about paper.** Nothing about the offer is described and nothing about the refusal is staged, and the two documents are the third refusal in a document in three volumes and it is a document and not a scene. **The one System panel in the block is in Chapter 237, at the threshold of the two declines, in two plain lines, with no number in it, and it names neither the city, the dawn, the roadmark nor the light, and it restates none of the four panels before it, and it is not a list: *You have said no twice tonight and both of them were yours to say. There is no figure for what either of them cost and there is not going to be one.*

611. **THE RETURN, AND IT IS THROUGH A LIVING ANCHOR THAT IS A CHILD OF NINE, AND IT IS NOT A STITCH, AND THERE IS A WITNESS AND NO LINE.** On the fortieth day, at about the ninth hour, at the low end of nine hundred feet of paving, **a child of nine years old came down the lane, put its bundle down on the kerb, looked at a man of thirty-two with a limp for about as long as it takes to count nine, looked at his left hand, and then put its own left hand flat on the stone in the way anybody puts a hand flat on a thing to see whether it is warm, and the stone was cold on the other side of its hand too, and about a minute and a half later a man of thirty-two with a limp felt everything about a thing he has been building for four years stop being something he was holding.** It did not say anything, nobody said anything to it, it did not go out through a gate, and it went down the lane. **A man of about forty at a winch stopped winding for the length of that minute and a half and did not look round and has not been asked.** The man of thirty-two did not put his hand anywhere and does not know what the eleven feet was for and neither does the child. **On the other end, the eighth of Hearthmonth, YR 315, a Saturday, a market morning, at first light, four hundred miles off, a man of thirty-two with a limp was at the low end of a sill and could not get up the bank, and there is no line in the coping on either side of that sill and nothing on it, and a man of forty-seven said the four things and said them again and then said the third thing he has said on a bridge in a year: there was no line in this, he is the witness at this end, he has not been asked to be, he is not a road warden, and he wants the whole of that said in whatever anybody writes down, and there is going to be nothing in it.** That is the volume's fourth time and its no-line time, and **no second mark, no second line, no second witness, no preparation and no offer is made or recorded, and the crossing is in no minute and a clerk of about sixty entered nothing.**

612. **THE FEVER, AND WHOSE HANDS HELD THE TOOLS, AND NOBODY ASKED HIM ABOUT THE MORNING.** The fever is a week and it is Stage 3's and it was earned by the stage, and **a boy of fifteen held the ferrier's stick, the notebook and a coat with four sheets of printed paper in it for seven days, without being asked, and did not open the notebook and gave it back flat and in the right order with the first leaf turned to the first page, and the right order is a thing a person can only get right by not having opened it, and the word tools was used once, by a man of forty-seven, in the tone of a man saying a price, and has not been used again in that county.** A woman of about sixty put the coat on the top shelf on the second day because there is a boy of fifteen in that house and there are four sheets in that coat and she did not ask what was in them. **Nobody asked him about the morning, in any of the seven days, by anybody, and he did not offer it, and a woman of twenty-nine with a door on a lane forty feet from the room he was in did not come out of it once in the week, and a bench of nine has not been asked anything since the crossing out, and a clerk of about sixty entered no line about a fever, and a second copyist two hundred miles off did not open a letter.** The tax of holding three paths arrives in this block as a way of being unable to be given a thing without losing the thread: **on the thirty-first day he is handed a strip of paper and cannot remember nine minutes later whether it has four lines or five, and on the thirty-third the same, and on the thirty-ninth he loses the thread of four minutes of a man ruling a form and gets it back at the fourth minute, and on the fourth day of the fever he is given a cup and asks a woman of about sixty what it is for twice in about nine minutes and she answers it both times in the same words and does not say the same words the second time.** The leg is the same leg and is not worse, and nobody in that house has said that it is worse, and a boy of fifteen moved the stick twice in seven days and both times were on the side the leg is on.

613. **THE REASON HE WROTE DOWN AND THE FIGURE HE DID NOT, AND THE ARITHMETIC COUNTED HERE AND BY NOBODY'S CHARACTER.** On the seventeenth day of Hearthmonth, YR 315, at about the sixth hour, **he wrote one line in a notebook, in about four minutes, in his own hand, and it is the fourth page he has filled in in four years and it is not the page with no hour and no name in it, and it is about a frame and not about a figure, and there is no figure on it and there is not going to be one:** *a city that keeps one hour standing has a frame that does not run away from this one, and that is a claim about the length of the interval and not about the length of the warning, and the length of the interval is a conversion somebody made and I cannot check it, and the claim is either the whole of what happened to me or it is nothing and there is no way at all to tell from here which.* **The frame and the error are kept apart on the page: the line is a claim about the path interval, the path interval is a main-world conversion made by a person and not by the narrative, and no chapter in this block states the frame and the error in one sentence and no character is told any of it.** Counted here and printed nowhere, and footed before it is recorded: **a main-world absence of ninety days from the eighth of Embermonth, YR 314 to the eighth of Hearthmonth, YR 315 on the chain at `outline/volume-05.md` §17, day 13 to day 103; a printed warning of three weeks in an office's hand, two years old, unchanged; an error against that warning of sixty-nine days; and sixty-nine over ninety is about three quarters of the absence, which is the first narrowing in this case, against Volume 04's hundred and seventy-one over a hundred and ninety-two.** **The block printed no drift figure, no character is told any of it, and no character in this block uses the word *failed* about a road.** The printed warning is referred to as a warning in a file in a county two hundred miles off that has said three weeks every week since and has not changed, and he has not got a copy of it and has never had one.

614. **THE NAME BUDGET: NO NEW NAMES AND SIX SLOTS UNFILLED, AND THE BLOCK IS CARRIED ENTIRELY BY RETURNED FACES AND THE CHILD.** Dermit Crane, 66, Osmund Cusk, 61, Ivo Marrow, 52 and Nesh Karrow, 28 are spent names and all four have pages and **none of the four is re-described**; Marrow is on the page twice, in a working yard in Chapter 237, at the end of a bench with his hands behind his back and then at the foot of a ladder, and **both of those are a thing he does and neither of them is a second account of him.** **Volume 05 stands at five names of six and twenty-four of thirty unfilled across the five batches, against the volume's planned five and twenty-four, and this block spends none.** The whole of Block 0004 is carried by Crane, Cusk, Karrow, the child, and the man off the road. The child is the post, is nine years old, **is not named in any of the ten chapters and does not count**, and is the same child as Chapter 210, the nineteenth day and the twenty-ninth day. The man of thirty-four with lime, the woman of about thirty with a pail, the man of fifty with a waggon, the man of fifty-five in a hut, the man of about forty at a winch, the man of about thirty-one and the man of forty-six with satchels, the woman of about fifty who owns the room, the woman of sixty, the clerk of forty, the boy of fourteen, the man of thirty who sells names for a penny, the carter of thirty, the man of forty-seven, the boy of fifteen, the woman of about sixty in Weir Street and the man of about nineteen are addressed by trade or by age. **In the three main-world chapters the returned faces are Bram Ottery by name and the woman of about twenty with a pail and the boy of fifteen and the carter of thirty and the man of about nineteen, and Toban appears once, by name, in a yard, in Chapter 239, and the word brother is used once about him by the narrator in a room he is not in, on the same precedent as Chapter 228, and nothing in this block touches the estrangement.**

617. **THE TEN DEVIATIONS FROM THE TEN CARDS IN THE PROMPT AND FROM `outline/volume-05.md` §8 BLOCK 4, AND THE NINE OF THEM ARE THE PROMPT'S AND ONE IS THE OUTLINE'S.** **One, the outline's.** §8 Block 4 places this block on *days sixty-one to ninety of ninety*, and the page is on the thirty-first to the fortieth, because Block 0003 ended on the thirtieth and the chain on the page is continuous, and the prompt for this batch says days thirty-one to sixty and the recording instruction for `state/current.md` says the volume's remaining chain runs from the sixtieth day onward. **The page and the prompt win and the outline's sixty-one is not built on, and the reconciliation is not attempted here, and a Batch 0005 writer must not count from the sixtieth day as if sixty days of the city were on the page.** **Two, the prompt's, and the second largest.** The prompt's own frame is internally inconsistent: it says *days thirty-one to sixty of ninety* in one sentence and *Block 4 ends on the thirtieth day of the count* in the next, and the recording instruction says the volume's remaining chain runs from the sixtieth day onward, and `outline/volume-05.md` §8 says days sixty-one to ninety. **The block is on days thirty-one to the fortieth, one day a chapter as Batch 0003 was, because a chapter is a day on the page and the page is continuous from the thirtieth, and because ten chapters cannot honestly hold thirty days in a city where nothing is built and nothing is fought. this city were on the page.** Three, the prompt's: **the message system is built out of the same strip, the same rule and the same whalebone as the city's eleven-word forms, and the prompt lists those materials and does not say they are the same, and making them the same is the block's finding and it is on the page in Chapter 236 in nine words.** Four, the prompt's: **a mark comes back in a strip on the thirty-fifth day, and the prompt requires the block to show that two places can know each other is there without explaining it, and nothing in this block explains it and the four people who
