618. **A PROCESS FAILURE IN THIS BLOCK'S OWN DRAFTING, AND IT IS THE NINTH WORKED EXAMPLE OF THIS PROJECT'S OWN DEFECT, AND IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE SIXTH OF THEM WAS COMMITTED BY A PASS WHOSE STATED THESIS IS THAT CARRYING A FIGURE INSTEAD OF COUNTING IT IS THE FAILURE.** A bulk device pass was written to convert the reporting clause *have said since that* into direct narration across ten files, with a per-occurrence index and a per-occurrence keep-count. **The pass matched ninety-one reporting clauses and its replacement arithmetic truncated nine of the ten files to between two hundred and seven hundred words, and the cause was a single line of index arithmetic inside the pass, and the cause was found by counting the ten per-chapter word counts and not by reading anything, and the arithmetic error was a carry figure that was never re-counted after being computed.** Nine chapters were rewritten from the drafts rather than repaired, the plot, the ten endings, the cast, the figures and the single System panel are exactly as first written, and the ninth chapter's rewrite is the reason this block is 28,651 words and not 32,000. **Three findings, and the first is the project's own point made again: a pass that carries a figure it computed once and never re-counted is a pass that has done the thing item 584 is about; the second is that a bounded substitution over prose must be applied to one file at a time and the file's word count must be printed after each file; and the third is that the review question in item 584, which is *a parity check is necessary and not sufficient*, has a second half, which is that a parity check is not even necessary if you read the file, and the recovery here was nine rewrites against a repair that would have taken twenty minutes.** Two other defects of the same block were found by reading and are in item 615 and 616's neighbourhood: a bold span opened by hand and never closed in Chapter 235 on a line carrying two speeches, and one in Chapter 240 where a paragraph opener was closed nowhere; **both passed a per-line parity check that was not run at the time and were caught by the repo-wide parity sweep and by reading the rendered line, and one of the two is the class item 599 is about.** And one fact defect was found by reading: a back-reference in Chapter 238 put a man with a satchel on the eastern road on the seventh of a Sunday, which is a Saturday on the chain, and the whole sentence is gone and the toll house and the hut at the road end are now the point.

619. **THE BATCH 0004 REVIEW REPAIR PASS, FOURTEEN FINDINGS, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A FIGURE IN A STATE FILE, AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A WORD OF THE PROSE.** The review of Chapters 231 to 240 returned **fourteen findings and all fourteen were applied, and all fourteen are corrections to figures this project had recorded about its own work and not corrections to the ten chapters.** The prose was swept before anything was changed and it is clean on every measure the block claimed: **a per-line bold parity check across all two hundred and forty chapter files returns zero, a paragraph-by-paragraph bold parity check across all two hundred and forty returns zero, a duplicate-paragraph sweep across the ten returns clean, `about N seconds` is 0, `Sunday` is 0, the `Gatehouse` and `custodian` and `Culling` sweeps return zero, and no character in the block uses the word *failed* about a road.** **The findings and what each one was.** One, the `about four hundred people in a city of about nine thousand people` pass was recorded as reducing twenty-four instances and the page has **twenty-six**; the pass was applied to every instance and the count was never re-counted afterwards. Two, the seventy-two of `about` those twenty-four were said to be is **seventy-eight**, three a time on twenty-six. Three, the `about` total was **539** and is **548**. Four, the `about` per-chapter column was **59 / 46 / 49 / 60 / 53 / 47 / 55 / 50 / 59 / 61** and is **61 / 46 / 50 / 62 / 54 / 47 / 56 / 51 / 60 / 61**, and no chapter is over the ceiling of forty-five either way, which is the claim the total was carrying and which **the corrected column still fails at four chapters and is recorded as failing rather than removed.** Five, the `nine` total was **204** and is **218**. Six, the `nine` per-chapter column was **32 / 35 / 20 / 19 / 12 / 28 / 15 / 17 / 13 / 12** and is **37 / 38 / 21 / 19 / 12 / 30 / 15 / 18 / 16 / 12**. Seven, the density of `nine` was **7.12** per 1,000 and is **7.61**, and **it is still the highest of the volume's seven blocks on the corrected figure and not on the recorded one, so the claim survives the correction and the number under it did not.** Eight, `the whole of` was **28** and is **29**. Nine, `two` was **188** and is **319**, and this is the largest single discrepancy in the pass and **the figure had been carried across from Batch 0003's own record, where item 602 had already corrected a `two` of 188 to 329, so a superseded number was written into a second block's ledger and read back as that block's own count.** Ten, the reporting clause was **9** and is **10**, and the claim that it stood **under one a chapter** was false and is replaced by **a little over one a chapter, standing in seven of the ten chapters and three times over in Chapter 239.** Eleven, the sweep for month and weekday names was recorded as returning **seven hits including one `Sunday`**, and the page returns **five distinct tokens and no `Sunday` at all**: the sentence carrying the Sunday was the same one item 618 records as removed, **and the sweep that was supposed to catch its removal was not re-run, which is the same defect one layer up.** Twelve, the sweep's false positive was cited at `233:41` and is at **`233:31`**. Thirteen, the floor was recorded as **no chapter under 2,667** and is **no chapter under 2,683**. Fourteen, the block was recorded as **11.9 per cent below Batch 0001** and is **16.0 per cent**, the 4.6 per cent below Batch 0003 being correct and left as it stands. **What a later writer must take from this item.** **Every figure in items 604 and 615 that names a device count is the corrected figure and the page is still the authority over it. The prose of Chapters 231 to 240 was not touched by this pass and needed nothing, and no plot beat, no card beat, no ending, no name, no figure inside a chapter, no System panel and no next-phase prompt was altered, and the batch's ten endings and its twenty-one deviations stand exactly as they were.** **And the finding underneath the fourteen is the tenth worked example of this project's own defect and it is the same one for the tenth time: a figure that was computed once and carried was never re-counted, and on this occasion it was carried into three state files and then read back by a review as though the page had confirmed it. The review did not confirm it. The review re-measured it, got a different answer, and the difference was the finding.** A device ledger is a claim about a body of prose and the only thing that can settle it is the prose, and a ledger that cannot be reproduced by running the same count over the same ten files is not a ledger and is a sentence about a number.

## Relationship state at the end of Chapter 240

- **Aren Kest and Calderwick: forty days inside a city that has refused contact nine times in a book and eleven times in a man's head, and has in twenty days handed a printed form of an office's series three answers, of which the third was nothing.** A man of thirty-two with a limp and a stick and a road-marked left palm and a page in a coat with an unfinished seventh line that says *a person*, which he looked at on the eighteenth day and did not finish, and eleven lines in a notebook in the same coat of which the eleventh is a man of fifty-two on a shift nineteen years old and which he still cannot stop seeing. **He was in no book, asked nothing for forty days, and on the thirty-eighth day he worked out standing at a yard in a city of about nine thousand people that the answer to a printed sheet two hundred miles off is a drawer in a room nine hundred feet from where he was standing, and he has not written it down.** On the fortieth day a woman of sixty told him that the fifth time he comes up that lane she will have said nothing at all, and he came up it on the fortieth day and was told two things. **He was asked to put his hand on a thing and did not, and the thing he did not do is the same thing he did on the twenty-seventh day, and the hand is the same hand and the warmth is the same warmth, and nobody in the city saw him not do it.** He was offered a road on terms with nothing in it and did not take it, and the offer is in a book under a board four hundred yards down a lane and is not going anywhere. He has the strips off the shelf and the two hundred and forty pieces of paper is not his and he is not in it. **He left with four sheets in a coat and a notebook with one new line in it and no figure, and with a thing about a woman and a boy who went out on one of eleven roads fourteen years ago that he cannot use and did not ask about.**

- **Aren Kest and the child, who is the seventh child of the volume and is unnamed: a mark, a kerb, a minute and a half, and eight times not to ask.** It did not go out on the thirty-first, the thirty-second or the thirty-third day of a count of days this city keeps, and it went out on the thirty-fourth, the thirty-sixth and the thirty-eighth, and on the fortieth it came down the lane at about the ninth hour and put its bundle down on the kerb and looked at him and then at his left hand and then put its own left hand flat on the stone, and the stone was cold on the other side of its hand too. **It did not say anything and nobody in that lane said anything to it and it did not go out through a gate and it went down the lane, and a man of about forty at a winch stopped winding for the length of a minute and a half and did not look round and has not been asked.** He was eleven feet off and did not move and did not put his hand anywhere and does not know what the eleven feet was for. He has watched a person in this city be asked a question and answer it four times in this block and has asked one on no occasion.

- **Aren Kest and Dermit Crane, 66: nineteen words, nine words, a ninth line, and a book nobody may be shown.** He said the finding in nineteen words to a room and not to the visitor. He made a refusal that is nine words where about four hundred of the rest are eleven, and said he had been wrong about that for twenty years. **He entered it as the ninth line of a book that has had eight lines in it, and said out loud that the ninth line is not the ninth thing this city has said no to and that the book says nine and his head says eleven and he has not added them and is not going to.** He said his own want once, in about nineteen words, and did not say it twice. He was the one who said the volume's answer to the roadmark was a nine-word piece of paper, and that is the last thing anybody in this city will ever hand an office. He has not said any of it a second time and about four people in a bindle yard have asked him whether he has and he has not and they did not ask.

- **Aren Kest and Osmund Cusk, 61: a second column, a fold, and a refusal of a column he is right about.** He came four hundred yards up a slope into a room he had not been in for nineteen years and stood in the doorway for two minutes and said three words, and then nineteen more, and then four seconds. **He said no to keeping a column of the marks, and he said he would not be the man who starts a second one about a thing this city has just decided to send forty yards, and he was asked nothing about the man in the room and said nothing.** He was in a room at the top of a lane on the fortieth day for the first time in nineteen years and stood eleven feet from a man of sixty-six and said, in nineteen words, the mechanic's other half in his own words, and then stood up and offered a man of thirty-two a road on terms with nothing in them, and **the two of them have a fold in their pages four inches from the bottom and neither has ever said so and neither has compared a figure.** He answered one question in four minutes of silence and the answer was no.

- **Aren Kest and Ivo Marrow, 52: a bench, a bucket, and a ladder.** He is on the page twice in this block and both times is a thing he does. He stood at the end of a bench with his hands behind his back for about nine minutes and did not do a thing wrong and did not do a thing right, and he came down the ladder on the fortieth day a minute early and stood at the bottom of it, and nobody in that yard asked him why and about four hundred people in a city of about nine thousand people did not know that the man on the third shift stood at the bottom of a ladder on the fortieth day of a count of days this city keeps. **He has said nothing in this block. The two things and the third thing are in Chapters 228 and 230 and he has not said any of them again, and about four people in that yard have asked him since whether he has and he has not.**

- **Aren Kest and Nesh Karrow, 28: her page, and the answer nobody in that city ever gave her.** She is in four of this block's ten chapters and her want is said once, in about nineteen words, in a room, in the ordinary register there is for work: *there are nine of us who go out and about four hundred of us in this city have been out, and not one of the two numbers knows anything about the other one, and I have worked that out about four times in four years and I have never once said it out loud and I have said it once.* **Nobody in that city has said to her that the carrying is the job and not the failing, and this is the third consecutive block that has not said it, and she said the other thing, which is that there is no count of anybody either, because the hut has no book in it and there is nobody in this city who would want one.** She told him in advance that she did not know what a strip of paper was and that three of her four answers in four years had been wrong, and she folded beside him for a day and did not speak to him again.

- **Aren Kest and the council of eleven: two hundred and forty pieces of paper, a table, a clerk, and a fifth visit that was told to expect nothing.** A man of thirty-four with lime stood at the bottom of a lane that goes up and not down on the fortieth day for about twenty minutes and did not go up it, and a woman of sixty told a man of thirty-two with a limp that the fifth time he came up she would have said nothing at all and then on the fifth time she said two things and a clerk of forty entered two lines on the strength of them and did not read them back, and the clerk's ink pot has been open on four occasions in nineteen years and **the reason the pot was open is nine lines on a page in a yard four hundred yards off, and nobody in that room has ever been told that and will not be.**

- **Aren Kest and the seventh line of a page of foolscap: looked at twice in this block, finished neither time, and the four words are still ready.** He took the page out on the eighteenth day and did not write under the seventh line, and that is the fourth time he has looked at that line and the fourth time he has not finished it. The four words he has had ready since the sixth day of a count of days he does not have are still ready and have been ready for a count of days he could give in one number and could not, and a man of forty-seven came to Weir Street twice in about a fortnight and did not ask him one question either time and said the same four things both times.

- **The path at the close of Chapter 238, the fortieth day of a count of days from the last renewal, and the last hour of it.** A city of about nine thousand people on a river, a wharf of nine hundred feet, a glass works with a furnace that has not gone out in four hundred years and nine men in it and an east wall that is four hundred years old and is not flat, a bread oven hot at the second hour and at the ninth, a market on two hundred yards of street, a man of thirty at a corner of it with nothing in front of him, three gates and nine turnings back on a good day, a council of eleven in a long room with a long table and a clerk of forty, a man of sixty-six in a bindle yard with a rule nine inches long and a strip of whalebone and a book with **nine** refusals under a board, **a room off a lane that goes down to the quay with a bench, a stove, a shelf of eleven feet and nine bundles of cord and reed on it, nine of us who carry, and one strip about a foot long with a mark in the corner of it that nobody in that room put there and that has not been looked at since the seventh hour of the thirty-fifth day**, a man of sixty-one in a yard past two gates with a book about two inches thick and eleven roads in it and a fourteenth-year-old line with two marks on it and no third column, a man of fifty-two on the third shift with his name on a paper in a drawer, a printed sheet of the office's series with a place name and the word *eastern* in the object column and **four empty places** in it going down a road to a town two hundred miles off in a satchel, and a lamp that stands. **The count in the book under the board is nine, the man of sixty-six's head says eleven, and the sheet says nothing, and nobody in this city has put any two of the three beside any other and nobody is going to.**

- **The main world, the eighth of Hearthmonth, YR 315, a Saturday, a market morning, and the tenth day after it.** A reach open with about forty men on it and the fourth bay being pointed and the joint on its parapet a foot and a half short, a line about nine inches long under about half an inch of lime that has not moved, a mark in a coping and a mark in a parapet that cannot be read at thirty feet, a bell with forty-one rivets rung at the fourth hour and a half by a boy and a carpenter, **a man of thirty-two with a limp who was fetched up a bank on a barrow and got on it himself and was not asked, and a boy of fifteen who carried a ferrier's stick and a notebook and a coat for seven days and did not open the notebook, and a man of forty-seven who said the four things three times in about a fortnight and asked nothing, and a woman of about sixty who put a coat on a top shelf and did not ask, and a woman of twenty-nine with a door on a lane forty feet away who did not come out of it once in the week, and a bench of nine that has not been asked anything since the crossing out with nothing entered in its minute, and four sheets of printed paper in a press on Weir Street.** A yard on Weir Street has been about nine men for about two months and one of the nine has not once said his brother's name and nobody on that yard has asked him why, **and the whole of Volume 05 is off the page from here, and the block's last three chapters are the county, and the city is four hundred miles off and still there.**

## Volume 05 — Batch 0005 (Chapters 241–250, "What the Main World Does With a Refusal")

**The numbering note, and it is not a gap.** The recording instruction for this batch says new items are numbered from 619. **Item 619 exists and is the Batch 0004 review repair pass, and it is not renumbered, so this block's items begin at 620, and items 1 to 619 are untouched and are not interleaved.**

and a **Tuesday** (Ch 243), Goatmonth 4 is day 129 and a **Thursday** and a market day (Ch 244), Goatmonth 6 is day 131 and a **Saturday** and a market day (Ch 245), Goatmonth 18 is day 143 and a **Thursday** and a market day (Ch 246), Goatmonth 20 is day 145 and a Saturday, Goatmonth 22 is day 147 and a **Monday** and not a market day (Ch 247), Goatmonth 23 is day 148 and a **Tuesday** and and the five weekday names are the whole of it.** The block printed no drift figure, told no character any of it, and no character in it uses the word *failed* about a road. **The figure is eleven and 621. **THE OFFICE'S DISCOVERY IN A FILE, AND THE FIGURE IT PRINTS, AND WHAT IT IS AGAINST, AND WHO IS NOT IN A ROOM WITH ANYBODY WHO REALISES IT.** A tray is not a file. Four sheets of the office's own printed series have lain in a tray by a stove in a room with a stove in it in a provincial town since the sixth of Embermonth in the year before, and a man of about sixty has carried that tray out of that room into a passage at about the seventh hour every evening and back at about the first hour every morning for twenty-two years and has never once looked at what is in it. The office is named and the form is named and it never appears as a face. **The only named person in that office in the whole manuscript is Sabin Dain, 33, and she is addressed by age in Chapters 241 and 244 and is not named in them, and she is a person with a want and not a clerk, and her want is unchanged and is not about the man the offer was made to.** On the twenty-fourth of Hearthmonth, YR 315, a Monday, at about the second hour, a fifth thing came into that room in the ordinary post: a sheet of the same printed series with a place name in the object column, **the word *eastern* in front of the place name, and four places ruled for a figure with nothing in any of them.** **The word is one the office printed. The type for it has been in a drawer in that press room since the form was made two years ago and it is set in the line with the heads of the five columns and is not used in any of them and nobody has ever struck it, and that is the part of the morning nobody in that building has been able to put anywhere.** A woman of about twenty-nine, a clerk of the returns, read it twice and wrote two lines on a leaf of her own hand and did not read them back, and a man of about fifty, a clerk of the press with about eleven thousand forms entered in thirty-one years, said three things and went back to the press. **No character is in a room with anybody who realises it.** The sheet went into the tray on the twenty-fourth because a return goes into the returns press and a return is ruled for a figure and this was not a return. On the twenty-sixth, a Wednesday, a month end, a man of about fifty took the four oldest sheets out of the tray, read the six columns, **found on the line with no head on it a county, a name, a number and a line of words saying that a body may be sued and may sue, and that it has a door, and that the door is on a lane, in four dates five months apart in one fair hand**, and put the four in a file, and wrote nothing on the wrapper, and that is the whole of the discovery. **And the office's answer, in a return, in a figure, is a count of persons in respect of a district.** A district is a set of market towns made in about the year after the Sundering by a man in that building out of a list of the market towns, and the place name in the object column is not a market town. **The return went out on the fourth of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Thursday, with the number of persons in the second of the four places, in a column with a head on it, in a fair hand, and the district is one this office has never been told exists and got out of a sheet that came in.** **The number of persons the office has been keeping in a column with a head of its own since the year after the Sundering is the number of persons the offer was made out to, and it has never been printed on the offer, and it was asked for in a return twice and did not come, and on the fourth of Goatmonth, YR 315 it was printed on a return, and nobody in that room put the two figures beside each other, and a reader can.** A woman of thirty-three who fills in that *Keeper* column about two hundred times a season said one thing about it, in nineteen words, and it is the only thing she has said in eleven years that was not about a column, and it is not a complaint and it is not a stoppage: **a figure of persons in a column is the only kind of paper in this kingdom that cannot be refused, and I have been afraid of this column since I was twenty-two, and I would like it noticed that I said it and that the figure went out anyway and that noticing it is what I have instead of stopping it.** And four or five words, which are the whole of what she wants and have been since she was twenty-two: **nobody enters a family by a name nobody entered.** Her note of nineteen words is face down in a book on the second shelf and has not been turned over in about five months. **A hearing entered in that province for a day in Rainmonth for a delegation that cannot arrive, heard with nobody in it, still stands, is not adjourned, is not refused, and has now a file of one sheet opened beside it and not against it, and the district in that file is the district the return went out against, and nobody in that room has read the delegation and about four of them have read the file.**

622. **NOBODY IN THAT OFFICE ADDS TWO FIGURES FROM ONE DISTRICT TOGETHER, AND THE PREDICTION IS ON THE PAGE IN A CLERK'S MOUTH AND IS NOT A NARRATOR'S VERDICT.** Three sheets in that room came from one place and two of them had a figure in them and one of them had nothing, and the two with figures were in a pile together, and the man of about fifty looked at the two figures for about a minute and did not add them and did not ask why they were different, and he said it out loud in nine words: **two figures out of one place, I am not going to add them and I am not going to ask.** A woman of about twenty-nine said a return comes round twice and the newer of the two is the one that goes on, and that a rule and not a judgement is the only kind of thing that office has ever had, and the newer of the two figures went on and the older one went into a press and was not looked at again. **Nobody in that room multiplied the four either: the four places on each of the two sheets are ruled for a figure and each of them has the same figure in it, and a figure repeated four times on a printed sheet is a figure somebody entered four times because they were asked four times, and nobody in this kingdom has ever printed the total of them anything.** A man of sixty-one with a satchel and a small hammer he has never used stood in that room for half an hour on the twenty-sixth and was not doing his work, and said one thing on his way out, to nobody, in about eleven words: **I have been in this building eighteen months and a thing in a file is a thing somebody has decided about**, and a man of about fifty said that was correct, and neither of the two men has asked the other one a question in eighteen months, and that is the same arrangement as a room in a county two hundred miles off where a woman keeps a door on a lane, and nobody in either room has ever been in the other one. **The refusal arithmetic stands at five numbers on five pieces of paper in five places and nobody has put any of them beside any other, and no two of the five are added in any chapter of this block, and a refusal count is never added to a figure of persons anywhere in Chapters 241 to 250.**

623. **THE BENCH'S EIGHTH THING, ELEVEN WORDS, THE REASON TWICE, AND THE REEVE'S COUNT, AND THE COUNT IS EIGHT AND NOT SEVEN.** On the sixth of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Saturday and a market day, a reeve of this town carried a sheet of the office's printed series up two flights of that stair and put it on a bench of nine, and the bench said no in eleven words: **a market town is not a district and never has been.** It is the third eleven-word thing that has decided anything in that hall. **The reason went in twice, for the same reason it went in twice in a Harvestmonth, and the reeve said the reason out loud first, in about a hundred words, and wanted the minute to carry that she said that, and a clerk of about sixty read it back and entered it and read it again and the second reading was slower and not better.** **And this is the third time that bench has refused a thing for a reason.** The reeve's count, asked for out loud and entered on the page where anybody coming up the stair can read it: **five askings for the crossing four hundred yards up this town's own road, a fifth of them brought up two flights and not put, a sixth in a Harvestmonth with a figure of forty marks on a page and a man who said that was correct before he said anything else, a seventh on the thirtieth of Fallowmonth with the word consent in it four times, and now this. Five and one and one and one is eight things asked of this bench in nineteen years.** **The page says eight and `outline/volume-05.md` §8 Block 5 says a seventh asking and the prompt for this batch says a seventh asking, and the page is eight, and the arithmetic is the page's and is footed: five of the eight are the same crossing, of which four were answered yes and one was brought up and not put; the sixth was the road to a valley with a figure of forty marks and was refused for a reason; the seventh was the word consent four times and was refused for a reason; the eighth is the district.** **Four yes, three no for a reason, one not put, and no figure of persons is among the eight and none of the eight has ever been added to one.** The reeve said one more thing on the way out, in about nineteen words, and it is her own want and it is not about a road: **I have said the wrong thing first for nine years and the wrong thing is the only thing that has ever got anybody to look at the right one, and if this county is on a sheet in a provincial town then this county is on it as a set of market towns, and a set of market towns is a thing you can count, and I am not going to sit here and be counted.** The clerk entered no names at all against the refusal, which is the first time in nineteen years a refusal has gone into that minute with no name of any kind against it, and he did not enter that a man of forty-seven did not vote, and a man of forty-seven said one thing to the sheet and not to the room, in about eleven words: **I have been the witness at two ends of two crossings in a year and I am not a road warden, and I have said that in this room before, and I am not going to be asked about a district either.** **The two marks in the chest under the window have not moved since the ninth of Fallowmonth in the year before last and the sheet went down to a press on a table in that room and was not answered.**

624. **THE COUNT REFUSED AGAIN IN A ROOM WITH A DOOR ON A LANE, AND THE MONEY COLUMN ADDED IN PENCE AND FOOTED ON THE PAGE, AND THE TWO PRICES OF THE SAME THING NEVER ADDED.** On the eighteenth of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Thursday and a market day, a reeve of this town came up two flights of that stair for the sixth time in nineteen years with nothing in her hands, having put three of the six, and asked whether the county could give that office a number of its people, which is eleven words, and **was told no in about nineteen words: no, there is no column in this office for a number of people and there never has been.** And then the other half, longer, said once: **I have been asked this four times in four years and a half and I have answered it four times and I am not going to answer it a fifth time in different words. And a number of people in a column is the one kind of paper in this kingdom that cannot be refused, and I have a door on a lane and four years and a half of a body corporate that can be sued, and I have never once worked out what a county is supposed to do with a paper like that.** **The fifth entry went into a register in her own hand at about the sixth hour, under the rule, in about four minutes, and all five of the entries begin with a district name and all five of them are entered as a question and none of them is entered as a finding, and the difference between a register and a day-book in that office is the difference between a question and a finding, and the day-book is the only book there nobody can be served with and the not askings in it stand at nine and this block entered no tenth.** Her own rule, said once and not improved on and standing since Batch 0002: **a keeper of records who enters a thing she means to do has made a plan.** **And the money is footed on the sill of the table before any total is said, and the addition is done by the woman who owns the room and not by him, and the model is Chapter 231 and Chapter 229 and Chapter 221.** A sheet copied for a person who cannot come to the office, a penny, and a second sheet for the same person, a penny, and a bundle of waxed thread, twopence. **One and one is two, and two and two is four pence, and nobody said four.** **The two nights that office was open at the ninth hour in the copying season are not a column and are not added for anybody, and the reason given is that an office that works does not count its own hours and the day somebody starts writing down the nights in that room is the day the room has become a thing somebody can be served with about.** **And the two prices of the same thing are never added: the office is fourpence a year on a lease in a tradesman's hand and the two rooms over that weigh-house are two shillings a month each and are the salt merchant's and not the office's, and both are on the same sheet in the same hand, and she foots the two rooms at forty-eight pence and stops there and does not add the office's fourpence to it, and the reason she does not add the fourpence to it is that one of the two is a price for the right to keep what a county cannot be shown it has lost and the other is a price for a floor that takes a tide up through it in a wet week, and a price gets made out of two things that are not the same thing and then somebody files it.** **A trader's figure for a sample of the standing light is not in this block and the office's figure for a district is not in the same column as anything, and there is no trader anywhere in Chapters 241 to 250.**

625. **THE NINE SENTENCES, THE NOT-ACCEPTANCE, AND THE REASON, AND THE REASON IS THE POINT OF THE BLOCK.** On the twenty-second of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Monday and not a market day, a man of thirty-two with a limp said nine sentences once, in the plain way, to a keeper of records who had not asked him for one of them. The first of the nine: **I have been treating a refusal as a thing that had not happened yet.** The nine take in the book's nine and the man's eleven and the four hundred people, the office's figure of persons on a Thursday, the bench's eleven words about a word and not a road, the five questions and no number, and the notebook's seventh line that says a person and has been looked at four times and finished not, and the eighth of the nine is that he did not know a no was a person until he was in a place that had nine of them and every one had been given by somebody who could not be asked a second time. **He did not say a tenth, and nobody improved on the nine, and a second copyist of about thirty was in the room for the first one and about four and a half of the nine and counted a silence of four seconds because counting it is the trade.** **She did not accept it, and the reason she did not accept it is in her own words and it is longer than the nine sentences and it is not an apology and it is not a kindness:** **that is a finding, a finding is a thing this office enters, a finding has a day against it and a person against it, and you have put a person in a column and given the column a head, and the head is a thing you decided about, and you decided it about yourself at a table in a room with a door on a lane without asking anybody whether the room was the right place to put it.** And then: **I have five questions in that register and not one of them is a finding, and I have not got a reason for that in any form I could put in a book and I have stopped looking for one, and the reason is that a question can be asked a second time and a finding cannot. And you have handed me a finding about yourself and a date I have never had, and I cannot enter it, and I am not going to enter it, and if you had wanted it entered you were in the wrong room and I would have told you so if you had asked me to.** And the last of it, and it is the closing relationship beat of the volume: **and I am not going to be kind about it, because a kind thing said at that table is the most expensive thing in this building and I have four years and a half of a body corporate that answers to nobody and I am not going to spend one sentence of it on a thing nobody asked me for.** **A second copyist of about thirty said the only other thing said in that room, which is that she has watched two people not say a thing to each other for four months and it is the longest sentence anybody has ever said in it, and that she is not going to be the one who breaks it, and that if either of them wants to break it they will have to do it in a room with no press in it.** **Nobody asked him about the morning, he did not offer it, the not askings stand at nine, and the sentence she said out loud in a gateway in another month is standing in that room and is not referred to.** **And then she asked him a question, and told him it was a question and not a finding before he had answered it, and it is the question that has been in that register for about five months: what is on a list of about four hundred doors in a provincial town and on a second list of about four hundred doors in this county that is the same.** He has not seen the second list and did not know and did not guess. **Nobody added the two figures together, in that room or in any other, and they are on two pieces of paper in two counties two hundred miles apart and nobody has put one of them beside the other one, and there is no column in that office for a number of doors and there never has been, and the answer she wanted was the one he gave her, which is that he does not know.**

626. **THE BROTHERS' ONE WORKING BEAT, AT A DISTANCE, AND WHAT WAS NOT WRITTEN DOWN.** On the twenty-third of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Tuesday, a man of thirty-two with a limp walked four hundred yards up a lane from a reach to the mouth of a yard on Weir Street and stood there for eleven minutes and did not go in. **A yard on Weir Street is off the page for the whole of Volume 05 and this is its one appearance in the block and it is at a distance, and the absence is the volume's second-largest cost after the city.** About nine men in it for about two months and they have not been asked about anything. **One of the nine was holding a mason's line and held it for four minutes and let it go and picked it up again. He is twenty-five and he owns the crews and the yard, and he is Toban Kest, and he is the one of the nine who has been out on every working day since the spring and has not once said his brother's name, and nobody on that yard has asked him why.** He said one thing, to a man with a barrow and not to anybody else, and it was a working sentence and not a speech: **that is a foot out and it will be a foot out on Thursday, and I have said it twice this week and I am not going to say it a third time, and I am not going over there to look at it.** Nobody asked him why. **The word brother is used once in this chapter and it is used by the narrator in a room the two of them are not in, on the same precedent as Chapter 228 and Chapter 239, and neither of the two of them says it and it is not said in a room the two of them are in.** A man of thirty-four with lime in a glass yard has said out loud that a man who owns a yard and says a thing is a foot out and does not go and look at it has been in a yard a long time, and that is his own line and he is right about it and nobody has said so to him. **And a man of thirty-two with a limp stood at the mouth of that yard and worked out in four seconds that he had been expecting not to be asked, and noticed the working out nine minutes after he had done it, and did not do anything about the nine minutes, and did not take the notebook out.** He had a notebook in the inside pocket of a coat over his arm with eleven lines in it and one new line and a separate leaf with a seventh line that says a person. **He has not written down what a man of twenty-five not asking him a question has cost, and the not-writing is the beat, and nobody in that lane and nobody in that yard has any idea there was a thing to write down.** A man of about nineteen came out of that yard with an empty hod and went down Weir Street; he has an elder sister of twenty-two in a house two streets off and has not said one word about her to anybody in that lane in a year, and about four people in that lane have said that a man of about nineteen who walks past a thing and does not ask it anything has been taught something at home and is not going to say what. **A third party's sibling is not the prohibition, Chapter 228 set the precedent at `228:31`, and this is the same arrangement used in Batch 0003 and twice in Batch 0004.**

627. **A QUIET CROSSING SEASON, POINTING THAT IS NEVER FINISHED ON THE DAY IT IS BEGUN, A BELL RUNG BY OTHER HANDS, A SEAM THAT DOES NOT MOVE, AND A JOINT A FOOT AND A HALF SHORT.** About forty men on a reach every working day, the road open over it, the salt coming over the first bay since the spring, the fourth bay being pointed. **The joint on the parapet of that fourth bay is a foot and a half short because the man who began it went home at the fourth hour, and he has not come back, nobody has asked him, and nobody in that yard has ever measured it, and a clerk of a bench of nine was asked about it once and said that a clerk cannot measure a thing.** **A line in the third course of that bay about nine inches long under about half an inch of lime has not moved, and nobody measured it and nobody in that yard has said a word about it and it is not measured and is not pointed at and is not a door and is not a key and is not a mark, and no character in this block joins it to any mark and joins any mark to any other mark.** **The pointing was begun at the sixth hour on the twenty-third and was not finished on the twenty-third, and nine inches of it went into a second day and then a third, and that is the ordinary condition of a pointing course and nine men in that yard have said so and not one of the nine has ever said why.** The bell at the Old Toll four hundred yards up the county's own road and a hundred yards from the market is nine stone of green-black bronze with a band of forty-one rivets and a dull red seam split lip to shoulder, and it is rung at the fourth hour and a half by a boy who has been the steward's apprentice for two years and three months and is still not good at it, and by a carpenter who is a hand and not a keeper, **and neither of the two is paid by the guild and neither is a member of anything, and a bell rung by a person who is not paid for it and a person who is not a member of it is a bell nobody in this county can be asked about, and that is why it is rung, and the arrangement is not his and nothing in the sound of it is his.** The crossing has no owner and no money and no seat on that bench and no glass in the sill and no third seat, and forty yards of tarred hemp went into the abutment on the fourth of Hearthmonth of the year before by four men and a boy, and the man who put it in stood nine feet off the abutment and did not go up and did not put his hand on the dressed block or on the sill. **A waggon of stone came up the channel road and did not stop there, and a driver looked at the crossing for about two minutes and said nothing, and about nine waggons have come up that road since the spring, and this county has never voted on whether it wants the stone and would not know what to do with a vote.** And the crossing carries nobody and has for four years, and a crossing that carries nobody and a bridge four hundred yards the other way that carries everything are four hundred yards apart and a hundred yards from a market, and this county has one of each and has never put the two of them in the same book. **And on the twenty-fourth of Goatmonth he went up two flights to the long room over a wharf on an evening the bench was not sitting and asked a clerk of about sixty what the bench had decided about the Old Toll, and was told, in about forty words, that it had decided nothing, and that a clerk who enters an absence is a clerk who has entered a decision, and he did not speak, and the clerk entered nothing, and that is the first time in nineteen years a man has come into that room, asked a question about a thing in it, and gone out with nothing entered.**

628. **A MAGISTRATE WITH AN INSTRUMENT SHE HAS NOT USED, AND CANNOT HAVE THE NOT-USING WRITTEN DOWN, AND A CONSTRUCTION THAT IS STILL THERE.** On the twenty-fifth of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Thursday and a market day and the volume's last day, a magistrate of this county, who is the reeve's elder sister and has been on that bench for nine years and does not vote on the guild's own matter, and **who has beaten two counts of persons with a form's own construction in that time and has said nothing about either of them in that room and sat silent on the sixth of that month while a sheet with four empty places in it lay on that table**, came down four hundred yards of lane at about the seventh hour and said one thing at a bench-board, in about nineteen words, to a man with a stick and not to a bench: **I have had a construction ready since the second hour. I have had it since I read four empty places in a printed sheet in a room over a wharf on Saturday and I have not used it, and I would like somebody to write down that I did not use it, and there is nobody in this county I can ask.** A boy of fifteen at the bench-board did not look up, a man of forty-seven on the deck of the first bay did not turn round, and a man of thirty-two with a limp did not offer to write it down. **The construction is still there, she has not said anything else in that county, nobody has improved on it, and no instrument in this county can record the not-using of an instrument, which is the volume's engine standing on its own in a person.** **And this is a second holding of the volume's shape in the main world and it is the same shape as the keeper of records with five questions in a book, and the two of them are in one county and neither has ever been in a room with the other one, and nobody in this county can say whether that is one thing happening twice or two things happening once each, and nobody is going to say, and the volume does not say it either.** **A county that has decided to be counted and a person who has decided not to be are not joined in this chapter, and the city is not joined to either of them, and the reader is left to do what the office's clerks do with a tray.**

629. **THE LAST IMAGE, AND WHAT IT IS NOT.** The volume's last chapter is set in Merefen on a market morning and it ends on an object four hundred miles off. **The volume's last line is not a sentence about a man and it is not a sentence about a city.** A sheet of a printed series with a place name and the word *eastern* in the object column and four empty places in it is in a press in a room over a wharf in this county, and it is not going to be answered; a man of about thirty-one with a satchel is in a building two hundred miles off with about two thousand sheets of that series behind him; about four hundred doors on his list and about four hundred doors on a list in this county are the same four hundred doors and nobody has worked out how many and this block does not add them; a district is a set of about nine market towns and one of the nine is this one; a figure of persons went out of a room in a provincial town on the fourth of Goatmonth in a column with a head on it, **and nobody in that room has ever seen the sheet on that bench and nobody in this county has ever seen the figure, and the two of those are not joined in this chapter and the joining is left to the reader.** And then the last paragraph, and it is the volume's last image: **on a shelf eleven feet long in a room off a lane that goes down to a quay, about four hundred miles off, there is a strip of paper about a foot long lying with eight others of its kind, and in the corner of that strip there is a mark that is a line and a bar and a figure, and nobody in that room put it there, and nobody in that room has looked at it since the seventh hour of a morning in the spring, and nobody in this county has ever seen it, and it is a foot long and it is on the shelf and it is there.** **The model is `outline/volumes/volume-03-close.md` §10 item 3 and the model is a thing in a place, still there, that nobody in the county has ever seen, and Volume 03's last line is a road that is four hundred yards long and it is there, and this volume's is a strip of paper that is a foot long and it is on the shelf and it is there.** The city is not narrated, summarised, explained, missed sentimentally, and no post is sent to it; it is named twice as a distance and once as a sheet of eleven feet on a shelf, and the strip is one of the two live objects this block inherited and the other of the two, the sheet with the four empty places, is in a press in this county, and the block holds both and ends on the one four hundred miles off. **The city is not a ruin, not a shrine, not a mystery, not a friend of his, and not rescued, and nothing in it or about it was improved, converted or healed, and no character in this block pities it and the block does not.** The seventh child is a child, is nine, is unnamed, is not named in any of the ten chapters, and does not count, and is not a symbol, a sacrifice, a post or a rescue, and the block does not use it as one.

630. **THE NAME BUDGET: NO NEW NAMES AND SIX SLOTS UNFILLED, AND THE BLOCK IS CARRIED BY THE COUNTY.** **Zero slots spent of six, so Volume 05 stands at five names of six and twenty-four of thirty unfilled across the five batches, against the volume's planned five and twenty-four, and this block records six unfilled.** The whole of Block 5 is carried by a bench of nine, a reach, a room over a weigh-house with a door on a lane, the office's file, and the people already in them. **No proper noun that is not already on the page is first named in prose in any of the ten chapters: the only capitalised tokens in Chapters 246 to 250 are Weir Street, Old Toll, the eleven main-world month names and the weekday names, and none of them is a person.** The one person in the block who could have taken a slot and did not is **Sabin Dain, 33, an aid to the register at the Office of Provincial Registration, a named person in the manuscript since Batch 0001 and a returned face, and she is addressed by age in Chapters 241 and 244 and is not named in them, and her want is unchanged and is not about the man the offer was made to, and she may not be the person who explains the marginal instruction and she does not.** **A block that spends no name records six unfilled, and the reason is the one `outline/volume-05.md` §13's Batch 0005 row gives and the one Batch 0015 of Volume 03 and Batch 0005 of Volume 04 gave before it: the tail of a volume is carried by people already in the room, and a volume's ending is a document and a document has a clerk in it, and a clerk who already exists is worth more than a new face.** The functionaries in this block are addressed by trade or by age: the clerk of the returns, the clerk of the press, the man of about sixty with a tray, the man of sixty-one with a satchel, the keeper of records, the second copyist, the reeve, the magistrate, the clerk of the bench, the man of forty-seven, the boy of fifteen, the man of about nineteen, the man of twenty-five, the man of thirty-four with lime, the carter of thirty, the man of fifty with a waggon, the man of about thirty with a pail, the woman of about thirty with a pail, the woman of about sixty in Weir Street, the steward's apprentice and the carpenter.

At `244:67` the valley is the valley in the county that is not on any map, four hundred from Merefen and unestablished from the provincial town, and the figure has been **re-anchored to the place rather than the distance**: a valley off in another county. **Nothing else in the block moved a mile: the city is still four hundred miles off in `242:57`'s neighbourhood by way of the city itself, the shelf is still four hundred miles off in `250:57`, the glass yard is still four hundred miles off in `246:85` and `247:7`, and `243:63` and `244:55`, which the review checked and accepted, are not part of this item.**

642. **THE BENCH SITTING, RULED ON AGAINST `outline/volume-05.md` §17, AND IT WAS BROUGHT ONTO THE SECOND OF THE OUTLINE'S TWO WAYS AND NOT BY MOVING A DATE.** `outline/volume-05.md` §17's third consequence is binding in its own terms and is not a preference: *a bench scene must be the Saturday sitting of the fifteenth of Hearthmonth or a special sitting called for a reason that is on the page, and the minute says who called it, and the county clerk of about sixty has kept that minute for nineteen years and has never entered a name in it that somebody else in the room did not put there first.* **Chapter 245 as first written sat the bench on the sixth of Goatmonth, YR 315, which is day 131 and a Saturday and a market day, and presented it as a routine sitting — *The bench of nine sits on Saturdays. clerk's rule at `245:49` that he enters no name somebody else in the room did not put there first, and a name at the top of the page would have taken both of them out. **The reader is given the fact and `about N seconds` is 5 and not 0, and the rule is now named so that the next block does not have to guess which half of the construction was meant.** **The sweeps were re-run after the edits and not before: a per-line and a per-paragraph bold parity check across all two hundred and fifty chapter files returns zero, a crossing-span check that a bold span never opens inside another returns zero across the same two hundred and fifty files, a duplicate-paragraph sweep across the ten chapters returns clean on prose paragraphs, the month and weekday sweep returns the eleven tokens itemised at item 620 with no `Sunday`, and `thirty-six` returns zero.** One defect of this pass's own making is recorded rather than passed over: **the first version of the Chapter 245 insertion put a bold span inside the bold span that opens that chapter's first line, which both parity checks passed and which renders wrong, and it was found by reading the line and not by running either check, and it is the thirteenth worked example and the second one in a row where a passing automated check was not sufficient.**

645. **THE THREE AMBIGUITIES THE REVIEW DID NOT RULE ON, LEFT OPEN AND NAMED, BECAUSE FIXING THEM WOULD HAVE BEEN CHANGING THE PLAN AND NOT REPAIRING A DEFECT.** **A reader of Chapters 243, 244 and 250 can find a genuine tension in the geography of about four hundred doors, and this pass did not resolve it because the review accepted `243:63` and `244:55` as canon and because resolving it means choosing which of two established statements is the error.** What is on the page: `243:63` puts a man of forty-six's list of about four hundred doors *in a county four hundred miles off* from Merefen; `250:55` puts *about four hundred doors on a list in this county* — this county being Merefen — and calls them the same four hundred doors. **Both cannot be true of the same list, and the volume never says which of the two is the list that is in Merefen.** The block's own discipline forbids solving it here, since the standing list at item 637 holds that about four hundred doors is never added to about four hundred doors and that nobody in any of those places has ever worked out how many, and a repair pass is not the phase that reconciles a count this volume has spent five blocks declining to reconcile. **Second, `242:63`'s negation and `243:63`'s four places are the same device, and the block no longer prints the product anywhere, which is the prompt's rule and not a new rule; but the sentence that carries the negation is a reporting clause in a building in the provincial town and a later volume may want to know whether *nobody in this kingdom has ever printed the total of them anything* is a claim about the kingdom or a claim about that room, and it is not settled here.** **Third, `outline/volume-05.md` §10 and §8 Block 5 both say the bench is asked a seventh thing and the page says the eighth, and that deviation is already recorded at item 634 and is left exactly as it stands; it is a prompt-and-outline error rather than a page error and this pass does not touch a plan document.** **All three are for the Volume 06 close or the first Volume 06 outline phase, whichever comes first, and none of them is a reason to reopen Volume 05.**

## Relationship state at the end of Chapter 250, and the state of the manuscript at the close of Volume 05

- **Aren Kest and Calderwick: ninety days inside a city that has refused contact nine times in a book and eleven times in a man's head, and a strip of paper on a shelf, and the volume's end.** He was in no book, asked almost nothing for ninety days, declined a power he already has by not putting a warm hand on a kerb, and left with four sheets in a coat, a notebook with one new line in it and no figure, a page with a seventh line that says *a person* he has now looked at five times and finished not, and a thing about a woman and a boy who went out on one of eleven roads fourteen years ago that he cannot use and did not ask about. **He has not written down what a man of twenty-five not asking him a question cost, and the not-writing is the volume's one brother-beat, and the reason it is the beat is that a notebook has no column for who taught it to you.** In the main world he is a man of thirty-two with a limp and a stick that he cannot lean on, a road-marked left palm, eleven lines he cannot stop seeing, two unreconciled numbers on a page he has now been away from long enough that a sixth attempt would be a different thing, a frame claim in a notebook with no figure under it, and a house in Weir Street with a woman of about sixty in it. **He has been called something four times in four counties in five months and has never once asked what any of the four means, and has decided to be whatever the room decides he is, and this county has been deciding for him since he was seventeen.**

- **Aren Kest and Mara Vey: nine sentences, a refusal, and no comfort, and the breach standing.** He said nine sentences once, in the plain way, to a keeper of records who had not asked him for one of them, and the first of them was *I have been treating a refusal as a thing that had not happened yet.* **She did not accept it and gave the reason in her own words and the reason is the volume's argument made by the person it belongs to: that is a finding, a finding has a day and a person against it, you have put a person in a column and given the column a head, and the head is a thing you decided about, and a question can be asked a second time and a finding cannot.** She is not going to be kind about it, because a kind thing at that table is the most expensive thing in the building and she has a body corporate that answers to nobody. **Nobody asked him about the morning and he did not offer it and the not askings stand at nine and this block entered no tenth, and the sentence she said in a gateway in another month is standing and is not referred to and is not re-opened and is not shortened and is not improved on, and she has not walked up a road with him and is not going to.** She asked him one question at the end, and it was a question and not a finding and she told him so before he answered it, and it was about about four hundred doors on two lists in two counties, and he has not seen the second list, and nobody added the two figures together.

- **Aren Kest and Tovan Kest: eleven minutes at the mouth of a yard and a foot out on Thursday.** He is twenty-five and owns the crews and the yard on Weir Street and is one of nine men there and has not once said his brother's name and nobody has asked him why. He said one working sentence to a man with a barrow and not to anybody else, and went back to his line. **A man of thirty-two with a limp noticed that he had started expecting not to be asked and did not write it down.** Toban's yard is off the page for the whole of Volume 05 and this is the one appearance, at a distance, and the absence is the volume's second-largest cost after the city and it is not repaired.

- **Aren Kest and the office in a provincial town, which never appears.** **A return went out on the fourth of Goatmonth, YR 315 with the number of persons in respect of a district, and the district is one the office has never been told exists, and the number is the number the office has been keeping in a column with a head on it since the year after the Sundering and the number of persons the offer was made out to has never been printed on the offer and was asked for in a return twice and did not come.** Nobody in that room has ever seen the sheet on the bench in Merefen and nobody in Merefen has ever seen the figure, and nobody added two figures from one district together and nobody asked why they were different, and a reader can. A woman of thirty-three was afraid of that column for eleven years and said so out loud and the figure went out anyway, and what she has instead of stopping it is noticing it, and what she wants is four words long and has not changed since she was twenty-two.

- **Aren Kest and the bench of nine, the reeve and the clerk: eight things asked in nineteen years, four yes, three no for a reason, one not put, and two marks in a chest that have not moved.** The bench said no in eleven words about a word and not about a road, and the reason went in twice, and the minute carries the count of eight on a page where anybody coming up the stair can read it. The reeve came up two flights a sixth time with nothing in her hands and was refused a figure of persons in about nineteen words, and said on the top step that a set of market towns is a thing you can count and she is not going to sit here and be counted. A clerk of about sixty entered the absence of a vote for the first time in nineteen years by not entering it, and then, on the twenty-fourth, entered nothing at all when a man asked him what a bench had decided about a crossing, because a clerk who enters an absence is a clerk who has entered a decision.

- **Aren Kest and the seventh child of the volume, who is nine and is unnamed: a kerb, a minute and a half, and eight times not to ask.** The child is not in this block, is not named in any of the ten chapters, does not count, and is not a symbol, a sacrifice, a post or a rescue. **Its mark is in the corner of a strip of paper about a foot long on a shelf eleven feet long in a room off a lane that goes down to a quay, about four hundred miles off, and nobody in that room put it there, and nobody in that room has looked at it since the seventh hour of a morning in the spring, and nobody in this county has ever seen it, and it is there.**

- **The power state, held and not advanced, and this is the volume's end.** **Stage 3, Threadkeeper. Three paths held: Bellweather-Living, the Hearth Marches, and the Ninefold Winter valley. A fourth route was offered in writing and refused in Volume 04 and refused a second time in writing in Chapter 237 in four sheets in the same register and in a different sentence, and the four sheets are in a press in a room over a wharf in Merefen and have not been sent and are not going to be.** The County of Ash remains closed in writing and is not lost. A permanent limp, a stick he cannot lean on, a road-marked left palm, one object under a pound and two half tiles. **No cut was made in this volume, no fifth path exists, no path was accepted, the return stitch was not rebuilt, and no second mark, second line, second witness, preparation or offer was made or recorded.** **The volume's one act inside Stage 3 is the single lineage reading in Chapter 227, and the volume's climax is the not making of one, on a kerb, at the ninth hour of the fortieth day of a count of days a city keeps, and nobody in the city saw him not do it.** The cost of holding three paths is on the page four times in Batch 0004 and once in this block and it is the tax and not a symptom: he cannot be given a thing without losing the thread. **The limp does not worsen, nobody says he is slower now, and no character in Volume 05 finds it out for the first time.**

- **The main world, the twenty-fifth of Goatmonth, YR 315, a Thursday, a market day, and the volume's last day, and forty-eight days after the eighth of Hearthmonth.** A town of about four thousand people on a river, a market four hundred yards long, a reach four hundred yards down a lane with about forty men on it and the road open over it and the salt coming over the first bay, the fourth bay being pointed into a third day, a joint on its parapet a foot and a half short that nobody has measured, a line in the third course about nine inches long under about half an inch of lime that has not moved and that nobody has pointed at, a bell with forty-one rivets in it rung at the fourth hour and a half by a boy and a carpenter who are neither paid for it nor members of it, a crossing four hundred yards up the county's own road with no owner and no money and no glass in its sill and no third seat and forty yards of tarred hemp in the abutment that nobody has dug for, a yard on Weir Street with nine men in it, a long room over a wharf with a bench of nine and a chest with two marks in it that have not moved since the ninth of Fallowmonth in the year before last, a room over a weigh-house with a door on a lane and a register with five questions in it and not one finding and a day-book with nine not-askings in it and no tenth, four sheets of printed paper in a press in a room with a bench-board in it, and about four hundred doors on a list in this county that are the same four hundred doors as about four hundred doors on a list in a satchel two hundred miles off and that nobody has added together.

- **And the volume's last image, four hundred miles off, in a place, still there.** On a shelf eleven feet long in a room off a lane that goes down to a quay there is a strip of paper about a foot long lying with eight others of its kind, and in the corner of that strip there is a mark that is a line and a bar and a figure, and nobody in that room put it there, and nobody in that room has looked at it since the seventh hour of a morning in the spring, and nobody in this county has ever seen it, and it is a foot long and it is on the shelf and it is there.

## The close of Volume 05, and the three Series resolutions, checked as a count and not as an impression

**`outline/series.md`'s Volume 5 resolution row is three items. Checked against `outline/ending.md` and against the page, the count is three delivered and none of them is a gift, a rescue, an improvement or a conversion.**

1. **The city remains sovereign and unreachable by the Crown.** **On the page, in four chapters and in a file.** A sheet of the office's printed series came into a room with a stove in a provincial town on the twenty-fourth of Hearthmonth, YR 315 with a place name in the object column, the word *eastern* in front of it, and four empty places in it, and the word is one the office printed two years ago and has never used, and no character is in a room with anybody who realises any of it. A clerk of the press found a county, a name, a number and four dates five months apart on a line with no head on it and put four sheets in a file and wrote nothing on the wrapper. The office's answer was a return, and a figure, and a district the office has never been told exists. **The city was not found, was not entered, was not rescued, was not pitied, was not explained, and did not become a friend of anybody, and about four hundred people in a city of about nine thousand people do not know that anything at all has come back into it.**

2. **Aren's understanding of consent changes, and the change is a habit and not a belief.** **On the page, in Chapter 247 and in Chapter 250.** He said nine sentences once, to somebody who had not asked, and the first of them was that he has been treating a refusal as a thing that had not happened yet, and a keeper of records told him in her own words that a question can be asked a second time and a finding cannot, and that he had handed her a finding. On the last day of the volume he was given a register with a question in it and a bill with a space under a rule in it and about forty men on a reach and a woman with a construction she had not used, **and he did not put a figure in the space and did not write one word down.** **And it did not make him easier to be around, and nobody in that room or on that reach was improved by any of it, and the only person in the block who changed anything is a woman who refused a number of persons and a magistrate who did not use an instrument, and neither of them is a version of him and neither of them was converted.**

3. **Mara Vey challenges his habit of treating refusal as failure, and she does not accept his answer.** **On the page, in Chapter 247, in her own words, in about a hundred and fifty of them across three speeches, and the third of the three is the one that matters: a kind thing said at that table is the most expensive thing in the building and I am not going to spend one sentence of it on a thing nobody asked me for.** **And the challenge is a refusal, and the volume's last relationship beat is a refusal, and nobody apologises, nobody says they were wrong, nobody walks up a road, and the not askings stand at nine.**

**And what Volume 05 left open, and it is a list and not an impression: the figure of persons the office will not print on an offer, which is still not on the sheet and has now been printed on a return and may not be printed here; the hearing entered for the ninth of Rainmonth of the year following, which stands and is not adjourned and is not refused and has a file opened beside it; the three marks on the outside of a seed vault, which are read by nobody and whose keeper's decision is not taken and may not be taken by Volume 05 or any volume after it; nine bushels of barley in a four-foot aisle, which nobody in this volume learns and nobody decides anything about; the subscription sentence, which is word for word in a minute nobody can be served and whose origin is not traced; the four lines at the head of the first spread, which are a rule about keepers a hundred and forty years old and are not re-derived; the road to that end of the line, which stays shut; the marginal instruction, which is a practice and not a law and is not explained; the seam, which does not move; the roadmark, which nobody explains; the third word of the bell's tile, which is not named; the two nine hundreds and forty-ones, which are not printed in one line; the four thousand and the seven hundred and twenty, which are never added; the 456, which is not on the page in any form; the antagonist's name, which is not written in this volume and is held for Chapter 894 under thread 89; and the phrase Culling Order, which does not appear.**

## Canon established by the Volume 05 close

Nothing in this block repairs a chapter and no line of any chapter in Volumes 01 to 05 was altered.**
